at sagsøge.explanation: "At sagsøge" means "to sue". It is built from "en sag" (a case) and "at søge" (to seek). To name the person who sues, say "en sagsøger" (a plaintiff).

sentence.da: Hun vil **sagsøge** firmaet, fordi det ikke betalte hende.
sentence.en: She wants to sue the firm because it did not pay her.

at samarbejde.explanation: "At samarbejde" means "to cooperate". It is built from "sam" (together) and "at arbejde" (to work). To name the person you cooperate with, add "med" (with) before that person: "Jeg samarbejder med naboen" (I cooperate with the neighbor).

sentence.da: Vi skal **samarbejde** for at løse opgaven.
sentence.en: We have to work together to solve the task.

at samle.explanation: "At samle" means "to gather or collect". To bring people together, say: "Læreren samler børnene" (The teacher gathers the children). To say what you collect as a hobby, add "på" (on): "Min farmor samler på kopper" (My grandmother collects cups). To say you put parts together, say: "Jeg samler en reol" (I am putting together a bookcase).

sentence.da: Min bror vil **samle** på gamle mønter.
sentence.en: My brother wants to collect old coins.

at samle på.explanation: "At samle på" means "to collect", as in a hobby. To say what you collect, put it after "på" (on): "Min onkel samler på gamle ure" (My uncle collects old watches). Without "på", "at samle" means "to gather": "Hun samler blomster" (She gathers flowers).

sentence.da: Min søn vil **samle på** frimærker.
sentence.en: My son wants to collect stamps.

at sammenfatte.explanation: "At sammenfatte" means "to summarize". It is built from "sammen" (together) and "at fatte" (to grasp). To say how you summarize a text, say: "Hun sammenfatter rapporten på en side" (She summarizes the report on one page).

sentence.da: Kan du **sammenfatte** mødet i tre linjer?
sentence.en: Can you summarize the meeting in three lines?

at sammenkalde.explanation: "At sammenkalde" means "to convene". It is built from "sammen" (together) and "at kalde" (to call). To say you call people together, say: "Hun sammenkalder familien" (She calls the family together).

sentence.da: Formanden vil **sammenkalde** bestyrelsen til et møde i morgen.
sentence.en: The chairman will convene the board for a meeting tomorrow.

at sammenligne.explanation: "At sammenligne" means "to compare". To say what you compare something with, add "med" (with): "Jeg sammenligner prisen med prisen i går" (I compare the price with yesterday's price). It is built from "sammen" (together) and "at ligne" (to resemble).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sammenligne** priserne i to butikker.
sentence.en: I want to compare the prices in two stores.

at sammensætte.explanation: "At sammensætte" means "to put together". It is built from "sammen" (together) and "at sætte" (to put). To say you put together a menu, say: "Jeg sammensætter en ny menu" (I am putting together a new menu). A word made of two words is "et sammensat ord" (a compound word).

sentence.da: Træneren skal **sammensætte** et hold til næste kamp.
sentence.en: The coach has to put together a team for the next match.

at sanse.explanation: "At sanse" means "to sense". It comes from "en sans" (a sense). To say you notice someone's mood without being told, say: "Hun sanser, at han er nervøs" (She senses that he is nervous).

sentence.da: Hun kan **sanse**, når nogen er ked af det.
sentence.en: She can sense when someone is sad.

at satse.explanation: "At satse" means "to bet or go for". To say you put your effort on one choice, add "på" (on): "Hun satser på en karriere som musiker" (She is going for a career as a musician). To say you put money on something, use the same verb: "Han satsede hundrede kroner på hesten" (He bet a hundred kroner on the horse).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **satse** på en uddannelse i stedet for et job.
sentence.en: I want to go for an education instead of a job.

at savne.explanation: "At savne" means "to miss". To say you miss a person, say: "Jeg savner dig" (I miss you). To say you missed a bus, do not use it. Say: "Jeg nåede ikke bussen" (I did not catch the bus).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **savne** min familie meget.
sentence.en: I will miss my family a lot.

at scanne.explanation: "At scanne" means "to scan". To copy a paper into a computer, say: "Jeg scanner kvitteringen" (I scan the receipt). To read a barcode with your phone, say: "Scan stregkoden med din telefon" (Scan the barcode with your phone).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **scanne** brevet og sende det.
sentence.en: I want to scan the letter and send it.

at score.explanation: "At score" means "to score". It is borrowed from English. To say a player scored two times, say: "Hun scorede to gange" (She scored twice).

sentence.da: Han vil **score** et mål i kampen.
sentence.en: He wants to score a goal in the match.

at scrolle.explanation: "At scrolle" means "to scroll". To say which way you scroll, add "ned" (down) or "op" (up): "Jeg scroller ned" (I scroll down), "Jeg scroller op" (I scroll up).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **scrolle** i timevis på min telefon.
sentence.en: I can scroll for hours on my phone.

at se.explanation: "At se" means "to see". When you watch a movie, it also means "to watch": "Jeg ser en film" (I am watching a movie). To say you understand, say: "Jeg kan se, hvad du mener" (I can see what you mean). To say goodbye, say: "Vi ses!" (See you!). To look on purpose, use "at kigge" (to look): "Kig her!" (Look here!).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **se** dit hus fra her.
sentence.en: I can see your house from here.

at se bort fra.explanation: "At se bort fra" means "to disregard". It is built from "at se" (to see), "bort" (away) and "fra" (from). To say you leave something out of your judgment, say: "Hvis vi ser bort fra prisen, er det en god bil" (If we disregard the price, it is a good car).

sentence.da: Du kan ikke bare **se bort fra** reglerne.
sentence.en: You cannot just disregard the rules.

at se efter.explanation: "At se efter" means "to look for or check". To say you are looking out for the bus, say: "Jeg ser efter bussen" (I am looking out for the bus). To ask someone to check that a door is locked, say: "Se efter, om døren er låst" (Check whether the door is locked).

sentence.da: Kan du **se efter** mine nøgler?
sentence.en: Can you look for my keys?

at se frem til.explanation: "At se frem til" means "to look forward to". It is built from "at se" (to see), "frem" (forward) and "til" (to). To say what you look forward to doing, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Jeg ser frem til at høre fra dig" (I look forward to hearing from you).

sentence.da: Børnene kan **se frem til** en lang sommerferie.
sentence.en: The children can look forward to a long summer break.

at se ned på.explanation: "At se ned på" means "to look down on". To say you look down from a high place, say: "Jeg ser ned på gaden" (I look down at the street). The opposite is "at se op til" (to look up to): "Jeg ser op til min storesøster" (I look up to my big sister).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **se ned på** folk, bare fordi de er fattige.
sentence.en: You must not look down on people just because they are poor.

at se op til.explanation: "At se op til" means "to look up to". It is built from "at se" (to see), "op" (up) and "til" (to). To say you admire your mother, say: "Jeg ser op til min mor" (I look up to my mother).

sentence.da: Børn har ofte brug for nogen at **se op til**.
sentence.en: Children often need someone to look up to.

at se på.explanation: "At se på" means "to look at". To say you look at the sky, say: "Han ser på himlen" (He looks at the sky). To say you search for something, use "at lede efter" (to look for): "Jeg leder efter min nøgle" (I am looking for my key).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **se på** billedet.
sentence.en: I want to look at the picture.

at se tilbage.explanation: "At se tilbage" means "to look back". It is built from "at se" (to see) and "tilbage" (back). To say you turn your eyes behind you, say: "Hun så tilbage over skulderen" (She looked back over her shoulder).

sentence.da: Hun vil **se tilbage** på sin barndom.
sentence.en: She wants to look back on her childhood.

at se tv.explanation: "At se tv" means "to watch TV". Danish uses "se" (to see) where English says "watch". To say you watch a movie, say: "Jeg ser en film" (I am watching a movie). The letters "tv" are said "te-ve".

sentence.da: Vi vil **se tv** i aften.
sentence.en: We want to watch TV tonight.

at se ud.explanation: "At se ud" means "to look", as in how something appears. To say how a person seems, say: "Du ser træt ud" (You look tired). To ask what something looks like, say: "Hvordan ser det ud?" (What does it look like?) To look at something with your eyes, use "at se på" (to look at): "Jeg ser på billedet" (I look at the picture).

sentence.da: Min bror skal **se ud** som en pirat til festen.
sentence.en: My brother has to look like a pirate at the party.

at sejle.explanation: "At sejle" means "to sail". To say you travel on water by boat, even with an engine, use the same verb: "Vi sejler til Sverige" (We are going to Sweden by boat). Rowing is "at ro" (to row): "Vi ror over søen" (We row across the lake).

sentence.da: Om sommeren vil vi **sejle** til en lille ø.
sentence.en: In the summer, we want to sail to a small island.

at sende.explanation: "At sende" means "to send". To name the person right after the verb, say: "Jeg sender dig en besked" (I send you a message). To name the person after the item, add "til" (to): "Jeg sender en besked til dig" (I send a message to you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sende** et brev til mor.
sentence.en: I want to send a letter to Mom.

at sende en sms.explanation: "At sende en sms" means "to text". It is literally "to send an SMS". To name the person you text, put "dig" (you) right after the verb: "Jeg sender dig en sms" (I send you a text).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sende en sms** til min ven.
sentence.en: I want to send a text to my friend.

at servere.explanation: "At servere" means "to serve", as in giving food or drink. To say you give guests something to eat and drink, say: "Vi serverer kaffe og kage" (We serve coffee and cake).

sentence.da: Tjeneren vil **servere** maden nu.
sentence.en: The waiter will serve the food now.

at shoppe.explanation: "At shoppe" means "to shop". It is borrowed from English. To say you buy groceries, use "at købe ind" (to buy groceries) instead: "Jeg køber ind til aftensmad" (I am buying groceries for dinner).

sentence.da: Vi skal **shoppe** i byen i weekenden.
sentence.en: We are going shopping in town this weekend.

at sidde.explanation: "At sidde" means "to sit". To say where you sit, use "ved" (at): "Jeg sidder ved computeren" (I am sitting at the computer). To say you sit down, use "at sætte sig" (literally, to put oneself): "Jeg sætter mig" (I sit down).

sentence.da: Du kan **sidde** på stolen.
sentence.en: You can sit on the chair.

at sidde fast.explanation: "At sidde fast" means "to be stuck". To say a key will not come out of a lock, say: "Nøglen sidder fast i låsen" (The key is stuck in the lock). To say you cannot go on with a task, say: "Jeg sidder fast med opgaven" (I am stuck on the task).

sentence.da: Lastbilen kan **sidde fast** i mudderet.
sentence.en: The truck can end up stuck in the mud.

at sige.explanation: "At sige" means "to say". To ask what someone is saying, say: "Hvad siger du?" (What are you saying?) To tell a story, use "at fortælle" (to tell) instead: "Hun fortæller en historie" (She tells a story).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **sige** tak.
sentence.en: The children must say thank you.

at sige farvel.explanation: "At sige farvel" means "to say goodbye". To say goodbye in a casual way, say: "Hej hej, vi ses!" (Bye bye, see you!)

sentence.da: Vi skal **sige farvel** til vores gæster.
sentence.en: We have to say goodbye to our guests.

at sige goddag.explanation: "At sige goddag" means "to say hello". It is literally "to say good day". To tell someone to say hi in a short way, use "hej" (hi): "Sig hej til din mor" (Say hi to your mother).

sentence.da: Du skal **sige goddag** til min mor.
sentence.en: You must say hello to my mother.

at sige op.explanation: "At sige op" means "to resign or quit". To say you leave your job, say: "Han sagde op i går" (He quit yesterday). To say you cancel a subscription, say: "Jeg sagde mit abonnement op" (I canceled my subscription).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sige op** og finde et nyt job.
sentence.en: I want to quit and find a new job.

at sige til.explanation: "At sige til" means "to tell or let know". To ask someone to let you know, say: "Sig til, hvis du har brug for hjælp" (Tell me if you need help). Without "til" (to), "at sige" means "to say": "Hun sagde hej" (She said hi).

sentence.da: Du skal **sige til**, når du er sulten.
sentence.en: You have to let me know when you are hungry.

at sige undskyld.explanation: "At sige undskyld" means "to say sorry". To get a stranger's attention, say "undskyld" by itself: "Undskyld, ved du, hvor stationen er?" (Excuse me, do you know where the station is?)

sentence.da: Du skal **sige undskyld** til din bror.
sentence.en: You have to say sorry to your brother.

at signere.explanation: "At signere" means "to sign". To sign a form or a contract, use "at skrive under" (to sign a paper): "Du skal skrive under her" (You have to sign here). To say a player joins a club by contract, use "at signere": "Spilleren har signeret med klubben" (The player has signed with the club).

sentence.da: Forfatteren vil **signere** bøger i boghandlen på lørdag.
sentence.en: The author will sign books in the bookstore on Saturday.

at sigte.explanation: "At sigte" means "to aim or charge". To say you point at what you want to hit, add "på" (at): "Han sigter på dåsen" (He aims at the can). To say the police officially suspect someone of a crime, say: "Han er sigtet for tyveri" (He is charged with theft).

sentence.da: Skytten skal **sigte**, før hun trykker på aftrækkeren.
sentence.en: The shooter has to aim before she pulls the trigger.

at sikre.explanation: "At sikre" means "to secure or ensure". To say you fasten something so it stays safe, say: "Jeg sikrer cyklen med en lås" (I secure the bike with a lock). To say you make sure something happens, say: "Vi sikrer, at alle får mad" (We make sure everyone gets food). Do not mix it up with "at forsikre" (to insure): "Jeg forsikrer bilen" (I insure the car).

sentence.da: Du skal **sikre** lasten med stropper, så den ikke falder af.
sentence.en: You must secure the load with straps so that it does not fall off.

at simulere.explanation: "At simulere" means "to simulate". When you mean to pretend something that is not true, it means "to fake": "Han simulerer sygdom" (He is faking an illness).

sentence.da: Piloterne kan **simulere** en nødlanding i en flysimulator.
sentence.en: The pilots can simulate an emergency landing in a flight simulator.

at sjuske.explanation: "At sjuske" means "to be sloppy". To name the task you are sloppy with, add "med" (with) before the task: "sjuske med lektierne" (to be sloppy with the homework).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **sjuske**, når du skriver en vigtig mail.
sentence.en: You must not be sloppy when you write an important email.

at skabe.explanation: "At skabe" means "to create". To say new jobs come into being, say: "skabe nye job" (to create new jobs). To say you make food, use "at lave" (to make) instead: "lave mad" (make food).

sentence.da: Vi vil **skabe** en ny hjemmeside sammen.
sentence.en: We want to create a new website together.

at skabe sig.explanation: "At skabe sig" means "to make a fuss". It is built from "at skabe" (to create) and "sig" (oneself), but it has nothing to do with creating. To say a child is making a fuss, say: "Barnet skaber sig i butikken" (The child is making a fuss in the shop).

sentence.da: Han kan **skabe sig**, når han ikke får sin vilje.
sentence.en: He can make a fuss when he does not get his way.

at skade.explanation: "At skade" means "to harm or damage". To say something does no harm, say: "Det skader ikke" (It does no harm). To say you hurt yourself, add "sig" (oneself): "Jeg skadede mig" (I hurt myself).

sentence.da: For meget sukker kan **skade** dine tænder.
sentence.en: Too much sugar can harm your teeth.

at skaffe.explanation: "At skaffe" means "to get or obtain". To ask someone to arrange something for people, say: "Kan du skaffe mad til alle?" (Can you get food for everyone?) To say you just receive something, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg fik en gave" (I got a gift).

sentence.da: Vi kan **skaffe** billetter til dig.
sentence.en: We can get tickets for you.

at skamme sig.explanation: "At skamme sig" means "to be ashamed". It is built on "skam" (shame) and "sig" (oneself). To tell someone to be ashamed, say: "Skam dig!" (Shame on you!)

sentence.da: Man skal ikke **skamme sig** over at bede om hjælp.
sentence.en: You should not be ashamed of asking for help.

at skele.explanation: "At skele" means "to be cross-eyed or glance". To say you glance at something, add "til" (at): "Han skeler til naboens bil" (He glances at the neighbor's car).

sentence.da: Drengen skal have briller, fordi han kan **skele**.
sentence.en: The boy needs glasses because he can be cross-eyed.

at skelne.explanation: "At skelne" means "to distinguish". To say you cannot tell two things apart, use "mellem" (between): "Jeg kan ikke skelne mellem tvillingerne" (I cannot tell the twins apart). To take things apart, use "at adskille" (to separate): "Han adskiller papir og plast" (He separates paper and plastic).

sentence.da: Farveblinde kan have svært ved at **skelne** rød fra grøn.
sentence.en: Colorblind people can have trouble telling red from green.

at skifte.explanation: "At skifte" means "to change or switch". To say you swap one thing for another, say: "Jeg skifter dæk" (I change tires). To make something become different, use "at ændre" (to change): "Jeg ændrer planen" (I am changing the plan).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skifte** tøj, når vi kommer hjem.
sentence.en: I want to change clothes when we get home.

at skifte mening.explanation: "At skifte mening" means "to change one's mind". To say someone decided differently, say: "Hun skiftede mening og blev hjemme" (She changed her mind and stayed home). To say you change a shirt, use plain "skifte" (change) without "mening": "skifte skjorte" (change a shirt).

sentence.da: Du kan **skifte mening**, når du vil.
sentence.en: You can change your mind whenever you want.

at skifte tøj.explanation: "At skifte tøj" means "to change clothes". To say you change jobs, use the same verb "at skifte" (to change): "skifte job" (to change jobs).

sentence.da: Jeg er våd og vil **skifte tøj**.
sentence.en: I am wet and want to change clothes.

at skifte ud.explanation: "At skifte ud" means "to replace". The small word "ud" (out) shows the old thing is taken out. To say you replace a light bulb, say: "Jeg skifter pæren ud" (I replace the light bulb).

sentence.da: Træneren vil **skifte ud** midt i kampen.
sentence.en: The coach wants to substitute in the middle of the game.

at skildre.explanation: "At skildre" means "to depict". To say a writer shows a place or a person in a book, say: "Forfatteren skildrer en lille by" (The author depicts a small town).

sentence.da: Maleren vil **skildre** havnen i et stort maleri.
sentence.en: The painter wants to depict the harbor in a large painting.

at skille.explanation: "At skille" means "to separate". To say a couple divorces, use "skilt" (separated): "De blev skilt" (They got divorced). To say you pull two people apart, add "ad" (apart): "Læreren skilte de to drenge ad" (The teacher separated the two boys).

sentence.da: Du skal **skille** æggeblommen fra hviden.
sentence.en: You have to separate the yolk from the white.

at skilles.explanation: "At skilles" means "to divorce or separate". To say two people go different ways, say: "Vi skilles ved stationen" (We part at the station).

sentence.da: Mine forældre vil **skilles**, men de er venner.
sentence.en: My parents want to get divorced, but they are friends.

at skinne.explanation: "At skinne" means "to shine". To say a person glows with happiness, say: "Hun skinner af glæde" (She glows with joy).

sentence.da: Solen vil **skinne** hele weekenden.
sentence.en: The sun will shine all weekend.

at skjule.explanation: "At skjule" means "to hide". To say you hide a feeling, say: "Hun skjuler sin vrede" (She is hiding her anger).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skjule** pakken under sengen.
sentence.en: I will hide the package under the bed.

at skrabe.explanation: "At skrabe" means "to scrape". To say you remove paint from a wall, say: "Han skrabede malingen af væggen" (He scraped the paint off the wall). To say you peel carrots, say: "at skrabe gulerødder" (to peel carrots).

sentence.da: Jeg må **skrabe** isen af forruden, før jeg kan køre.
sentence.en: I have to scrape the ice off the windshield before I can drive.

at skraldgrine.explanation: "At skraldgrine" means "to roar with laughter". To say what made you laugh, add "af" (at): "Vi skraldgrinede af filmen" (We roared with laughter at the movie). For a normal laugh, use "at grine" (to laugh): "Hun grinede af vittigheden" (She laughed at the joke).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **skraldgrine**, når klovnen falder i vandet.
sentence.en: The children will roar with laughter when the clown falls into the water.

at skrige.explanation: "At skrige" means "to scream". To say someone screams in pain, say: "Hun skreg af smerte" (She screamed in pain). For loud but normal calling, use "at råbe" (to shout): "Han råber på sin hund" (He shouts for his dog).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **skrige** højt, når jeg er bange.
sentence.en: I can scream loudly when I am scared.

at skrive.explanation: "At skrive" means "to write". To say you type or text a message, use the same verb: "Jeg skriver en besked" (I am writing a message).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skrive** et brev til mor.
sentence.en: I want to write a letter to Mom.

at skrive af.explanation: "At skrive af" means "to copy". It is built from "at skrive" (to write) and "af" (off). To say a pupil cheats by copying, say: "Han skrev af efter sin nabo" (He copied from his neighbor).

sentence.da: Munkene plejede at **skrive af** gamle bøger i hånden.
sentence.en: The monks used to copy old books by hand.

at skrive ned.explanation: "At skrive ned" means "to write down". To tell someone to put something on paper so they remember it, say: "Skriv det ned, så du ikke glemmer det" (Write it down so you do not forget it).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skrive ned**, hvad han siger.
sentence.en: I want to write down what he says.

at skrive til.explanation: "At skrive til" means "to write to". The person who receives the writing comes after "til" (to): "Hun skriver til sin onkel" (She writes to her uncle). To tell someone to text you, say: "Skriv til mig!" (Text me!)

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skrive til** min lærer i dag.
sentence.en: I want to write to my teacher today.

at skrubbe.explanation: "At skrubbe" means "to scrub". To say you scrub a pot, say: "Jeg skrubber gryden" (I scrub the pot). To tell someone rudely to go away, say: "Skrub af!" (Get lost!) It is rude.

sentence.da: Jeg skal **skrubbe** gulvet, fordi det er blevet meget beskidt.
sentence.en: I have to scrub the floor because it has gotten very dirty.

at skrue.explanation: "At skrue" means "to screw". To say you unscrew a lid, say: "Han skruer låget af" (He unscrews the lid). To make music quieter, use "ned" (down) and "for" (for): "Skru ned for musikken" (Turn down the music). To make it louder, use "op" (up): "Skru op for musikken" (Turn up the music).

sentence.da: Kan du **skrue** hylden fast på væggen?
sentence.en: Can you screw the shelf onto the wall?

at skrælle.explanation: "At skrælle" means "to peel". To say you peel an apple, say: "Hun skræller et æble" (She peels an apple). The noun for the skin you take off is "en skræl" (a peel).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **skrælle** fem kartofler.
sentence.en: I have to peel five potatoes.

at skræmme.explanation: "At skræmme" means "to scare". To say you scared someone, say: "Du skræmte mig!" (You scared me!) To say you are scared yourself, use "at være bange" (to be afraid): "Jeg er bange for edderkopper" (I am scared of spiders).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **skræmme** katten.
sentence.en: You must not scare the cat.

at skubbe.explanation: "At skubbe" means "to push". To tell someone to push a door open, the sign on the door says "Skub" (Push).

sentence.da: Kan du **skubbe** bilen sammen med mig?
sentence.en: Can you push the car together with me?

at skuffe.explanation: "At skuffe" means "to disappoint". To say you disappointed a person, put the person right after the verb, with no small word between: "Jeg skuffede dig" (I disappointed you). The noun "en skuffe" is a drawer: "Gaflerne ligger i skuffen" (The forks are in the drawer).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **skuffe** dig igen.
sentence.en: I do not want to disappoint you again.

at skulle.explanation: "At skulle" means "to have to or should". To say you must do something, use "skal" before the verb: "Jeg skal arbejde" (I have to work). To say where you are going, use "skal" with a place: "Jeg skal i skole" (I am going to school).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **skulle** arbejde i morgen.
sentence.en: I don't want to have to work tomorrow.

at skumme.explanation: "At skumme" means "to foam or skim". When soap or milk makes foam, use it for foaming: "Sæben skummer" (The soap is foaming). When you read something quickly, use it for skimming: "skumme en artikel" (to skim an article).

sentence.da: Mælken begynder at **skumme**, når du varmer den op.
sentence.en: The milk starts to foam when you heat it up.

at skyde.explanation: "At skyde" means "to shoot". To say a hunter shoots an animal, use it with the animal: "Jægeren skyder en hare" (The hunter shoots a hare). To say a player shoots in sports, use it with the ball: "Han skød bolden i mål" (He shot the ball into the goal).

sentence.da: Hun kan **skyde** med bue og pil.
sentence.en: She can shoot with a bow and arrow.

at skylde.explanation: "At skylde" means "to owe". To say you owe someone money, use the person and the amount: "Jeg skylder dig hundrede kroner" (I owe you a hundred kroner). To say you blame someone, add "på" (on): "Han skylder på mig" (He blames me).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **skylde** nogen penge.
sentence.en: I do not want to owe anyone money.

at skyldes.explanation: "At skyldes" means "to be due to". To name the reason for something, use it before the reason: "Problemet skyldes en fejl i systemet" (The problem is due to an error in the system). Do not mix it up with "at skylde" (to owe). To say you owe money, use "at skylde": "Jeg skylder dig hundrede kroner" (I owe you a hundred kroner).

sentence.da: Togets forsinkelse **skyldes** sne på skinnerne.
sentence.en: The train's delay is due to snow on the tracks.

at skylle.explanation: "At skylle" means "to rinse". To say you rinse something out, add "ud" (out): "Skyl munden ud" (Rinse your mouth out).

sentence.da: Du skal **skylle** grøntsagerne, før du skærer dem.
sentence.en: You should rinse the vegetables before you cut them.

at skynde sig.explanation: "At skynde sig" means "to hurry". The small word "sig" (oneself) changes with who hurries: "Jeg skynder mig" (I hurry) and "Han skynder sig" (He hurries). To tell someone to hurry, say "Skynd dig!" (Hurry up!)

sentence.da: Hun må **skynde sig**, fordi toget kører snart.
sentence.en: She has to hurry because the train leaves soon.

at skåle.explanation: "At skåle" means "to toast (with drinks)". To say who you toast, add "for" (for) before the person: "Vi skåler for dig" (We are toasting you).

sentence.da: Nu skal vi alle **skåle** for fødselaren.
sentence.en: Now we are all going to toast the birthday person.

at skåne.explanation: "At skåne" means "to spare". To say you go easy on a part of your body, use it with that part: "skåne sit knæ" (to go easy on your knee). To say you keep someone from something unpleasant, add "for" (from): "Jeg skåner dig for detaljerne" (I spare you the details).

sentence.da: Du bør **skåne** din ryg og ikke løfte tungt.
sentence.en: You should go easy on your back and not lift heavy things.

at skælve.explanation: "At skælve" means "to tremble". To say you shake from cold, add "af" (from) and the cause: "Jeg skælver af kulde" (I am trembling from cold). The verb is part of "et jordskælv" (an earthquake), literally "an earth trembling".

sentence.da: Mine hænder kan **skælve**, når jeg er meget bange.
sentence.en: My hands can tremble when I am very scared.

at skændes.explanation: "At skændes" means "to argue". To say a group argues, use it with "vi" (we): "Vi skændes aldrig" (We never argue). To name the person you argue with, add "med" (with): "Jeg skændes med min bror" (I argue with my brother).

sentence.da: Børnene **skændes** hele tiden om legetøjet.
sentence.en: The children argue all the time about the toy.

at skænke.explanation: "At skænke" means "to pour (a drink)". To offer to pour someone a drink, say: "Må jeg skænke en kop kaffe til dig?" (May I pour you a cup of coffee?) To say you give money as a gift, use "to donate" as the meaning: "skænke et beløb til en god sag" (to donate an amount to a good cause).

sentence.da: Tjeneren vil **skænke** vin til alle gæsterne.
sentence.en: The waiter will pour wine for all the guests.

at skære.explanation: "At skære" means "to cut". To say you cut food with a knife, use it with the food: "Jeg skærer brødet i stykker" (I cut the bread into pieces). To cut paper with scissors, use "at klippe" (to cut with scissors) instead: "Jeg klipper papiret" (I cut the paper).

sentence.da: Kan du **skære** løget for mig?
sentence.en: Can you cut the onion for me?

at skærpe.explanation: "At skærpe" means "to sharpen or tighten". It comes from the adjective "skarp" (sharp). To say you make rules stricter, use it with the rules: "skærpe reglerne" (to tighten the rules).

sentence.da: Politiet vil **skærpe** kontrollen i weekenden.
sentence.en: The police will tighten the checks over the weekend.

at sladre.explanation: "At sladre" means "to gossip or tell on". To say people talk about others, add "om" (about): "Naboerne sladrer om alt" (The neighbors gossip about everything). A child who tells on others is called "en sladrehank" (a tattletale).

sentence.da: Hun ville ikke **sladre** til læreren om sin bedste veninde.
sentence.en: She did not want to tattle to the teacher about her best friend.

at slanke sig.explanation: "At slanke sig" means "to diet". To say you diet, add "sig" (yourself), which changes with who diets: "Hun slanker sig" (She is dieting) and "Jeg slanker mig" (I am dieting).

sentence.da: Hun vil **slanke sig** og spiser derfor mindre brød og sukker.
sentence.en: She wants to diet and therefore eats less bread and sugar.

at slappe af.explanation: "At slappe af" means "to relax". To say you relax in a place, add the place: "Jeg slapper af på sofaen" (I relax on the sofa). To tell someone to calm down, say "Slap af!" (Relax!)

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og vil **slappe af**.
sentence.en: I am tired and want to relax.

at slentre.explanation: "At slentre" means "to stroll". To say you wander around with no goal, add "rundt" (around): "Vi slentrer rundt i byen" (We stroll around town).

sentence.da: Vi vil **slentre** langs havnen og kigge på bådene.
sentence.en: We will stroll along the harbor and look at the boats.

at slette.explanation: "At slette" means "to delete". To tell someone to delete a message, use it with the message: "Slet beskeden" (Delete the message).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **slette** alle de gamle billeder.
sentence.en: I want to delete all the old photos.

at slibe.explanation: "At slibe" means "to sharpen or sand". To say you make a knife sharp, use it with the knife: "Jeg sliber knivene" (I am sharpening the knives). To say you make wood smooth, use it with the furniture: "Jeg sliber bordet" (I am sanding the table).

sentence.da: Du skal **slibe** bordet med sandpapir, før du maler det.
sentence.en: You have to sand the table with sandpaper before you paint it.

at slide.explanation: "At slide" means "to wear out or toil". To say things wear out from use, use "slide op": "Skoene slides op, når man går meget i dem" (The shoes wear out when you walk a lot in them). To say someone works very hard, use the phrase "slide og slæbe" (to toil and drag).

sentence.da: Han må **slide** hårdt for at brødføde sin store familie.
sentence.en: He has to toil hard to feed his large family.

at slikke.explanation: "At slikke" means "to lick". To say you lick an ice cream, use it with the ice cream: "at slikke en is" (to lick an ice cream). To say you lie in the sun, use "slikke sol" (literally, to lick sun).

sentence.da: Katte bruger tungen til at **slikke** sig rene.
sentence.en: Cats use their tongues to lick themselves clean.

at slippe.explanation: "At slippe" means "to let go or escape". To tell someone to let go of you, say "Slip mig!" (Let go of me!) To say someone got away, add "væk" (away): "Han slap væk" (He got away). To say you were spared from doing something, add "for" (from): "Jeg slap for at vaske op" (I got out of doing the dishes).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **slippe** snoren nu.
sentence.en: You must not let go of the string now.

at slippe af med.explanation: "At slippe af med" means "to get rid of". It is built from "at slippe" (to escape) and "af med" (off with). To say you got rid of an illness, use it with the illness: "Hun slap af med sin forkølelse" (She got rid of her cold).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **slippe af med** min gamle sofa.
sentence.en: I would like to get rid of my old sofa.

at sludre.explanation: "At sludre" means "to chat". To say you chat with someone, add "med" (with): "sludre med naboen" (to chat with the neighbor). The noun "sludder" means "nonsense": "Det er sludder!" (That is nonsense!)

sentence.da: Vi kan **sludre** over en kop kaffe i dag.
sentence.en: We can chat over a cup of coffee today.

at sluge.explanation: "At sluge" means "to swallow". To say you swallow a pill, use it with the pill: "Hun slugte tabletten uden vand" (She swallowed the pill without water). To say someone eats very fast, use it for "to gulp down": "Han slugte maden på to minutter" (He gulped the food down in two minutes).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **sluge** den store tablet.
sentence.en: I cannot swallow the big pill.

at slukke.explanation: "At slukke" means "to turn off". To say you turn off a light, use it with the light: "slukke lyset" (turn off the light). To say you put out a fire, use it with the fire: "slukke en brand" (put out a fire). To turn off a TV, add "for" (for): "slukke for fjernsynet" (turn off the TV).

sentence.da: Husk at **slukke** lyset.
sentence.en: Remember to turn off the light.

at slukke for.explanation: "At slukke for" means "to turn off". To say you turn off the TV, the radio or the heating, add "for" (for) after the verb: "Jeg slukker for radioen" (I turn off the radio). To say you put out a fire, use "at slukke" (to put out) with no "for": "slukke en brand" (to put out a fire).

sentence.da: Husk at **slukke for** fjernsynet.
sentence.en: Remember to turn off the TV.

at slutte.explanation: "At slutte" means "to end or finish". To say when something ends, use it with the time: "Skolen slutter klokken tre" (School ends at three). To say you stop doing something, add "med" (with) and "at" (to): "Jeg slutter med at ryge" (I am quitting smoking).

sentence.da: Filmen skal **slutte** om en time.
sentence.en: The movie is going to end in an hour.

at slutte fred.explanation: "At slutte fred" means "to make peace". To name the person you make peace with, add "med" (with): "Jeg har sluttet fred med min bror" (I have made peace with my brother). To say you accept something that hurt you, use it for an inner struggle: "slutte fred med fortiden" (to make peace with the past).

sentence.da: Efter mange års krig vil landene endelig **slutte fred**.
sentence.en: After many years of war the countries finally want to make peace.

at slå.explanation: "At slå" means "to hit or beat". To say you strike someone, use it with the person: "Slå ikke din bror!" (Do not hit your brother!) To say a team or player wins against another, use it for beating: "Vi slog dem tre-nul" (We beat them three to nothing). To say you cut a lawn, use it with the grass: "slå græsset" (mow the lawn).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **slå** et søm i væggen med en hammer.
sentence.en: I can hit a nail into the wall with a hammer.

at slå et smut forbi.explanation: "At slå et smut forbi" means "to drop by". To say the visit is short and casual, add "lige" (just): "Vi slår lige et smut forbi bageren" (We will just stop by the bakery).

forms.da: jeg har slået et smut forbi

sentence.da: Jeg kan **slå et smut forbi** dig på vej hjem.
sentence.en: I can drop by your place on my way home.

at slå græs.explanation: "At slå græs" means "to mow the lawn". It is built from "slå" (hit) and "græs" (grass), so it is literally "to hit grass". To say you hit a ball, the same "slå" is used: "at slå en bold" (to hit a ball).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **slå græs**, fordi græsset er blevet langt.
sentence.en: I have to mow the lawn because the grass has gotten long.

at slå igennem.explanation: "At slå igennem" means "to break through". To say someone becomes a star, use it for a career: "Hun slog igennem som sangerinde" (She became a star as a singer). To say the sun comes out from behind clouds, use it with the sun: "Solen slår igennem" (The sun breaks through).

sentence.da: Mange unge musikere drømmer om at **slå igennem**.
sentence.en: Many young musicians dream of breaking through.

at slå op.explanation: "At slå op" means "to look up". To say you look up a word, use it with the word: "Jeg slår ordet op" (I look up the word). To say you end a relationship, add "med" (with) and the partner: "Hun slog op med ham" (She broke up with him).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **slå op** i ordbogen.
sentence.en: I have to look it up in the dictionary.

at slå sig ned.explanation: "At slå sig ned" means "to settle down". To say a family makes a new home somewhere, add the place: "Familien slog sig ned i Aarhus" (The family settled in Aarhus). To say you sit down for a while, use it with the place you sit: "Vi slog os ned på en bænk" (We took a seat on a bench).

sentence.da: Efter mange år i udlandet ville de **slå sig ned** i Danmark.
sentence.en: After many years abroad they wanted to settle down in Denmark.

at slå to fluer med et smæk.explanation: "At slå to fluer med et smæk" means "to kill two birds with one stone". Danish has two flies and one smack in this saying, not birds and a stone. It is built from "at slå" (to hit).

forms.da: Jeg vil slå to fluer med et smæk
forms.en: I want to kill two birds with one stone

forms.da: Her slår vi to fluer med et smæk
forms.en: Here we kill two birds with one stone

forms.da: at slå to fluer med et smæk
forms.en: to kill two birds with one stone

sentence.da: Du kan **slå to fluer med et smæk** ved at cykle på arbejde.
sentence.en: You can kill two birds with one stone by cycling to work.

at slå ud.explanation: "At slå ud" means "to knock out". To say a team beats another team so it leaves the competition, use it with the losing team: "Danmark slog Tyskland ud" (Denmark knocked Germany out). To say trees come into leaf, use it with the trees: "Træerne slår ud i maj" (The trees come into leaf in May). To say a fuse cuts the power, use it with the fuse: "Sikringen slår ud" (The fuse trips).

sentence.da: Hvis strømmen bliver for stærk, kan sikringen **slå ud**.
sentence.en: If the current gets too strong, the fuse can trip.

at slæbe.explanation: "At slæbe" means "to drag". To say you carry or pull something heavy with effort, use it with the thing: "Han slæbte kufferten hen til bilen" (He dragged the suitcase to the car). To say you walk home with no energy, add "mig" (myself): "Jeg slæber mig hjem" (I drag myself home).

sentence.da: Vi skal **slæbe** de tunge kasser op ad trappen.
sentence.en: We have to haul the heavy boxes up the stairs.

at smadre.explanation: "At smadre" means "to smash". To say a team beats an opponent by a lot, use it for a heavy defeat: "Holdet smadrede modstanderen" (The team beat the opponent badly). To say something is already smashed, use "smadret" (smashed): "Glasset er smadret" (The glass is smashed).

sentence.da: Glas kan **smadre**, når det rammer gulvet.
sentence.en: Glass can smash when it hits the floor.

at smage.explanation: "At smage" means "to taste". To say you try food, use it with the food: "Jeg smager på suppen" (I taste the soup). To say how something tastes, use "Det smager godt" (It tastes good). To name the flavor, add "af" (of): "Det smager af citron" (It tastes like lemon).

sentence.da: Må jeg **smage** din suppe?
sentence.en: May I taste your soup?

at smelte.explanation: "At smelte" means "to melt". To say something melts by itself, use it with the thing: "Isen smelter i solen" (The ice melts in the sun). To say you melt something yourself, use it with the thing you melt: "Jeg smelter smør" (I melt butter).

sentence.da: Sneen vil **smelte**, når det bliver varmt.
sentence.en: The snow will melt when it gets warm.

at smide.explanation: "At smide" means "to throw (away)". To say you throw away trash, use it with the trash and the place: "Jeg smider papiret i skraldespanden" (I throw the paper in the trash can). To say you throw a ball to someone, use "at kaste" (to throw) instead: "Han kaster bolden til mig" (He throws the ball to me).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **smide** affald på gaden.
sentence.en: You must not throw trash on the street.

at smide ud.explanation: "At smide ud" means "to throw out". To say you throw out old food, use it with the food: "Jeg smider maden ud" (I throw the food out). To say someone is made to leave a place, use it with "af" (out of) and the place: "De smed ham ud af baren" (They threw him out of the bar).

sentence.da: Vi skal **smide ud**, hvad vi ikke bruger.
sentence.en: We have to throw out what we do not use.

at smile.explanation: "At smile" means "to smile". To say what or who you smile at, add "til" (to): "Smil til kameraet!" (Smile for the camera!)

sentence.da: Hun er glad og kan **smile** til alle.
sentence.en: She is happy and can smile at everyone.

at sminke sig.explanation: "At sminke sig" means "to put on makeup". To say who puts on makeup, change "sig" (oneself) with the person: "Hun sminker sig" (She puts on makeup) and "Du sminker dig" (You put on makeup).

sentence.da: Hun vil **sminke sig** og tage en kjole på.
sentence.en: She wants to put on makeup and put on a dress.

at smitte.explanation: "At smitte" means "to infect". To say you pass an illness on to someone, use it with the person: "Jeg vil ikke smitte dig" (I do not want to infect you). To say a mood spreads, use it for laughter: "Hendes latter smitter" (Her laughter is catching).

sentence.da: Du kan **smitte** andre, når du er syg.
sentence.en: You can infect others when you are sick.

at smugle.explanation: "At smugle" means "to smuggle". To say someone secretly brings a small thing into a place, use it with the thing and the place: "Han smuglede slik ind i biografen" (He smuggled candy into the movie theater).

sentence.da: Det er ulovligt at **smugle** varer over grænsen.
sentence.en: It is illegal to smuggle goods across the border.

at smuldre.explanation: "At smuldre" means "to crumble". To say food comes apart in small pieces, use it with the food: "Kagen smuldrer" (The cake crumbles). To say hopes fall apart, use it with the hopes: "Hans håb smuldrede" (His hopes crumbled).

sentence.da: Murstenene i den gamle mur begynder at **smuldre**.
sentence.en: The bricks in the old wall begin to crumble.

at smutte.explanation: "At smutte" means "to slip away or pop out". To say you leave for a short moment, add "lige" (just): "Jeg smutter lige ud" (I will just pop out). To say something slips by accident, use it with the thing: "Kniven smuttede" (The knife slipped).

forms.en: I have slipped away / popped out

sentence.da: Jeg vil lige **smutte** ned i supermarkedet.
sentence.en: I'll just pop down to the supermarket.

at smøre.explanation: "At smøre" means "to spread or butter". To say you put butter on bread, use it with the bread and "med" (with): "Jeg smører brødet med smør" (I spread butter on the bread). To say you make a packed lunch, use it with "en madpakke" (a packed lunch): "at smøre en madpakke" (to make a packed lunch).

sentence.da: Kan du **smøre** et stykke brød til mig?
sentence.en: Can you butter a slice of bread for me?

at snakke.explanation: "At snakke" means "to talk or chat". To ask someone to talk with you, say: "Skal vi snakke sammen?" (Shall we talk together?)

sentence.da: Jeg har tid og kan **snakke** nu.
sentence.en: I have time and can talk now.

at snakke om.explanation: "At snakke om" means "to talk about". To name the topic, put it after "om" (about): "Vi snakker om mad" (We are talking about food). To name the person you talk with, use "snakke med" (talk with): "Jeg snakker med min mor" (I talk with my mother).

sentence.da: Vi vil **snakke om** vores ferie i aften.
sentence.en: We want to talk about our vacation tonight.

at snakke om vejret.explanation: "At snakke om vejret" means "to make small talk", literally "to talk about the weather". To name another topic, replace "vejret" (the weather) with it: "snakke om fodbold" (to talk about football).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke bare **snakke om vejret** med dig.
sentence.en: I don't just want to make small talk with you.

at sne.explanation: "At sne" means "to snow". To say it is snowing, use "det" (it): "Det sner" (It is snowing). The noun is spelled the same, "sne" (snow): "Der er sne" (There is snow).

sentence.da: I vinter kan det **sne** meget.
sentence.en: In winter it can snow a lot.

at snige sig.explanation: "At snige sig" means "to sneak". To say which way you sneak, add a direction word: "at snige sig ind" (to sneak in) and "at snige sig ud" (to sneak out).

sentence.da: Katten vil **snige sig** hen til fuglen uden en lyd.
sentence.en: The cat wants to sneak over to the bird without a sound.

at snooze.explanation: "At snooze" means "to snooze". It is borrowed from the English word "snooze". To say you sleep late on purpose, use "at sove længe" (to sleep in): "I morgen sover jeg længe" (Tomorrow I will sleep in).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **snooze** i fem minutter mere.
sentence.en: I want to snooze for five more minutes.

at snorke.explanation: "At snorke" means "to snore". To tell someone to stop, say: "Hold op med at snorke!" (Stop snoring!)

sentence.da: Min far plejer at **snorke** meget højt.
sentence.en: My dad usually snores very loudly.

at snuble.explanation: "At snuble" means "to stumble". To name the thing you trip on, use "over" (over): "snuble over et kabel" (to trip over a cable). To say you hit a problem in a word, use it with a word: "snuble over et svært ord" (to stumble over a hard word).

sentence.da: Det er nemt at **snuble** på en våd trappe.
sentence.en: It is easy to stumble on a wet staircase.

at snuppe.explanation: "At snuppe" means "to snatch or grab". To say someone takes a thing quickly, use it with the thing: "Han snuppede min kuglepen" (He grabbed my pen). To suggest a quick small thing together, use it for "to grab": "Skal vi snuppe en kop kaffe?" (Shall we grab a cup of coffee?)

sentence.da: Du kan lige **snuppe** en kage, og så går vi.
sentence.en: You can quickly grab a cake, and then we go.

at snyde.explanation: "At snyde" means "to cheat". To say you cheat someone out of money, add "for" (of) and the amount: "Han snød mig for hundrede kroner" (He cheated me out of a hundred kroner).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **snyde** til en eksamen.
sentence.en: You must not cheat on an exam.

at snøfte.explanation: "At snøfte" means "to sniffle". To say a child sniffles after crying, use it for the child: "Barnet snøftede længe bagefter" (The child sniffled for a long time afterward).

sentence.da: Han vil **snøfte** hele dagen, fordi han er forkølet.
sentence.en: He will sniffle all day because he has a cold.

at sortere.explanation: "At sortere" means "to sort". To say you sort trash, use it with the trash: "Vi sorterer affald" (We sort the trash).

sentence.da: Vi skal **sortere** tøjet efter farve.
sentence.en: We have to sort the clothes by color.

at sove.explanation: "At sove" means "to sleep". To say you sleep well, add "godt" (well): "Jeg sover godt" (I sleep well). To say you go to bed, use "at gå i seng" (to go to bed): "Jeg går i seng klokken ti" (I go to bed at ten).

sentence.da: Børnene er trætte og vil **sove**.
sentence.en: The children are tired and want to sleep.

at sove længe.explanation: "At sove længe" means "to sleep in". It is built from "at sove" (to sleep) and "længe" (a long time). To say you slept in, use it in the past: "Jeg sov længe i går" (I slept in yesterday).

sentence.da: I morgen er det lørdag, og jeg vil **sove længe**.
sentence.en: Tomorrow is Saturday, and I want to sleep in.

at sove over sig.explanation: "At sove over sig" means "to oversleep", literally "to sleep over yourself". To say you overslept and were late, say: "Jeg sov over mig og kom for sent" (I overslept and was late). To sleep late on purpose, use "at sove længe" (to sleep in): "I morgen sover jeg længe" (Tomorrow I will sleep in).

sentence.da: Hun vil ikke **sove over sig** i morgen.
sentence.en: She does not want to oversleep tomorrow.

at spadsere.explanation: "At spadsere" means "to stroll or walk". To say you go for a plain walk, use "at gå en tur" (to go for a walk): "Vi går en tur i skoven" (We go for a walk in the forest).

sentence.da: Vi vil **spadsere** langs havnen og nyde solen.
sentence.en: We want to stroll along the harbor and enjoy the sun.

at spare.explanation: "At spare" means "to save (money)". To say you put money aside for a trip, use it with the money: "Vi sparer penge til en rejse" (We are saving money for a trip). To say something gives you more time, use it with "tid" (time): "Det sparer tid" (That saves time).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spare** penge til en ny cykel.
sentence.en: I want to save money for a new bike.

at spare op.explanation: "At spare op" means "to save up". To say what you save up for, add "til" (for): "Jeg sparer op til en cykel" (I am saving up for a bike). To say you save time, leave out "op" (up): "at spare tid" (to save time).

sentence.da: Vi vil **spare op**, så vi kan købe et hus.
sentence.en: We want to save up so we can buy a house.

at spare på.explanation: "At spare på" means "to save on". To say you use less of something, use it with the thing: "Vi sparer på varmen" (We are saving on heat). To say you are careful with something, use it the same way: "Hun sparer på pengene" (She is careful with the money).

sentence.da: Vi skal **spare på** strømmen i vinter.
sentence.en: We have to save on electricity this winter.

at sparke.explanation: "At sparke" means "to kick". To say you kick a ball, use it with the ball: "Han sparkede bolden over hegnet" (He kicked the ball over the fence). To say you give something one kick, add "til" (to): "Hun sparkede til døren" (She gave the door a kick).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **sparke** bolden i mål.
sentence.en: The kids want to kick the ball into the goal.

at specialisere sig.explanation: "At specialisere sig" means "to specialize". To say the field, add "i" (in) after it: "at specialisere sig i hjertekirurgi" (to specialize in heart surgery).

sentence.da: Efter studiet vil lægen **specialisere sig** i hjertesygdomme.
sentence.en: After university, the doctor wants to specialize in heart disease.

at spejle.explanation: "At spejle" means "to mirror". It comes from the noun "et spejl" (a mirror). To say you look at your own image in a surface, add "sig" (yourself): "Hun spejler sig i vinduet" (She looks at herself in the window).

sentence.da: Bjergene kan **spejle** sig i den stille sø.
sentence.en: The mountains can be mirrored in the quiet lake.

at spekulere.explanation: "At spekulere" means "to speculate or wonder". To name what you wonder about, add "på" (about): "Jeg spekulerer på det" (I wonder about that). To say you invest money in something, add "i" (in): "spekulere i aktier" (to speculate in shares).

sentence.da: Hun begyndte at **spekulere** på, hvorfor han var så stille.
sentence.en: She began to wonder why he was so quiet.

at spilde.explanation: "At spilde" means "to waste or spill". To say liquid runs out by accident, use it with the liquid: "Jeg spildte vand på bordet" (I spilled water on the table). To say you waste something, use it with the thing: "Vi må ikke spilde mad" (We must not waste food).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **spilde** min tid på det.
sentence.en: I do not want to waste my time on that.

at spilde tid.explanation: "At spilde tid" means "to waste time". To say what wastes your time, add "på" (on): "Jeg spilder tid på telefonen" (I waste time on the phone). The verb "at spilde" (to waste) also works without "tid" (time) to mean "to spill": "Jeg spildte kaffe" (I spilled coffee).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **spilde tid** på det her.
sentence.en: I do not want to waste time on this.

at spille.explanation: "At spille" means "to play". To say you play a game, a sport or an instrument, use it with that word: "Vi spiller fodbold" (We play soccer). To say an actor plays a part, use it with the part: "Hun spiller en prinsesse" (She plays a princess). To say children play for fun, use "at lege" (to play) instead: "Børnene leger i haven" (The children are playing in the garden).

sentence.da: Min bror kan **spille** guitar og synge.
sentence.en: My brother can play the guitar and sing.

at spille en rolle.explanation: "At spille en rolle" means "to play a role". To say someone acts a part on stage, use it with the place: "Hun spiller en rolle i skolens teater" (She plays a role in the school theater). To say something does not matter, use it with "ikke nogen" (not any): "Prisen spiller ikke nogen rolle" (The price does not matter).

sentence.da: Han vil gerne **spille en rolle** i filmen.
sentence.en: He would like to play a role in the movie.

at spille fodbold.explanation: "At spille fodbold" means "to play soccer". The word "fodbold" is built from "fod" (foot) and "bold" (ball). The verb "at spille" (to play) works for other sports too: "spille håndbold" (to play handball).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **spille fodbold** i dag.
sentence.en: The children want to play soccer today.

at spise.explanation: "At spise" means "to eat". To say you eat at a restaurant, add "ude" (out): "Vi spiser ude i aften" (We are eating out tonight). To say you drink, use "at drikke" (to drink) instead: "Jeg drikker vand" (I drink water).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spise** brød, ost og æbler.
sentence.en: I want to eat bread, cheese and apples.

at sponsorere.explanation: "At sponsorere" means "to sponsor". To say a company pays for an event, use it with the event: "Firmaet sponsorerer kampen" (The company sponsors the match). The person or company that does it is "en sponsor" (a sponsor).

sentence.da: Et lokalt firma vil **sponsorere** fodboldholdets nye trøjer.
sentence.en: A local company wants to sponsor the soccer team's new shirts.

at spore.explanation: "At spore" means "to track or trace". It is built on "et spor" (a trail or footprint). To say you trace where a call came from, use it with the call: "spore et opkald" (to trace a call).

sentence.da: Med et nummer kan du **spore** din pakke på nettet.
sentence.en: With a number you can track your package online.

at sprede.explanation: "At sprede" means "to spread". To say something spreads by itself, add "sig" (itself): "Rygtet spreder sig" (The rumor spreads). To say someone spreads something, leave out "sig": "Han spreder rygtet" (He spreads the rumor).

sentence.da: Vinden kan **sprede** frøene over hele marken.
sentence.en: The wind can spread the seeds over the whole field.

at springe.explanation: "At springe" means "to jump". To say you skip a page, add "over" (over): "Jeg springer en side over" (I skip a page).

sentence.da: Hunden kan **springe** over hegnet.
sentence.en: The dog can jump over the fence.

at springe over.explanation: "At springe over" means "to skip". To say you leave out a meal, use it with the meal: "Jeg springer frokosten over" (I skip lunch). To say you jump across something, use it with the thing: "Hunden sprang over hegnet" (The dog jumped over the fence).

sentence.da: Jeg vil aldrig **springe over** morgenmaden.
sentence.en: I will never skip breakfast.

at sprænge.explanation: "At sprænge" means "to blow up". To say explosives destroy something, use it with the thing: "at sprænge en bro" (to blow up a bridge). To say you go over a limit, use it with the limit: "at sprænge budgettet" (to blow the budget).

sentence.da: Arbejderne bruger dynamit til at **sprænge** klippen.
sentence.en: The workers use dynamite to blow up the rock.

at sprøjte.explanation: "At sprøjte" means "to spray". The noun "en sprøjte" (a syringe) is spelled the same way: "Lægen giver mig en sprøjte" (The doctor gives me an injection).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **sprøjte** vand på hinanden.
sentence.en: The children want to spray water on each other.

at spytte.explanation: "At spytte" means "to spit". To say where you spit, add "på" (on): "spytte på gulvet" (spit on the floor). To say a dragon breathes out fire, use it with the fire: "Dragen spytter ild" (The dragon spits fire).

sentence.da: Barnet kan ikke lide smagen og vil **spytte** den ud.
sentence.en: The child does not like the taste and wants to spit it out.

at spænde.explanation: "At spænde" means "to tighten or fasten". To tell someone to pull a strap tight, say: "Spænd remmen" (Tighten the strap). To say you tense your body, use it with the muscles: "Jeg spænder musklerne" (I tense my muscles).

sentence.da: Du skal altid **spænde** sikkerhedsbæltet i bilen.
sentence.en: You must always fasten the seat belt in the car.

at spøge.explanation: "At spøge" means "to joke". To say you are not serious, add "kun" (only): "Jeg spøger kun" (I am only joking). To say a ghost is in a place, use "det" (it) and the place: "Det spøger i huset" (The house is haunted).

sentence.da: Han kan godt **spøge** med sin egen fejl, og alle griner.
sentence.en: He can joke about his own mistake, and everyone laughs.

at spørge.explanation: "At spørge" means "to ask". To ask a person about something, add "om" (about): "Jeg spørger ham om vejen" (I ask him about the way). To ask for something you want, use "at bede om" (to ask for) instead: "Jeg beder om en kop kaffe" (I ask for a cup of coffee).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spørge** læreren.
sentence.en: I want to ask the teacher.

at spørge om.explanation: "At spørge om" means "to ask about". To ask about a thing, put it after "om" (about): "spørge om prisen" (ask about the price). To ask for something you need, use it the same way: "spørge om hjælp" (ask for help).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spørge om** hjælp.
sentence.en: I want to ask for help.

at spørge om vej.explanation: "At spørge om vej" means "to ask for directions", literally "to ask about way". To stop a stranger and ask, say: "Undskyld, må jeg spørge om vej?" (Excuse me, may I ask for directions?)

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spørge om vej** til banegården.
sentence.en: I want to ask for directions to the station.

at stabilisere.explanation: "At stabilisere" means "to stabilize". To say something steadies by itself, add "sig" (itself): "Priserne stabiliserer sig" (The prices stabilize).

sentence.da: Vi bruger en stang til at **stabilisere** det høje telt.
sentence.en: We use a pole to stabilize the tall tent.

at stadfæste.explanation: "At stadfæste" means "to confirm or uphold". To say a court keeps a decision, use it with the decision: "Retten stadfæstede dommen" (The court upheld the verdict).

sentence.da: Kongen kan **stadfæste** en ny lov, og så gælder den.
sentence.en: The king can formally approve a new law, and then it applies.

at stamme.explanation: "At stamme" means "to stutter or come from". To say someone stutters, use it alone: "Han stammer, når han er nervøs" (He stutters when he is nervous). To say where something comes from, add "fra" (from): "Min familie stammer fra Jylland" (My family comes from Jutland).

sentence.da: Mange danske ord kan **stamme** fra tysk.
sentence.en: Many Danish words can come from German.

at standse.explanation: "At standse" means "to stop". To say a vehicle comes to a halt, use it with the vehicle: "Bilen standsede foran huset" (The car stopped in front of the house). To say you quit a habit, use "at holde op" (to quit) instead: "Jeg holder op med at ryge" (I am quitting smoking).

sentence.da: Bussen skal **standse** ved stationen.
sentence.en: The bus has to stop at the station.

at starte.explanation: "At starte" means "to start". To say an event begins, use it with the time: "Vi starter i morgen" (We start tomorrow). To say a machine will not run, use it with the machine: "Bilen starter ikke" (The car will not start). To say a lesson begins, "at begynde" (to begin) works too: "Timen begynder klokken ni" (The lesson begins at nine).

sentence.da: Filmen skal **starte** klokken otte.
sentence.en: The movie is going to start at eight.

at starte på.explanation: "At starte på" means "to start on". To say you begin a task, put "på" (on) before the task: "Jeg starter på opgaven" (I start on the assignment). To say an engine or a machine starts, use "at starte" (to start) without "på": "Bilen starter ikke" (The car does not start).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **starte på** et nyt projekt i dag.
sentence.en: I want to start on a new project today.

at stave.explanation: "At stave" means "to spell". To ask someone how a word is spelled, use it with "man" (one): "Hvordan staver man det?" (How do you spell that?)

sentence.da: Kan du **stave** dit navn?
sentence.en: Can you spell your name?

at stege.explanation: "At stege" means "to fry or to roast". To say you cook meat in a pan, say: "Jeg steger kød i panden" (I fry meat in the pan). To say you cook a duck in the oven, say: "Vi steger en and i ovnen" (We roast a duck in the oven). To cook in water, use "at koge" (to boil): "Jeg koger kartofler" (I boil potatoes).

forms.en: I have fried, I have roasted

sentence.da: Jeg skal **stege** æggene i panden.
sentence.en: I am going to fry the eggs in the pan.

at stemme.explanation: "At stemme" means "to vote". To say who you vote for, add "på" (on): "Jeg stemmer på ham" (I vote for him). To say a fact is correct, use the same verb: "Det stemmer!" (That is right!)

sentence.da: Alle over atten år kan **stemme** ved valget.
sentence.en: Everyone over eighteen can vote in the election.

at stemme på.explanation: "At stemme på" means "to vote for". To name the person or party you choose, put it after "på" (on), where English says "for": "Vi stemte på Peter" (We voted for Peter).

sentence.da: Til valget vil jeg **stemme på** Anna.
sentence.en: At the election, I want to vote for Anna.

at stige.explanation: "At stige" means "to rise or climb". To say a price goes up, say: "Prisen stiger" (The price is rising). To say you climb stairs, add "op ad" (up along): "Han stiger op ad trappen" (He climbs up the stairs). To say you get into a car, add "ind" (in): "Hun steg ind i bilen" (She got into the car).

sentence.da: Temperaturen kan **stige** til tredive grader.
sentence.en: The temperature can rise to thirty degrees.

at stige af.explanation: "At stige af" means "to get off". To say you leave a bus, a train or a bike, put "af" (off) after the verb: "Hun stiger af cyklen" (She gets off the bike). To say the opposite, use "at stige på" (to get on): "Jeg stiger på bussen" (I get on the bus).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **stige af** bussen ved torvet.
sentence.en: I will get off the bus at the square.

at stige på.explanation: "At stige på" means "to get on". To say you board a bus, a train or a bike, put "på" (on) after the verb: "Vi stiger på toget i Odense" (We get on the train in Odense). To say the opposite, use "at stige af" (to get off): "Hun stiger af toget" (She gets off the train).

sentence.da: Vi må **stige på** bussen nu.
sentence.en: We have to get on the bus now.

at stikke.explanation: "At stikke" means "to stick or sting". To say an insect stings you, say: "Bien stak mig" (The bee stung me). To say you push something into a place, add "i" (in): "Jeg stikker pengene i lommen" (I stick the money in my pocket).

sentence.da: Du skal **stikke** nøglen i døren.
sentence.en: You have to stick the key in the door.

at stikke af.explanation: "At stikke af" means "to run off". It is built from "at stikke" (to stick) and "af" (off). To tell what a thief did, say: "Tyven stak af" (The thief ran off).

sentence.da: Drengen ville **stikke af**, men læreren så ham.
sentence.en: The boy wanted to run off, but the teacher saw him.

at stikke en finger i jorden.explanation: "At stikke en finger i jorden" means "to take stock". Literally, it is "to stick a finger in the ground".

forms.da: Vi må stikke en finger i jorden
Hun stak en finger i jorden
Lad os stikke en finger i jorden

sentence.da: Vi må **stikke en finger i jorden** og se, hvor vi står.
sentence.en: We must take stock and see where we stand.

at stikke en kæp i hjulet.explanation: "At stikke en kæp i hjulet" means "to throw a wrench in the works". Literally, it is "to stick a stick in the wheel". To name the person whose plan you spoil, add "for" (for) and the person: "Jeg vil ikke stikke en kæp i hjulet for dig" (I do not want to spoil things for you).

forms.da: Han stikker en kæp i hjulet
forms.en: He throws a wrench in the works

forms.da: Hun stak en kæp i hjulet for os
Stik ikke en kæp i hjulet for dem
forms.en: Do not spoil things for them

sentence.da: Naboen vil **stikke en kæp i hjulet** for vores byggeplan.
sentence.en: The neighbor wants to throw a wrench in the works of our building plan.

at stille.explanation: "At stille" means "to put or place (upright)". To put something that stands, like a bottle, on a table, say: "Jeg stiller flasken på bordet" (I put the bottle on the table). To put something flat, like a book, use "at lægge" (to lay): "Jeg lægger bogen på bordet" (I put the book on the table).

sentence.da: Kan du **stille** flasken på bordet?
sentence.en: Can you put the bottle on the table?

at stille et spørgsmål.explanation: "At stille et spørgsmål" means "to ask a question". Literally, it is "to put a question". To ask a person directly, use "at spørge" (to ask): "Jeg vil spørge dig om noget" (I want to ask you something).

sentence.da: Må jeg **stille et spørgsmål** om lektien?
sentence.en: May I ask a question about the homework?

at stille op.explanation: "At stille op" means "to run (for office)". To say someone puts their name forward in an election, say: "Han stiller op for partiet" (He runs for the party). To say a team turns up to play, say: "Holdet stiller op til kampen" (The team turns out for the match). To say people line up, add "sig" (oneself): "Børnene stiller sig op i en række" (The children line up in a row).

sentence.da: Hun vil **stille op** til valget som borgmester.
sentence.en: She wants to run for mayor in the election.

at stille uret.explanation: "At stille uret" means "to set the clock". To say you move the clock ahead, add "en time frem" (an hour forward): "Vi stiller uret en time frem" (We set the clock an hour forward).

sentence.da: Vi skal **stille uret** en time tilbage.
sentence.en: We have to set the clock back an hour.

at stimulere.explanation: "At stimulere" means "to stimulate". To say you boost the economy, put "økonomien" (the economy) after it: "at stimulere økonomien" (to stimulate the economy).

sentence.da: Leg kan **stimulere** børns fantasi og nysgerrighed.
sentence.en: Play can stimulate children's imagination and curiosity.

at stirre.explanation: "At stirre" means "to stare". To name what you stare at, use "på" (at): "Hun stirrer på skærmen" (She stares at the screen). To say you stare into space, use "ud i luften" (out into the air): "Han stirrer ud i luften" (He stares into space).

sentence.da: Det er uhøfligt at **stirre** på fremmede mennesker.
sentence.en: It is rude to stare at strangers.

at stjæle.explanation: "At stjæle" means "to steal". To say something was taken from you, say: "Nogen stjal min cykel" (Someone stole my bicycle). To say someone robbed a bank, use "at røve" (to rob): "Han røvede banken" (He robbed the bank).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **stjæle** fra andre.
sentence.en: You must not steal from others.

at stole på.explanation: "At stole på" means "to trust". To say you trust someone, put "på" (on) before the person: "Jeg stoler på min læge" (I trust my doctor). In a sentence with "ikke" (not), "ikke" goes between the two words: "Jeg stoler ikke på ham" (I do not trust him).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **stole på** min bedste ven.
sentence.en: I can trust my best friend.

at stoppe.explanation: "At stoppe" means "to stop". To say you quit doing something, add "med at" (with to) and a verb: "Jeg stopper med at spise slik" (I stop eating candy).

sentence.da: Bilen skal **stoppe** ved det røde lys.
sentence.en: The car has to stop at the red light.

at straffe.explanation: "At straffe" means "to punish". To say what someone is punished for, add "for" (for): "Han blev straffet for sin fejl" (He was punished for his mistake).

sentence.da: Dommeren kan **straffe** en spiller med et rødt kort.
sentence.en: The referee can punish a player with a red card.

at stramme.explanation: "At stramme" means "to tighten". To tighten a screw, say: "Jeg strammer skruen" (I tighten the screw). To say rules become stricter, say: "at stramme reglerne" (to make the rules stricter).

sentence.da: Man kan **stramme** et bælte, når det sidder løst.
sentence.en: You can tighten a belt when it is loose.

at streame.explanation: "At streame" means "to stream". The Danish verb is borrowed from the English word "stream".

sentence.da: Vi vil **streame** en film i aften.
sentence.en: We want to stream a movie tonight.

at strejke.explanation: "At strejke" means "to strike", as in stopping work as a protest. To say the teachers are on strike, say: "Lærerne strejker" (The teachers are on strike). The noun is "strejke" (strike): "Der er strejke på skolen i dag" (There is a strike at the school today).

sentence.da: Lærerne vil **strejke**, fordi de ønsker højere løn.
sentence.en: The teachers want to strike because they want higher pay.

at strikke.explanation: "At strikke" means "to knit". To mix it up with the other yarn craft, use "at hækle" (to crochet): "Jeg hækler et tæppe" (I crochet a blanket).

sentence.da: Min mormor kan **strikke** en varm trøje.
sentence.en: My grandmother can knit a warm sweater.

at stryge.explanation: "At stryge" means "to iron". To say you iron clothes, say: "Jeg stryger tøj" (I iron clothes). To say you stroke a pet, use the same verb: "Hun stryger katten" (She strokes the cat).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **stryge** en skjorte før mødet.
sentence.en: I have to iron a shirt before the meeting.

at stræbe.explanation: "At stræbe" means "to strive". To name the goal you strive for, use "efter" (after): "stræbe efter succes" (to strive for success). The adjective "stræbsom" (ambitious) comes from the same verb.

sentence.da: Han vil **stræbe** efter at blive den bedste i klassen.
sentence.en: He wants to strive to become the best in the class.

at strække.explanation: "At strække" means "to stretch". To say you stretch something out, say: "Han strækker armene" (He stretches his arms). To say you stretch your own body, add "sig" (oneself): "Katten strækker sig" (The cat stretches).

sentence.da: Det er vigtigt at **strække** benene efter løbeturen.
sentence.en: It is important to stretch your legs after the run.

at strække sig.explanation: "At strække sig" means "to stretch". To say you stretch after a workout, say: "Han strækker sig efter træning" (He stretches after exercise). The small word "sig" (oneself) changes with who stretches: "vi strækker os" (we stretch).

sentence.da: Katten vil **strække sig** i solen.
sentence.en: The cat wants to stretch in the sun.

at strø.explanation: "At strø" means "to sprinkle or scatter". To say someone spends money freely, add "om sig" (around oneself): "Han strør om sig med penge" (He throws money around).

sentence.da: Vi må **strø** sand foran døren, når der er is.
sentence.en: We must sprinkle sand in front of the door when there is ice.

at studere.explanation: "At studere" means "to study". To say what someone is studying to become, use "at læse til" (literally, to read for): "Hun læser til læge" (She is studying to be a doctor).

related.en: a study, a course of study

sentence.da: Hun vil **studere** medicin på universitetet.
sentence.en: She wants to study medicine at the university.

at styre.explanation: "At styre" means "to control or steer". To say you run a company, say: "Han styrer firmaet" (He runs the company).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **styre** båden selv.
sentence.en: I can steer the boat myself.

at styrke.explanation: "At styrke" means "to strengthen". To say something made a friendship stronger, say: "Turen styrkede venskabet" (The trip strengthened the friendship).

sentence.da: Daglig motion kan **styrke** hjertet og musklerne.
sentence.en: Daily exercise can strengthen the heart and the muscles.

at styrte.explanation: "At styrte" means "to rush or crash". To say you hurry somewhere, use it with no "ned" (down): "Jeg styrtede hjem" (I rushed home). To say something falls or crashes, add "ned": "Flyet styrtede ned" (The plane crashed).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **styrte** ud af døren, når klokken ringer.
sentence.en: The children will rush out the door when the bell rings.

at stå.explanation: "At stå" means "to stand". To say where something upright is, say: "Flasken står på bordet" (The bottle is on the table). To say what is written somewhere, say: "Der står et navn på døren" (There is a name on the door).

sentence.da: Man kan **stå** eller sidde i bussen.
sentence.en: You can stand or sit on the bus.

at stå af.explanation: "At stå af" means "to get off". To say you leave a train, say: "Hun står af toget i Aarhus" (She gets off the train in Aarhus). For a bike, use "at stige af" (to get off): "Hun stiger af cyklen" (She gets off the bike).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **stå af** ved næste stop.
sentence.en: I will get off at the next stop.

at stå for.explanation: "At stå for" means "to be in charge of". To say you handle a job, say: "Jeg står for maden" (I am in charge of the food). To ask what an abbreviation means, use the same words: "Hvad står DSB for?" (What does DSB stand for?)

forms.en: I have been in charge of

sentence.da: Min bror vil **stå for** maden til festen.
sentence.en: My brother will be in charge of the food for the party.

at stå i kø.explanation: "At stå i kø" means "to stand in line". To say traffic is jammed, use "kø" (line) alone: "Der er kø på motorvejen" (There is a traffic jam on the highway).

sentence.da: Vi må **stå i kø** for billetter.
sentence.en: We have to stand in line for tickets.

at stå op.explanation: "At stå op" means "to get up", as in getting out of bed. It is built from "at stå" (to stand) and "op" (up). To say you stand up from a chair, use "at rejse sig" (to stand up): "Han rejser sig fra stolen" (He stands up from the chair).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **stå op** klokken syv.
sentence.en: I want to get up at seven.

at stå på ski.explanation: "At stå på ski" means "to ski". Literally, it is "to stand on skis". To say you water ski, use "vandski" (water ski) in place of "ski": "Jeg står på vandski" (I water ski).

sentence.da: Vi vil **stå på ski** i Norge.
sentence.en: We want to ski in Norway.

at støde på.explanation: "At støde på" means "to come across". To say you meet a person by chance, say: "Jeg stødte på min gamle lærer i byen" (I came across my old teacher in town). To say you face a difficulty, say: "Vi stødte på modstand" (We met resistance).

sentence.da: Vi kan **støde på** problemer, når vi bygger huset.
sentence.en: We may come across problems when we build the house.

at stønne.explanation: "At stønne" means "to groan". To name what you groan about, use "over" (about): "stønne over varmen" (to groan about the heat).

sentence.da: Man kan **stønne**, når man løfter noget meget tungt.
sentence.en: You can groan when you lift something very heavy.

at støtte.explanation: "At støtte" means "to support". To say you back a project, say: "Vi støtter projektet" (We support the project). To say you lean on something, add "sig til" (oneself on): "Han støttede sig til væggen" (He leaned on the wall).

sentence.da: Jeg vil altid **støtte** dig.
sentence.en: I will always support you.

at støve af.explanation: "At støve af" means "to dust". To say what you dust, put the things before "af" (off): "Jeg støver hylderne af" (I dust the shelves). To say you refresh an old skill, say: "støve sit fransk af" (to dust off your French).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **støve af** i stuen, når gæsterne kommer.
sentence.en: I will dust in the living room when the guests come.

at støvsuge.explanation: "At støvsuge" means "to vacuum". It is built from "støv" (dust) and "at suge" (to suck), and the machine is "en støvsuger" (a vacuum cleaner).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **støvsuge** stuen i dag.
sentence.en: I have to vacuum the living room today.

at suge.explanation: "At suge" means "to suck". To name what you suck on, use "på" (on): "Babyen suger på sutten" (The baby sucks on the pacifier). The noun "en støvsuger" (a vacuum cleaner) is built from "støv" (dust) and this verb.

sentence.da: Barnet kan **suge** saften op med et sugerør.
sentence.en: The child can suck the juice up with a straw.

at sukke.explanation: "At sukke" means "to sigh". To name what you sigh about, use "over" (about): "Hun sukker over vejret" (She sighs about the weather). The noun is "et suk" (a sigh).

sentence.da: Min bror kan **sukke** højt, når han keder sig.
sentence.en: My brother can sigh loudly when he is bored.

at sulte.explanation: "At sulte" means "to starve". To say you are simply hungry, use "sulten" (hungry) instead: "Jeg er sulten" (I am hungry).

sentence.da: Ingen skal **sulte**, når der er mad nok til alle.
sentence.en: Nobody should starve when there is enough food for everyone.

at summe.explanation: "At summe" means "to buzz". To say a place is full of life, say: "Byen summer af liv" (The city buzzes with life). To hum a tune, use "at nynne" (to hum): "Hun nynner en melodi" (She hums a tune).

sentence.da: Om sommeren kan man høre fluer **summe** i vinduet.
sentence.en: In summer you can hear flies buzz in the window.

at supplere.explanation: "At supplere" means "to supplement". To say two people each add what the other lacks, add "hinanden" (each other): "De supplerer hinanden" (They complement each other).

sentence.da: Du kan **supplere** din kost med frugt og grønt.
sentence.en: You can supplement your diet with fruit and vegetables.

at sutte.explanation: "At sutte" means "to suck". To name what you suck on, use "på" (on): "Babyen sutter på flasken" (The baby sucks on the bottle).

sentence.da: Barnet kan lide at **sutte** på tommelfingeren.
sentence.en: The child likes to suck on the thumb.
