at svare.explanation: "At svare" means "to answer". To answer a letter or a message, add "på" (on): "Hun svarer på brevet" (She answers the letter). To answer a person, name the person with no "på": "Jeg svarer ham" (I answer him).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **svare** på spørgsmålet.
sentence.en: I can answer the question.

at svare igen.explanation: "At svare igen" means "to talk back". The word "igen" means "again" in "gør det igen" (do it again), but here it means "back". To tell a child not to talk back, say: "Svar ikke igen!" (Do not talk back!)

sentence.da: Drengen må ikke **svare igen**, når mor skælder ud.
sentence.en: The boy must not talk back when mom scolds him.

at svare på.explanation: "At svare på" means "to answer or reply to". To reply to a message, put the message after "på" (on): "Jeg svarer på din besked" (I reply to your message).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **svare på** din mail i morgen.
sentence.en: I will reply to your email tomorrow.

at svede.explanation: "At svede" means "to sweat". To say someone is worried about something, add "over" (over): "Hun sveder over eksamen" (She is sweating over the exam).

sentence.da: Når det er varmt, kan jeg **svede** meget.
sentence.en: When it is hot, I can sweat a lot.

at svigte.explanation: "At svigte" means "to let down or fail". To say a friend let you down, say: "Han svigtede mig" (He let me down). To say a machine failed when you needed it, say: "Bremserne svigtede" (The brakes failed).

sentence.da: En ven må aldrig **svigte** en anden, når det går galt.
sentence.en: A friend must never let another down when things go wrong.

at svinge.explanation: "At svinge" means "to swing". To say something moves back and forth, say: "Pendulet svinger" (The pendulum swings). To say you turn a corner while driving or biking, say: "Jeg svinger til højre" (I turn right).

sentence.da: Du skal **svinge** til venstre ved lyskrydset.
sentence.en: You must turn left at the traffic light.

at svække.explanation: "At svække" means "to weaken". The opposite is "at styrke" (to strengthen): "Træning styrker kroppen" (Exercise strengthens the body).

sentence.da: Lange nætter uden søvn kan **svække** kroppen.
sentence.en: Long nights without sleep can weaken the body.

at sværge.explanation: "At sværge" means "to swear (promise)". To say you promise something is true, say: "Jeg sværger, at det er sandt" (I swear it is true). For bad language, use "at bande" (to curse): "Han bander, når han bliver vred" (He curses when he gets angry).

sentence.da: Vidnet skal **sværge** at sige sandheden i retten.
sentence.en: The witness must swear to tell the truth in court.

at svømme.explanation: "At svømme" means "to swim". To say you go for a dip in a lake or the sea, use "at bade" (to bathe): "Vi bader i søen" (We are going for a swim in the lake).

sentence.da: Fisk kan **svømme** i vandet.
sentence.en: Fish can swim in the water.

at sy.explanation: "At sy" means "to sew". To say a doctor closes a cut, use the same verb: "Lægen syede såret" (The doctor stitched the wound).

sentence.da: Min mor kan **sy** sine egne kjoler.
sentence.en: My mother can sew her own dresses.

at sygemelde sig.explanation: "At sygemelde sig" means "to call in sick". It is built from "syg" (sick) and "at melde" (to report). The small word "sig" (oneself) changes with who calls in sick: "vi sygemelder os" (we call in sick).

sentence.da: Hun må **sygemelde sig**, fordi hun har feber.
sentence.en: She has to call in sick because she has a fever.

at symbolisere.explanation: "At symbolisere" means "to symbolize". To say what a thing stands for, put the symbol first and the idea second: "Duen symboliserer fred" (The dove symbolizes peace).

sentence.da: Et rødt hjerte kan **symbolisere** kærlighed.
sentence.en: A red heart can symbolize love.

at synes.explanation: "At synes" means "to think (an opinion)". To say what your opinion is, say: "Jeg synes, det er godt" (I think it is good). To ask for someone's opinion, ask: "Hvad synes du?" (What do you think?) To say you guess a fact, use "at tro" (to believe): "Jeg tror, han kommer" (I think he is coming).

sentence.da: Hvad **synes** du om maden?
sentence.en: What do you think about the food?

at synge.explanation: "At synge" means "to sing". To say you join in a song, add "med" (with): "Jeg synger med" (I sing along).

sentence.da: Hun kan **synge** en smuk sang.
sentence.en: She can sing a beautiful song.

at synke.explanation: "At synke" means "to sink or swallow". To say a ship goes down, say: "Skibet synker" (The ship sinks). To say food or a pill goes down your throat, say: "Jeg kan ikke synke tabletten" (I cannot swallow the pill).

sentence.da: Den tunge sten vil **synke** i vandet.
sentence.en: The heavy stone will sink in the water.

at såre.explanation: "At såre" means "to hurt or wound". To say you hurt someone's feelings, say: "Hun sårede mig" (She hurt me). To say something hurts in the body, use "at gøre ondt" (to hurt): "Det gør ondt" (It hurts).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **såre** dig, men jeg må sige sandheden.
sentence.en: I do not want to hurt you, but I must tell the truth.

at sælge.explanation: "At sælge" means "to sell". To say something is for sale, use "til salg" (for sale): "Bilen er til salg" (The car is for sale).

sentence.da: Bageren vil **sælge** brød i butikken.
sentence.en: The baker wants to sell bread in the store.

at sænke.explanation: "At sænke" means "to lower". To say you speak more quietly, say: "Han sænker stemmen" (He lowers his voice). To say someone sinks a ship on purpose, say: "Piraterne sænker skibet" (The pirates sink the ship). When something goes down by itself, use "at synke" (to sink): "Skibet synker" (The ship sinks).

sentence.da: Butikken vil **sænke** priserne, fordi der er for få kunder.
sentence.en: The store wants to lower the prices because there are too few customers.

at sætte.explanation: "At sætte" means "to put or place". To say you put something on a shelf, say: "Jeg sætter bogen på hylden" (I put the book on the shelf). To tell someone to sit down, add "dig" (yourself): "Sæt dig" (Sit down). To say where you already are sitting, use "at sidde" (to sit): "Jeg sidder på stolen" (I sit on the chair).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sætte** koppen på bordet.
sentence.en: I want to put the cup on the table.

at sætte i gang.explanation: "At sætte i gang" means "to start or launch". To say you launch a project, say: "Vi sætter projektet i gang" (We are launching the project). When something starts without anyone starting it, use "at komme i gang" (to get going): "Projektet kommer i gang" (The project gets going).

sentence.da: Når I er klar, vil jeg **sætte i gang**.
sentence.en: When you are ready, I will get things started.

at sætte ind.explanation: "At sætte ind" means "to put in or deposit". To say you put money in the bank, say: "Jeg sætter pengene ind på kontoen" (I put the money into the account). To say you start using more of something, say: "Vi sætter flere busser ind" (We are putting more buses into service).

sentence.da: Jeg går i banken for at **sætte ind**.
sentence.en: I am going to the bank to make a deposit.

at sætte pris på.explanation: "At sætte pris på" means "to appreciate". Literally, it is "to put a price on". To say you appreciate something a lot, put "stor" (big) before "pris": "Jeg sætter stor pris på det" (I really appreciate it).

sentence.da: Man skal **sætte pris på** sine venner.
sentence.en: You should appreciate your friends.

at sætte på.explanation: "At sætte på" means "to put on". To say you start music or a pot of coffee, say: "Jeg sætter musik på" (I put some music on). For clothes, use "at tage på" (to put on): "Jeg tager jakken på" (I put on the jacket).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sætte på** noget kaffe, før gæsterne kommer.
sentence.en: I will put on some coffee before the guests come.

at sætte sig.explanation: "At sætte sig" means "to sit down". To say you take a seat, say: "Jeg sætter mig i sofaen" (I sit down on the sofa). To say where you already are sitting, use "at sidde" (to sit): "Jeg sidder i sofaen" (I am sitting on the sofa).

related.en: a seat (the part you sit on)

sentence.da: Han vil **sætte sig** på stolen.
sentence.en: He wants to sit down on the chair.

at søge.explanation: "At søge" means "to search or apply". To say you apply for a job, say: "Jeg søger et job" (I am applying for a job). To say you search for something, add "efter" (for): "Jeg søger efter mine nøgler" (I am searching for my keys).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **søge** et nyt job i København.
sentence.en: I want to apply for a new job in Copenhagen.

at søge efter.explanation: "At søge efter" means "to search for". To say you apply for a job, leave out "efter" (for) and use "at søge" (to apply): "Hun søger et job" (She is applying for a job).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **søge efter** en billig lejlighed.
sentence.en: I want to search for a cheap apartment.

at søge ind på.explanation: "At søge ind på" means "to apply to (a school)". To say you apply for a job, use "at søge" (to apply) without "ind på": "Hun søger et job" (She is applying for a job).

sentence.da: Min søster vil **søge ind på** universitetet i år.
sentence.en: My sister wants to apply to the university this year.

at søge job.explanation: "At søge job" means "to apply for a job". To say you are looking for work, say: "Jeg søger job som lærer" (I am looking for a job as a teacher). To say you apply for one position, use "at søge en stilling" (to apply for a position): "Han søger en stilling i banken" (He is applying for a position at the bank).

forms.en: I have applied for a job

sentence.da: Jeg vil **søge job** i en bank.
sentence.en: I want to apply for a job at a bank.

at søge om.explanation: "At søge om" means "to apply for". To say you ask an office for something, put the thing after "om" (for): "søge om tilladelse" (apply for a permit). To say you apply for a job, use "at søge" (to apply) without "om": "Hun søger et job" (She is applying for a job).

sentence.da: Han skal **søge om** et visum i dag.
sentence.en: He has to apply for a visa today.

at sørge for.explanation: "At sørge for" means "to make sure or take care of". To say you handle something, say: "Jeg sørger for maden" (I take care of the food). To tell someone to make sure of something, say: "Sørg for at låse døren" (Make sure you lock the door).

forms.en: to make sure / take care of
I make sure / take care of
I made sure / took care of
I have made sure / taken care of

sentence.da: Jeg skal **sørge for** børnene i aften.
sentence.en: I'll take care of the children tonight.

en sadel.explanation: "En sadel" means "a saddle". To talk about the seat of a bike, use the same word: "Sadlen på min cykel er for høj" (The seat on my bike is too high).

sentence.da: Rytteren sidder i en **sadel** på hestens ryg.
sentence.en: The rider sits in a saddle on the horse's back.

en sag.explanation: "En sag" means "a matter or case". To say something is a separate issue, say: "Det er en anden sag" (That is a different matter). To say a lawyer works on a legal case, say: "Advokaten arbejder på en sag" (The lawyer is working on a case).

sentence.da: Politiet arbejder på en vigtig **sag**.
sentence.en: The police are working on an important case.

en sagsbehandler.explanation: "En sagsbehandler" means "a caseworker". It is built from "en sag" (a case) and "at behandle" (to handle).

sentence.da: Min **sagsbehandler** ringer, når hun har læst min ansøgning.
sentence.en: My caseworker will call when she has read my application.

en saks.explanation: "En saks" means "a pair of scissors". To ask to borrow one pair, say: "Kan jeg låne din saks?" (Can I borrow your scissors?)

sentence.da: Jeg klipper papir med en **saks**.
sentence.en: I cut paper with a pair of scissors.

en sal.explanation: "En sal" means "a hall", as in a large room for events. For the hallway of a home, use "en gang" (a hallway): "Skoene står i gangen" (The shoes are in the hallway).

sentence.da: Koncerten foregår i den store **sal**.
sentence.en: The concert takes place in the big hall.

en salamander.explanation: "En salamander" means "a salamander". To say what its skin is like, say: "En salamander har fugtig hud" (A salamander has moist skin). Do not mix it up with "et firben" (a lizard): "Firbenet har skæl" (The lizard has scales).

sentence.da: Man finder ofte en **salamander** under en sten ved vandet.
sentence.en: You often find a salamander under a rock by the water.

en salat.explanation: "En salat" means "a salad or lettuce". To talk about a dish, say: "Jeg spiser en salat til frokost" (I eat a salad for lunch). To talk about the plant from the shop, use "en hovedsalat" (a head of lettuce): "Jeg køber en hovedsalat" (I buy a head of lettuce).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **salat** med tomat og agurk.
sentence.en: I eat a salad with tomato and cucumber.

en saltbøsse.explanation: "En saltbøsse" means "a salt shaker". To ask for it at the table, say: "Kan du række mig saltbøssen?" (Can you pass me the salt shaker?)

sentence.da: Jeg ryster salt på maden fra en **saltbøsse**.
sentence.en: I shake salt onto the food from a salt shaker.

en salve.explanation: "En salve" means "an ointment". To say you have one at home, say: "Jeg har en salve i skabet" (I have an ointment in the cupboard). The same word also means a volley: "en salve skud" (a volley of shots).

sentence.da: Lægen gav mig en **salve** til mit udslæt.
sentence.en: The doctor gave me an ointment for my rash.

en samlever.explanation: "En samlever" means "a live-in partner". It is built from "sammen" (together) and "at leve" (to live).

sentence.da: Min **samlever** og jeg bor sammen, men vi er ikke gift.
sentence.en: My partner and I live together, but we are not married.

en samling.explanation: "En samling" means "a collection". To talk about circle time at kindergarten, use "samling" with no "en": "Vi har samling klokken ti" (We have circle time at ten).

sentence.da: Min onkel har en stor **samling** af gamle mønter.
sentence.en: My uncle has a big collection of old coins.

en sammenhæng.explanation: "En sammenhæng" means "a connection". To say "in that context", use the phrase "i den sammenhæng": "I den sammenhæng er det vigtigt" (In that context it is important).

sentence.da: Der er en **sammenhæng** mellem rygning og lungesygdom.
sentence.en: There is a link between smoking and lung disease.

en sammenkomst.explanation: "En sammenkomst" means "a get-together". It is built from "sammen" (together) and "at komme" (to come). For a party, use "en fest" (a party): "Vi holder fest i aften" (We are having a party tonight).

sentence.da: Vi drak kaffe og spiste kage til en **sammenkomst** hos mormor.
sentence.en: We drank coffee and ate cake at a get-together at Grandma's.

en sammenligning.explanation: "En sammenligning" means "a comparison". To name the two things you compare, use "mellem" (between): "en sammenligning mellem to byer" (a comparison between two cities).

sentence.da: I **sammenligning** med Sverige er Danmark et lille land.
sentence.en: In comparison with Sweden, Denmark is a small country.

en sammensværgelse.explanation: "En sammensværgelse" means "a conspiracy". It is built from "sammen" (together) and "at sværge" (to swear).

sentence.da: Politiet afslørede en **sammensværgelse** mod kongen.
sentence.en: The police uncovered a conspiracy against the king.

en samtale.explanation: "En samtale" means "a conversation". It is built from "sam-" (together) and "en tale" (a talk). To say phone call, put "telefon" (phone) in front: "en telefonsamtale" (a phone call).

sentence.da: To mennesker har en **samtale**, når de taler sammen.
sentence.en: Two people have a conversation when they talk together.

en samtaleøvelse.explanation: "En samtaleøvelse" means "a conversation exercise". It is built from "samtale" (conversation) and "en øvelse" (an exercise).

sentence.da: I en **samtaleøvelse** taler vi sammen to og to.
sentence.en: In a conversation exercise, we talk together in pairs.

en samvittighed.explanation: "En samvittighed" means "a conscience". To say you have done nothing wrong, say: "Jeg har en ren samvittighed" (I have a clear conscience).

sentence.da: Hun fik dårlig **samvittighed** efter løgnen.
sentence.en: She got a guilty conscience after the lie.

en sandal.explanation: "En sandal" means "a sandal". To say a pair of sandals, use "et par" (a pair of): "et par sandaler" (a pair of sandals).

sentence.da: En **sandal** er en åben sko til sommer.
sentence.en: A sandal is an open shoe for summer.

en sandhed.explanation: "En sandhed" means "a truth". It is built from "sand" (true) and "-hed", an ending that makes nouns. To say something is true, use the form "sandt": "Det er sandt" (That is true).

sentence.da: Der er en **sandhed** i det, han siger.
sentence.en: There is a truth in what he says.

en sandkasse.explanation: "En sandkasse" means "a sandbox". It is built from "sand" (sand) and "en kasse" (a box). To say children play in it, use "i" (in): "Børnene leger i sandkassen" (The children play in the sandbox).

sentence.da: Barnet graver med en spade i en **sandkasse**.
sentence.en: The child digs with a shovel in a sandbox.

en sandstrand.explanation: "En sandstrand" means "a sandy beach". It is built from "sand" (sand) and "en strand" (a beach). To say a beach has stones instead of sand, use "en stenstrand" (a pebble beach): "Det er en stenstrand" (It is a pebble beach).

sentence.da: Børnene leger på den lange **sandstrand**.
sentence.en: The children play on the long sandy beach.

en sandsynlighed.explanation: "En sandsynlighed" means "a probability". It is built from "sandsynlig" (probable) and "-hed", an ending that makes nouns. To say something will very probably happen, use "med stor sandsynlighed" (with high probability): "Han kommer med stor sandsynlighed" (He will very probably come).

sentence.da: Der er stor **sandsynlighed** for sne i weekenden.
sentence.en: There is a high probability of snow this weekend.

en sandwich.explanation: "En sandwich" means "a sandwich". To talk about the Danish open sandwich, use "smørrebrød" (open sandwich), which has no top slice of bread: "Vi spiser smørrebrød til frokost" (We eat open sandwiches for lunch).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **sandwich** med ost og skinke.
sentence.en: I eat a sandwich with cheese and ham.

en sang.explanation: "En sang" means "a song". The word "sang" also starts "en sangtekst" (song lyrics) and "en sanger" (a singer).

sentence.da: Hun synger en smuk **sang** for os.
sentence.en: She sings a beautiful song for us.

en sangtekst.explanation: "En sangtekst" means "a song lyric". It is built from "sang" (song) and "en tekst" (a text). To say the lyrics of one particular song, use "til" (to): "teksten til sangen" (the lyrics to the song).

sentence.da: Ordene i en **sangtekst** rimer ofte på hinanden.
sentence.en: The words in a song lyric often rhyme with each other.

en sanktion.explanation: "En sanktion" means "a sanction". To talk about the measures one country takes against another country, use the plural with "mod" (against): "sanktioner mod Rusland" (sanctions against Russia).

sentence.da: Landet får en hård **sanktion**, hvis det bryder reglerne.
sentence.en: The country gets a harsh sanction if it breaks the rules.

en sans.explanation: "En sans" means "a sense", as in sight, hearing or touch. To say someone has a feel for something, use "sans for" (a sense of): "sans for humor" (a sense of humor).

sentence.da: Synet er en **sans**, og det er hørelsen også.
sentence.en: Sight is a sense, and hearing is too.

en satellit.explanation: "En satellit" means "a satellite". To say it circles the Earth, use "i kredsløb" (in orbit): "Satellitten er i kredsløb om Jorden" (The satellite is in orbit around the Earth). The spelling has two "l"s and ends in "-it", and the "t" is doubled before an ending, as in "satellitter".

sentence.da: En **satellit** i rummet sender billeder af vejret til Jorden.
sentence.en: A satellite in space sends pictures of the weather to Earth.

en sauna.explanation: "En sauna" means "a sauna". The word comes from Finnish, and Danish spells it the same way.

sentence.da: Efter træning sidder vi i **sauna** og sveder.
sentence.en: After working out, we sit in the sauna and sweat.

en scanning.explanation: "En scanning" means "a scan". It comes from the verb "at scanne" (to scan). To say you are going for a scan, use "til" (to): "Jeg skal til scanning" (I am going for a scan).

sentence.da: Lægen vil se indersiden af kroppen med en **scanning**.
sentence.en: The doctor wants to see the inside of the body with a scan.

en scene.explanation: "En scene" means "a stage or scene". To say someone is on a theater stage, use "på scenen" (on the stage): "Sangeren står på scenen" (The singer is standing on the stage). To talk about a part of a film or play, use "scene" for that part too: "Scenen i filmen er sjov" (The scene in the movie is funny).

sentence.da: Bandet spiller på en stor **scene** i aften.
sentence.en: The band is playing on a big stage tonight.

en scooter.explanation: "En scooter" means "a scooter", the kind with a motor. To talk about a kick scooter that you stand on, use "et løbehjul" (literally "a running wheel"): "Barnet kører på løbehjul" (The child rides a kick scooter).

sentence.da: Hun kører på **scooter** gennem byen.
sentence.en: She rides a scooter through town.

en score.explanation: "En score" means "a score", as in a game. To say a player puts the ball in the goal, use the verb "at score" (to score): "Han scorer et mål" (He scores a goal).

sentence.da: Min **score** i spillet er meget høj.
sentence.en: My score in the game is very high.

en seddel.explanation: "En seddel" means "a note", as in a message on paper. To talk about paper money, use "seddel" at the end of a word: "en hundredkroneseddel" (a 100-krone bill).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver en **seddel** og lægger den på døren.
sentence.en: I write a note and put it on the door.

en seer.explanation: "En seer" means "a viewer". It comes from the verb "at se" (to see). To name a person who watches TV, put "tv" in front: "en tv-seer" (a TV viewer).

sentence.da: En **seer** ser programmet hjemme i sin sofa.
sentence.en: A viewer watches the show at home on their couch.

en sejlbåd.explanation: "En sejlbåd" means "a sailboat". It is built from "et sejl" (a sail) and "en båd" (a boat). To say you go on a sailing trip, use "en sejltur" (a sailing trip): "Vi tager på sejltur" (We go on a sailing trip).

sentence.da: Når der er vind, sejler min onkel i sin **sejlbåd**.
sentence.en: When there is wind, my uncle sails in his sailboat.

en sejr.explanation: "En sejr" means "a victory". It is also a verb: to say a team wins, use "at sejre" (to win): "Holdet sejrer i dag" (The team wins today).

sentence.da: Vi fejrer vores store **sejr** med kage.
sentence.en: We celebrate our big victory with cake.

en sekretær.explanation: "En sekretær" means "a secretary". To say what job someone has, leave out the article: "Hun er sekretær" (She is a secretary). The ending is spelled "-ær" with "æ", not with an "e" as in English.

sentence.da: Vores **sekretær** svarer i telefonen.
sentence.en: Our secretary answers the phone.

en sektion.explanation: "En sektion" means "a section". It is spelled with "k", where English has "c": "sektionen" (the section).

sentence.da: Børnebøgerne står i en anden **sektion**.
sentence.en: The children's books are in another section.

en sektor.explanation: "En sektor" means "a sector". To talk about the part of the economy run by companies, use "den private sektor" (the private sector). It is spelled with "k", where English has "c".

sentence.da: Skoler og hospitaler hører til den offentlige **sektor**.
sentence.en: Schools and hospitals belong to the public sector.

en sele.explanation: "En sele" means "a seat belt or harness". To tell someone to put a seat belt on, use "at tage på" (to put on): "Tag selen på" (Put the seat belt on). In a car you can also say "en sikkerhedssele" (a safety belt).

sentence.da: Børnene skal have **sele** på i bilen.
sentence.en: The children must wear seat belts in the car.

en selvbetjeningskasse.explanation: "En selvbetjeningskasse" means "a self-checkout". It is built from "selvbetjening" (self-service) and "en kasse" (a checkout). The first part "selv" means "self", as in "selvbetjening".

sentence.da: Ved en **selvbetjeningskasse** scanner du selv varerne og betaler.
sentence.en: At a self-checkout you scan the goods yourself and pay.

en senator.explanation: "En senator" means "a senator". Denmark has no senate. Its parliament is "Folketinget" (the Folketing), and its members are not called senators.

sentence.da: Hun er **senator** for Texas og arbejder i Washington.
sentence.en: She is a senator for Texas and works in Washington.

en sending.explanation: "En sending" means "a shipment or broadcast". It comes from the verb "at sende" (to send). To talk about goods on the way to someone, use "sending" for the load: "Sendingen kommer i morgen" (The shipment arrives tomorrow). To talk about a radio or TV program, use it for the program: "Sendingen starter klokken otte" (The broadcast starts at eight o'clock).

sentence.da: Vi venter på en **sending** med varer fra Kina.
sentence.en: We are waiting for a shipment of goods from China.

en sene.explanation: "En sene" means "a tendon". Do not mix it up with "et ledbånd" (a ligament), which joins one bone to another bone: "Hun har skadet et ledbånd" (She has injured a ligament).

sentence.da: Den tykkeste **sene** i kroppen sidder lige over hælen.
sentence.en: The thickest tendon in the body is right above the heel.

en seng.explanation: "En seng" means "a bed". To say you make the bed in the morning, use "at rede" (to make): "Jeg reder sengen hver morgen" (I make the bed every morning).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og går i **seng**.
sentence.en: I am tired and go to bed.

en sengegavl.explanation: "En sengegavl" means "a headboard". It is built from "en seng" (a bed) and "en gavl" (an end wall). "En gavl" also means the end wall of a house: "gavlen på huset" (the end wall of the house).

sentence.da: Jeg sidder i sengen og læner mig mod min **sengegavl**.
sentence.en: I sit in bed and lean against my headboard.

en sergent.explanation: "En sergent" means "a sergeant". The English spelling "sergeant" has an "a", but the Danish "sergent" does not, and "sergenten" (the sergeant) keeps that spelling.

sentence.da: Som **sergent** leder han en lille gruppe i hæren.
sentence.en: As a sergeant he leads a small group in the army.

en serie.explanation: "En serie" means "a series". To say several things happen one after another, put the thing after "en serie": "en serie fejl" (a series of mistakes).

sentence.da: Vi ser en god **serie** hver aften.
sentence.en: We watch a good series every evening.

en seriemorder.explanation: "En seriemorder" means "a serial killer". It is built from "serie" (series) and "en morder" (a murderer). The same "morder" ends "en massemorder" (a mass murderer).

sentence.da: Filmen handler om en **seriemorder**, og politiet jagter ham.
sentence.en: The film is about a serial killer, and the police are hunting him.

en server.explanation: "En server" means "a server", as in a computer. In a restaurant, a waiter is "en tjener" instead: "Tjeneren bringer maden" (The waiter brings the food).

sentence.da: Siden virker ikke, når vores **server** er nede.
sentence.en: The site does not work when our server is down.

en service.explanation: "En service" means "a service", as in help for customers. To say a car goes in for its check, use "til service" (for service): "Bilen skal til service" (The car has to go in for service). To say a favor, use "en tjeneste" (a favor): "Kan du gøre mig en tjeneste?" (Can you do me a favor?).

sentence.da: Vi fik rigtig god **service** på hotellet.
sentence.en: We got really good service at the hotel.

en serviet.explanation: "En serviet" means "a napkin". To ask for one at the table, say: "Må jeg få en serviet?" (May I have a napkin?).

sentence.da: Der ligger en **serviet** ved gaflen.
sentence.en: There is a napkin by the fork.

en servitrice.explanation: "En servitrice" means "a waitress". To talk about a man who works in a restaurant, use "en tjener" (a waiter): "Tjeneren kommer med regningen" (The waiter brings the bill).

sentence.da: En **servitrice** tager imod bestillinger og serverer maden.
sentence.en: A waitress takes orders and serves the food.

en seværdighed.explanation: "En seværdighed" means "an attraction". It is built from "seværdig" (worth seeing) and "-hed", an ending that makes nouns. To say a castle is worth seeing, use "seværdigt": "Slottet er seværdigt" (The castle is worth seeing).

sentence.da: Turisterne besøger hver **seværdighed** i byen.
sentence.en: The tourists visit every attraction in the city.

en sfo.explanation: "En SFO" means "an after-school club". The letters stand for "skolefritidsordning" (school after-hours scheme). In Denmark it is for the youngest schoolchildren, after lessons.

sentence.da: Min søn er i **SFO**, når skolen er slut.
sentence.en: My son is in the after-school club when school is over.

en shelter.explanation: "En shelter" means "a shelter". In Denmark it is a simple wooden hut in nature where hikers can sleep. To say you stay the night in one, use "at overnatte" (to stay the night): "Vi overnatter i en shelter" (We stay the night in a shelter).

sentence.da: En **shelter** har tag og tre vægge, men ingen dør.
sentence.en: A shelter has a roof and three walls, but no door.

en sherif.explanation: "En sherif" means "a sheriff". English speakers would spell it with two "f": the Danish "sherif" has one, and two only before an ending, as in "sheriffen" (the sheriff). Denmark has no sheriffs, and the police are "politiet" (the police).

sentence.da: Hun er **sherif** og holder ro og orden i den lille by.
sentence.en: She is the sheriff and keeps order in the small town.

en si.explanation: "En si" means "a sieve". To sift flour, use the verb "at sigte" (to sift): "Sigt melet" (Sift the flour).

sentence.da: Jeg hælder te gennem en **si**.
sentence.en: I pour tea through a strainer.

en side.explanation: "En side" means "a page or side". To talk about two sides of an issue, use "på den ene side" (on the one hand) and "på den anden side" (on the other hand): "På den ene side er det dyrt, men på den anden side er det godt" (On the one hand it is expensive, but on the other hand it is good).

sentence.da: Åbn bogen på **side** ti.
sentence.en: Open the book on page ten.

en sidebemærkning.explanation: "En sidebemærkning" means "a side note". It is built from "side" (side) and "en bemærkning" (a remark). To say a point was only an extra, say: "Det var bare en sidebemærkning" (That was just a side note).

sentence.da: Hun kom med en **sidebemærkning** midt i foredraget.
sentence.en: She added a side note in the middle of the talk.

en sikkerhedskontrol.explanation: "En sikkerhedskontrol" means "a security check". It is built from "sikkerhed" (security) and "kontrol" (check). English speakers write "control" with two "l", but Danish "kontrol" has one.

sentence.da: Alle skal igennem en **sikkerhedskontrol** i lufthavnen.
sentence.en: Everyone has to go through a security check at the airport.

en sikkerhedskopi.explanation: "En sikkerhedskopi" means "a backup". It is built from "sikkerhed" (security) and "en kopi" (a copy). To say you make a backup, use "at tage" (to take): "Jeg tager en sikkerhedskopi" (I make a backup).

sentence.da: Når telefonen går i stykker, har jeg en **sikkerhedskopi**.
sentence.en: When the phone breaks, I have a backup.

en sikkerhedssele.explanation: "En sikkerhedssele" means "a seatbelt". It is built from "sikkerhed" (safety) and "en sele" (a harness). To say you must wear it, use "have ... på" (literally, "have ... on"): "Du skal have sikkerhedsselen på" (You must wear your seatbelt).

sentence.da: En **sikkerhedssele** beskytter dig i bilen.
sentence.en: A seatbelt protects you in the car.

en sikring.explanation: "En sikring" means "a fuse". It is built on the verb "at sikre" (to secure). To say you replace a fuse, use "at skifte" (to change): "Jeg skifter sikringen" (I replace the fuse).

sentence.da: Lyset gik ud, fordi en **sikring** var sprunget.
sentence.en: The light went out because a fuse had blown.

en sikringsboks.explanation: "En sikringsboks" means "a fuse box". It is built from "en sikring" (a fuse) and "en boks" (a box).

sentence.da: Lyset gik ud, og nu leder jeg efter vores **sikringsboks**.
sentence.en: The light went out, and now I am looking for our fuse box.

en situation.explanation: "En situation" means "a situation". To ask what someone does in a given case, use "i den situation" (in that situation): "Hvad gør du i den situation?" (What do you do in that situation?).

sentence.da: Det er en svær **situation** for alle.
sentence.en: It is a hard situation for everyone.

en sjæl.explanation: "En sjæl" means "a soul". To say there was nobody somewhere, use "ikke en sjæl" (not a soul): "Der var ikke en sjæl i byen" (There was not a soul in town).

sentence.da: Mange tror på, at man har en **sjæl**.
sentence.en: Many believe that you have a soul.

en skabning.explanation: "En skabning" means "a creature". It comes from the verb "at skabe" (to create).

sentence.da: I eventyret møder drengen en mærkelig **skabning** i skoven.
sentence.en: In the fairy tale the boy meets a strange creature in the forest.

en skade.explanation: "En skade" means "an injury or damage". To say a part of the body is hurt, use "skade" for the injury: "Hun har en skade i foden" (She has an injury in her foot). To say damage was done, use "at gøre skade" (to do damage): "Stormen gjorde stor skade" (The storm did great damage).

sentence.da: Han fik en **skade** i knæet under kampen.
sentence.en: He got an injury to his knee during the game.

en skadestue.explanation: "En skadestue" means "an ER". It is built from "en skade" (an injury) and "en stue" (a room). To say where you are, use "på" (literally "on"): "Jeg er på skadestuen" (I am at the ER).

sentence.da: Læger hjælper skadede folk på en **skadestue**.
sentence.en: Doctors help injured people in an ER.

en skala.explanation: "En skala" means "a scale", as in a range from low to high. For a scale you weigh yourself on, use "en badevægt" (a bathroom scale): "Jeg står på badevægten" (I am standing on the bathroom scale).

sentence.da: Hvor ondt gør det på en **skala** fra et til ti?
sentence.en: How much does it hurt on a scale from one to ten?

en skammel.explanation: "En skammel" means "a stool". The "e" before the last "l" drops when an ending is added: "skamlen" (the stool) and "skamler" (stools).

sentence.da: Jeg står på en **skammel** og når hylden.
sentence.en: I stand on a stool and reach the shelf.

en skandale.explanation: "En skandale" means "a scandal". To say something is outrageous, say "Det er en skandale" (It is a scandal): "Det er en skandale, at bussen er forsinket!" (It is a scandal that the bus is late!).

sentence.da: Avisen skrev om en stor **skandale** i regeringen.
sentence.en: The newspaper wrote about a big scandal in the government.

en skat.explanation: "En skat" means "a tax". To say a treasure, use "skat" too: "en skjult skat" (a hidden treasure). To address a loved one, say "skat" (sweetheart): "Hej skat" (Hi, sweetheart).

sentence.da: Vi betaler meget i **skat** i Danmark.
sentence.en: We pay a lot in tax in Denmark.

en skattejagt.explanation: "En skattejagt" means "a treasure hunt". It is built from "skat" (treasure) and "en jagt" (a hunt). "Skat" also means "tax", as in "Jeg betaler skat" (I pay tax). To say you take part, use "at gå på" (to go on): "Vi går på skattejagt" (We go on a treasure hunt).

sentence.da: På en **skattejagt** følger man spor for at finde en skjult skat.
sentence.en: On a treasure hunt you follow trails to find a hidden treasure.

en skatteyder.explanation: "En skatteyder" means "a taxpayer". It is built from "skat" (tax). To say something is paid with public money, use "skatteyderne" (the taxpayers): "Skatteyderne betaler for broen" (The taxpayers pay for the bridge).

sentence.da: Som **skatteyder** betaler man en del af sin løn til staten.
sentence.en: As a taxpayer you pay part of your salary to the state.

en ske.explanation: "En ske" means "a spoon". It is the base of "en teske" (a teaspoon) and "en spiseske" (a tablespoon, literally "an eating spoon").

sentence.da: Jeg spiser suppen med en **ske**.
sentence.en: I eat the soup with a spoon.

en ski.explanation: "En ski" means "a ski". The plural is "ski" or "skier": "Jeg har to nye ski" (I have two new skis). To say you go skiing, use "at gå på ski" (literally "to go on skis"): "Vi går på ski" (We go skiing).

sentence.da: Min ene **ski** er gået i stykker.
sentence.en: One of my skis has broken.

en skik.explanation: "En skik" means "a custom". To say that every country has its own customs, use the saying "Andre lande, andre skikke" (Other countries, other customs).

sentence.da: Det er en gammel **skik** at tænde lys i vinduet i december.
sentence.en: It is an old custom to light candles in the window in December.

en skildpadde.explanation: "En skildpadde" means "a turtle". Danish uses it for a tortoise too. To say a tortoise that lives on land, add "land" in front: "en landskildpadde" (a tortoise).

sentence.da: En **skildpadde** går langsomt, men den bliver gammel.
sentence.en: A turtle walks slowly, but it gets old.

en skildring.explanation: "En skildring" means "a depiction". It comes from the verb "at skildre" (to depict). To name what is depicted, use "af" (of): "en skildring af byen" (a depiction of the city).

sentence.da: Romanen er en levende **skildring** af livet på landet.
sentence.en: The novel is a lively depiction of life in the countryside.

en skilsmisse.explanation: "En skilsmisse" means "a divorce". To say someone is divorced, use "skilt" (divorced): "Hun er skilt" (She is divorced).

sentence.da: Deres **skilsmisse** var svær for børnene.
sentence.en: Their divorce was hard on the children.

en skinke.explanation: "En skinke" means "a ham". To say how much ham, use "et stykke" (a piece of): "et stykke skinke" (a piece of ham).

sentence.da: **Skinke** er kød fra en gris.
sentence.en: Ham is meat from a pig.

en skinne.explanation: "En skinne" means "a splint or rail". To talk about a splint that holds a broken bone still, use "skinne": "Han har en skinne på armen" (He has a splint on his arm). To talk about a train track, use the plural for the rails: "Toget kører på skinner" (The train runs on rails).

sentence.da: Lægen satte en **skinne** på hendes brækkede finger.
sentence.en: The doctor put a splint on her broken finger.

en skive.explanation: "En skive" means "a slice". To say what is sliced, put it after "skive": "en skive ost" (a slice of cheese). For cake, you can say "et stykke kage" (a piece of cake).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer en **skive** af brødet.
sentence.en: I cut a slice off the bread.

en skjorte.explanation: "En skjorte" means "a shirt". English speakers would write "sh", but Danish writes "skj" at the start of "skjorte".

sentence.da: En **skjorte** har knapper og lange ærmer.
sentence.en: A shirt has buttons and long sleeves.

en sko.explanation: "En sko" means "a shoe". The plural "sko" is spelled like the single word, so a number shows how many: "to sko" (two shoes).

sentence.da: Jeg har kun en **sko** på.
sentence.en: I only have one shoe on.

en skobutik.explanation: "En skobutik" means "a shoe store". It is built from "sko" (shoes) and "en butik" (a shop). The same "butik" is in "en bogbutik" (a bookstore).

sentence.da: Jeg køber nye sko i en **skobutik**.
sentence.en: I buy new shoes in a shoe store.

en skole.explanation: "En skole" means "a school". To say a child is at the school building, use "på" (at): "Barnet er på skolen" (The child is at school).

sentence.da: Min datter går i **skole** hver dag.
sentence.en: My daughter goes to school every day.

en skole-hjem-samtale.explanation: "En skole-hjem-samtale" means "a parent-teacher conference". It is built from "skole" (school), "hjem" (home) and "en samtale" (a conversation). To say you are going to one, use "til" (to): "Vi skal til skole-hjem-samtale" (We are going to a parent-teacher conference).

sentence.da: Vi taler med læreren om vores søn til en **skole-hjem-samtale**.
sentence.en: We talk with the teacher about our son at a parent-teacher conference.

en skoledag.explanation: "En skoledag" means "a school day". It is built from "skole" (school) and "en dag" (a day). To say a day with no school, use "en fridag" (a day off): "I morgen er det en fridag" (Tomorrow is a day off).

sentence.da: Efter en lang **skoledag** er børnene trætte og sultne.
sentence.en: After a long school day the children are tired and hungry.

en skolegård.explanation: "En skolegård" means "a schoolyard". It is built from "skole" (school) and "en gård" (a yard). "En gård" also means a farm: "Vi besøger en gård med køer" (We visit a farm with cows).

sentence.da: Børnene leger i en stor **skolegård** mellem timerne.
sentence.en: The children play in a big schoolyard between classes.

en skoletaske.explanation: "En skoletaske" means "a school bag". It is built from "skole" (school) and "en taske" (a bag). The same "taske" is in "en håndtaske" (a handbag).

sentence.da: Børnene har bøger og madpakke i deres **skoletaske**.
sentence.en: The kids have books and a packed lunch in their school bag.

en skoletur.explanation: "En skoletur" means "a school trip". It is built from "en skole" (a school) and "en tur" (a trip). The same "tur" is in "en cykeltur" (a bike ride).

sentence.da: Hele klassen skal på **skoletur** til Berlin.
sentence.en: The whole class is going on a school trip to Berlin.

en skomager.explanation: "En skomager" means "a shoemaker or cobbler". The ending "-mager" means "maker", as in "en urmager" (a watchmaker).

sentence.da: Min **skomager** kan reparere hælen på mine sko.
sentence.en: My shoemaker can fix the heel on my shoes.

en skorsten.explanation: "En skorsten" means "a chimney". The person who cleans a chimney is "en skorstensfejer" (a chimney sweep): "Skorstensfejeren kommer i dag" (The chimney sweep is coming today).

sentence.da: Der kommer røg op af vores **skorsten**.
sentence.en: Smoke is coming up out of our chimney.

en skorstensfejer.explanation: "En skorstensfejer" means "a chimney sweep". It is built from "en skorsten" (a chimney) and "at feje" (to sweep). To say you sweep a floor, use the same verb: "Jeg fejer gulvet" (I sweep the floor).

sentence.da: En **skorstensfejer** tjekker skorstenen i vores hus hvert år.
sentence.en: A chimney sweep checks the chimney in our house every year.

en skostørrelse.explanation: "En skostørrelse" means "a shoe size". In Denmark shoe sizes are European sizes, such as 40. To say your size, use "at bruge" (to use): "Jeg bruger størrelse 40" (I wear a size 40).

sentence.da: Min **skostørrelse** er 40, men skoene er for små.
sentence.en: My shoe size is 40, but the shoes are too small.

en skov.explanation: "En skov" means "a forest". To say you go for a walk in the woods, use "en skovtur" (a forest trip): "Vi tager på skovtur" (We go on a forest trip).

sentence.da: Der er mange høje træer i en **skov**.
sentence.en: There are many tall trees in a forest.

en skovbrand.explanation: "En skovbrand" means "a wildfire". It is built from "en skov" (a forest) and "en brand" (a fire).

sentence.da: En **skovbrand** kan sprede sig hurtigt, når det er tørt.
sentence.en: A wildfire can spread quickly when it is dry.

en skovl.explanation: "En skovl" means "a shovel". For a tool used to dig into the ground, use "en spade" (a spade): "Han graver et hul med en spade" (He digs a hole with a spade).

sentence.da: Han fjerner sneen med en **skovl**.
sentence.en: He clears the snow with a shovel.

en skovsti.explanation: "En skovsti" means "a forest path". It is built from "skov" (forest) and "en sti" (a path). The same "sti" is in "en cykelsti" (a bike path).

sentence.da: Vi gik langs en smal **skovsti** i går.
sentence.en: We walked along a narrow forest path yesterday.

en skraldebil.explanation: "En skraldebil" means "a garbage truck". It is built from "skrald" (garbage) and "en bil" (a car). The same "bil" is in "en varebil" (a van).

sentence.da: Hver tirsdag kommer en **skraldebil** og henter vores skrald.
sentence.en: Every Tuesday a garbage truck comes and picks up our trash.

en skraldemand.explanation: "En skraldemand" means "a garbage collector". It is built from "skrald" (garbage) and "en mand" (a man). The word "mand" ends many job words, such as "en brandmand" (a firefighter). The plural is "skraldemænd", where "a" changes to "æ".

sentence.da: Vores **skraldemand** tager skraldet hver tirsdag.
sentence.en: Our garbage collector takes the garbage every Tuesday.

en skraldepose.explanation: "En skraldepose" means "a garbage bag". It is built from "skrald" (garbage) and "en pose" (a bag). The same "pose" is in "en indkøbspose" (a shopping bag).

sentence.da: Jeg putter affaldet i en **skraldepose** og binder den.
sentence.en: I put the waste in a garbage bag and tie it.

en skraldespand.explanation: "En skraldespand" means "a trash can". It is built from "skrald" (garbage) and "en spand" (a bucket). To tell someone to throw something away, use "at smide ud" (to throw away): "Smid flasken ud" (Throw the bottle away).

sentence.da: Jeg smider papiret i en **skraldespand**.
sentence.en: I throw the paper in a trash can.

en skranke.explanation: "En skranke" means "a counter". For the counter in a food store, use "en disk" (a serving counter): "Jeg køber ost ved disken" (I buy cheese at the counter).

sentence.da: Ved en **skranke** i lufthavnen kan du aflevere din kuffert.
sentence.en: At a counter in the airport you can hand in your suitcase.

en skribent.explanation: "En skribent" means "a writer". For someone who writes books, use "en forfatter" (an author): "Hun er forfatter" (She is an author).

sentence.da: Som **skribent** skriver hun artikler til flere aviser.
sentence.en: As a writer, she writes articles for several newspapers.

en skrue.explanation: "En skrue" means "a screw". To turn it into something, use the verb "at skrue" (to screw): "Jeg skruer skruen i væggen" (I screw the screw into the wall).

sentence.da: Hylden falder ned, fordi der mangler en **skrue**.
sentence.en: The shelf falls down because a screw is missing.

en skruetrækker.explanation: "En skruetrækker" means "a screwdriver". It is built from "en skrue" (a screw) and "at trække" (to pull).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger en **skruetrækker** til at stramme skruen.
sentence.en: I use a screwdriver to tighten the screw.

en skrællekniv.explanation: "En skrællekniv" means "a paring knife". It is built from "at skrælle" (to peel) and "en kniv" (a knife). To say you peel something, use the same verb: "Jeg skræller kartofler" (I peel potatoes).

sentence.da: Jeg skræller æblet med en **skrællekniv**.
sentence.en: I peel the apple with a paring knife.

en skuespiller.explanation: "En skuespiller" means "an actor", and it is used for both men and women. It is built from "et skuespil" (a play) and "en spiller" (a player).

sentence.da: Hun er **skuespiller** og arbejder på et teater.
sentence.en: She is an actor and works at a theater.

en skuespillerinde.explanation: "En skuespillerinde" means "an actress". It is built from "skuespiller" (an actor) and "-inde", an ending that makes a female form. To talk about an actor of either sex, use "skuespiller": "Hun er skuespiller" (She is an actor).

sentence.da: Hun er en kendt **skuespillerinde**, og hun har spillet i mange film.
sentence.en: She is a famous actress, and she has acted in many films.

en skuffe.explanation: "En skuffe" means "a drawer". Do not mix it up with "en skuffelse" (a disappointment): "Det var en skuffelse" (That was a disappointment).

sentence.da: Gaflerne ligger i en **skuffe** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: The forks are in a drawer in the kitchen.

en skuffelse.explanation: "En skuffelse" means "a disappointment". It comes from the verb "at skuffe" (to disappoint). To say that you are disappointed, use "skuffet" (disappointed): "Jeg er skuffet" (I am disappointed).

sentence.da: Det var en stor **skuffelse**, og jeg blev ked af det.
sentence.en: It was a big disappointment, and I felt sad.

en skulder.explanation: "En skulder" means "a shoulder". To say a part of your body hurts, use "ondt i" (pain in) and the form with "the": "Jeg har ondt i skulderen" (My shoulder hurts). To say someone shrugs, use "at trække på skuldrene" (literally "to pull on the shoulders"): "Han trak på skuldrene" (He shrugged).

sentence.da: Hun lægger sin arm om min **skulder**.
sentence.en: She puts her arm around my shoulder.

en skuldertaske.explanation: "En skuldertaske" means "a shoulder bag". It is built from "en skulder" (a shoulder) and "en taske" (a bag).

sentence.da: En **skuldertaske** bærer man på skulderen.
sentence.en: You carry a shoulder bag on the shoulder.

en skulptur.explanation: "En skulptur" means "a sculpture". To say someone makes one out of clay, use "at lave" (to make): "Hun laver en skulptur af ler" (She makes a sculpture out of clay).

sentence.da: I parken står en stor **skulptur** af bronze.
sentence.en: In the park stands a large sculpture made of bronze.

en skurk.explanation: "En skurk" means "a villain". The same word is used for a crook in real life: "Politiet fanger skurken" (The police catch the crook).

sentence.da: Helten fanger til sidst den onde **skurk**.
sentence.en: In the end, the hero catches the evil villain.

en sky.explanation: "En sky" means "a cloud". The adjective "sky" (shy) is spelled the same: "Han er sky" (He is shy).

sentence.da: Der er en mørk **sky** på himlen.
sentence.en: There is a dark cloud in the sky.

en skygge.explanation: "En skygge" means "a shadow". To say the sun makes a shadow: "Solen kaster en lang skygge" (The sun casts a long shadow). The same word also means "shade": "Jeg sidder i skyggen" (I am sitting in the shade).

sentence.da: Træet giver en dejlig **skygge** på varme dage.
sentence.en: The tree gives lovely shade on hot days.

en skyskraber.explanation: "En skyskraber" means "a skyscraper". It is built from "en sky" (a cloud) and "at skrabe" (to scrape), so literally it is a cloud scraper.

sentence.da: Fra mit hotelvindue kan jeg se en høj **skyskraber**.
sentence.en: From my hotel window I can see a tall skyscraper.

en skytte.explanation: "En skytte" means "a shooter or marksman". It is the noun for the verb "at skyde" (to shoot).

sentence.da: Han er en god **skytte** og rammer næsten altid skiven.
sentence.en: He is a good shooter and almost always hits the target.

en skål.explanation: "En skål" means "a bowl". When you raise a glass with other people, you say the same word: "Skål!" (Cheers!).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser suppe af en **skål**.
sentence.en: I eat soup from a bowl.

en skæbne.explanation: "En skæbne" means "a fate or destiny". To talk about what finally happens to a thing, use it for that outcome: "Bygningens skæbne er uvis" (The building's fate is uncertain).

sentence.da: Jeg tror ikke på **skæbne**, kun på hårdt arbejde.
sentence.en: I do not believe in fate, only in hard work.

en skærm.explanation: "En skærm" means "a screen", as on a computer or TV. A screen in a cinema is a different word, "et lærred" (a canvas): "Filmen vises på et stort lærred" (The film is shown on a big screen).

sentence.da: Min computer har en stor **skærm**.
sentence.en: My computer has a big screen.

en skøjte.explanation: "En skøjte" means "a skate", as in an ice skate. To say you ice skate, use "at løbe på skøjter" (literally, to run on skates): "Børnene løber på skøjter på søen" (The children ice skate on the lake).

sentence.da: Man tager en **skøjte** på hver fod og glider hen over isen.
sentence.en: You put a skate on each foot and glide across the ice.

en skøjtebane.explanation: "En skøjtebane" means "an ice rink". It is built from "en skøjte" (a skate) and "en bane" (a track).

sentence.da: Om vinteren fryser de vandet til en **skøjtebane** i parken.
sentence.en: In winter they freeze the water into an ice rink in the park.

en skønhed.explanation: "En skønhed" means "a beauty". To say a person is very beautiful, use it for that person: "Hun er en skønhed" (She is a beauty).

sentence.da: Jeg elsker naturens **skønhed**.
sentence.en: I love the beauty of nature.

en skønhedssalon.explanation: "En skønhedssalon" means "a beauty salon". It is built from "en skønhed" (a beauty) and "en salon" (a salon). To get your hair cut, you go to "en frisør" (a hairdresser) instead: "Jeg skal til frisør" (I am going to the hairdresser).

sentence.da: I en **skønhedssalon** kan man få lakeret neglene.
sentence.en: In a beauty salon you can have your nails painted.

en slags.explanation: "En slags" means "a kind of". It stays "en slags" before a word that takes "et": "en slags værelse" (a kind of room).

sentence.da: Han bor i en **slags** hytte ved søen.
sentence.en: He lives in a kind of cabin by the lake.

en slagter.explanation: "En slagter" means "a butcher". To say where you buy meat: "Jeg køber kød hos slagteren" (I buy meat at the butcher's).

sentence.da: Min onkel er **slagter** og sælger kød.
sentence.en: My uncle is a butcher and sells meat.

en slange.explanation: "En slange" means "a snake". The same word also means "a hose": "Jeg vander blomsterne med haveslangen" (I water the flowers with the garden hose).

sentence.da: En **slange** har ingen ben og kryber på jorden.
sentence.en: A snake has no legs and crawls on the ground.

en slave.explanation: "En slave" means "a slave". To say someone works extremely hard, compare them to one: "Hun arbejder som en slave" (She works like a slave).

sentence.da: I gamle dage kunne en rig mand eje en **slave**.
sentence.en: In the old days a rich man could own a slave.

en slette.explanation: "En slette" means "a plain", as in flat land. The verb "at slette" (to delete) has the same stem: "Jeg sletter filen" (I delete the file).

sentence.da: Landet er en flad **slette** uden bjerge.
sentence.en: The land is a flat plain without mountains.

en slikbutik.explanation: "En slikbutik" means "a candy store". It is built from "slik" (candy) and "en butik" (a shop).

sentence.da: I en **slikbutik** kan du købe slik og chokolade.
sentence.en: In a candy store you can buy candy and chocolate.

en slikpind.explanation: "En slikpind" means "a lollipop". It is built from "slik" (candy) and "en pind" (a stick). The word "pind" is also in "spisepinde" (chopsticks).

sentence.da: Barnet slikker på en **slikpind**.
sentence.en: The child licks a lollipop.

en slutning.explanation: "En slutning" means "an ending". It is the noun for the verb "at slutte" (to end). To ask how a story ends: "Hvad er slutningen på bogen?" (What is the ending of the book?).

sentence.da: Filmen har en meget sjov **slutning**.
sentence.en: The film has a very funny ending.

en slægt.explanation: "En slægt" means "a family line or lineage". In biology, the same word means "genus": "Ulven og hunden hører til samme slægt" (The wolf and the dog belong to the same genus).

sentence.da: Vores **slægt** har boet på samme gård i mange generationer.
sentence.en: Our family line has lived on the same farm for many generations.

en slægtning.explanation: "En slægtning" means "a relative". It is built from "en slægt" (a family line). To say you have relatives somewhere: "Jeg har mange slægtninge i Jylland" (I have many relatives in Jutland).

sentence.da: En **slægtning** fra Norge kommer på besøg i morgen.
sentence.en: A relative from Norway is coming to visit tomorrow.

en smag.explanation: "En smag" means "a taste", as in flavor. It is the noun for the verb "at smage" (to taste). To talk about what a person likes, the same word works: "Vi har ikke samme smag" (We do not have the same taste).

sentence.da: Suppen har en dejlig **smag** af hvidløg.
sentence.en: The soup has a lovely taste of garlic.

en smagsprøve.explanation: "En smagsprøve" means "a taste or sample". It is built from "en smag" (a taste) and "en prøve" (a sample). To ask to try something before you buy it: "Må jeg få en smagsprøve?" (May I have a taste?).

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **smagsprøve** af osten og købte et stykke.
sentence.en: I got a taste of the cheese and bought a piece.

en smartphone.explanation: "En smartphone" means "a smartphone". A shorter word for it is "en mobil" (a mobile phone): "Jeg har glemt min mobil" (I forgot my phone).

sentence.da: Min **smartphone** har internet og kamera.
sentence.en: My smartphone has internet and a camera.

en smed.explanation: "En smed" means "a smith". To name a smith who works with one metal, put the metal in front: "en guldsmed" (a goldsmith), as in "Ringen er lavet af en guldsmed" (The ring was made by a goldsmith).

sentence.da: En **smed** varmer jernet og former det med en hammer.
sentence.en: A smith heats the iron and shapes it with a hammer.

en smerte.explanation: "En smerte" means "a pain". To say you are in pain, use the plural: "Jeg har smerter" (I am in pain). To say a body part hurts, use "ondt" (pain): "Jeg har ondt i hovedet" (My head hurts, literally "I have pain in the head").

sentence.da: Jeg har en skarp **smerte** i foden.
sentence.en: I have a sharp pain in my foot.

en smoothie.explanation: "En smoothie" means "a smoothie". To say you make one at home: "Jeg laver en smoothie af banan og mælk" (I make a smoothie from banana and milk).

sentence.da: Til morgenmad drikker jeg en **smoothie** med bær.
sentence.en: For breakfast I drink a smoothie with berries.

en sms.explanation: "En sms" means "a text message". For more than one, add an apostrophe before the ending: "Jeg fik tre sms'er i går" (I got three text messages yesterday). For a message in general, you can say "en besked" (a message).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver en kort **sms** til dig.
sentence.en: I write a short text message to you.

en småkage.explanation: "En småkage" means "a cookie or biscuit". It is built from "små" (small) and "en kage" (a cake). To say there are several on the table: "Der er småkager på bordet" (There are cookies on the table).

sentence.da: Må jeg få en **småkage** til min te?
sentence.en: May I have a cookie with my tea?

en smørkniv.explanation: "En smørkniv" means "a butter knife". It is built from "smør" (butter) and "en kniv" (a knife).

sentence.da: Giv mig en **smørkniv** til brødet.
sentence.en: Give me a butter knife for the bread.

en snack.explanation: "En snack" means "a snack". A common phrase with the same meaning is "en bid mad" (a bite of food): "Jeg skal lige have en bid mad" (I just need a bite to eat).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **snack** før middag.
sentence.en: I eat a snack before dinner.

en snaps.explanation: "En snaps" means "a schnapps". The word means both the drink and one small glass of it. To say you are having one glass: "Vi tager en snaps" (We have a schnapps).

sentence.da: Til frokost drikker mange en lille, kold **snaps** til sild.
sentence.en: At lunch many people drink a small, cold schnapps with herring.

en sneaker.explanation: "En sneaker" means "a sneaker". The plural is "sneakers", with only an s added. To say what you are wearing: "Jeg har hvide sneakers på" (I am wearing white sneakers).

sentence.da: En **sneaker** er en blød sko med gummisål.
sentence.en: A sneaker is a soft shoe with a rubber sole.

en snedker.explanation: "En snedker" means "a joiner or cabinetmaker". Do not mix it up with "en tømrer" (a carpenter), who builds the wooden frame of a house: "Tømreren bygger taget på huset" (The carpenter builds the roof of the house).

sentence.da: Vores **snedker** har bygget et nyt køkken til os.
sentence.en: Our joiner has built a new kitchen for us.

en snegl.explanation: "En snegl" means "a snail or slug". To order a spiral pastry at the bakery, use the same word: "Jeg vil gerne have en snegl" (I would like a spiral pastry).

sentence.da: En **snegl** bærer sit hus på ryggen og bevæger sig langsomt.
sentence.en: A snail carries its house on its back and moves slowly.

en snemand.explanation: "En snemand" means "a snowman". It is built from "sne" (snow) and "en mand" (a man). The plural changes the vowel: "to snemænd" (two snowmen).

sentence.da: Børnene bygger en stor **snemand** i haven.
sentence.en: The children are building a big snowman in the yard.

en snerydning.explanation: "En snerydning" means "a snow removal". It is built from "sne" (snow) and "at rydde" (to clear). To say the roads are being cleared tonight: "Der er snerydning på vejene i nat" (There is snow removal on the roads tonight).

sentence.da: Byen sørger for **snerydning** på de store veje.
sentence.en: The city takes care of snow removal on the big roads.

en snestorm.explanation: "En snestorm" means "a snowstorm". It is built from "sne" (snow) and "en storm" (a storm). To say one is forecast: "Der er varslet snestorm" (A snowstorm is forecast).

sentence.da: Der kom en kraftig **snestorm** i nat.
sentence.en: A strong snowstorm came last night.

en snigskytte.explanation: "En snigskytte" means "a sniper". It is built from "at snige" (to sneak) and "en skytte" (a shooter).

sentence.da: Soldaten blev ramt af en **snigskytte** fra et hustag.
sentence.en: The soldier was hit by a sniper from a rooftop.

en snog.explanation: "En snog" means "a grass snake". The general word for any kind of snake is "en slange" (a snake): "Der ligger en slange i græsset" (There is a snake in the grass).

sentence.da: Den ufarlige **snog** svømmer over søen.
sentence.en: The harmless grass snake swims across the lake.

en snor.explanation: "En snor" means "a string or cord". The same word also means "leash". To say a dog must be on a leash: "Hunden skal i snor" (The dog must be on a leash).

sentence.da: Hun bandt en **snor** om pakken.
sentence.en: She tied a string around the package.

en socialrådgiver.explanation: "En socialrådgiver" means "a social worker". It is built from "social" (social) and "en rådgiver" (an adviser). To say you have an appointment: "Jeg har en tid hos en socialrådgiver" (I have an appointment with a social worker).

sentence.da: En **socialrådgiver** hjælper folk med penge og bolig.
sentence.en: A social worker helps people with money and housing.

en sodavand.explanation: "En sodavand" means "a soda". It is built from "soda" (soda water) and "vand" (water). The plural stays the same: "to sodavand" (two sodas).

sentence.da: En **sodavand** er sød og har bobler.
sentence.en: A soda is sweet and has bubbles.

en sodavandsis.explanation: "En sodavandsis" means "a popsicle". It is built from "en sodavand" (a soda) and "en is" (an ice), so literally it is a soda ice.

sentence.da: En **sodavandsis** er frossen sodavand på en pind.
sentence.en: A popsicle is frozen soda on a stick.

en sofa.explanation: "En sofa" means "a sofa". The low table in front of it is "et sofabord" (a coffee table), built from "sofa" and "et bord" (a table): "Kopperne står på sofabordet" (The cups are on the coffee table).

sentence.da: Vi sidder på en blød **sofa**.
sentence.en: We sit on a soft sofa.

en sok.explanation: "En sok" means "a sock". To talk about a pair, use "et par sokker" (a pair of socks): "Jeg har købt et par sokker" (I bought a pair of socks).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **sok** på min venstre fod.
sentence.en: I have a sock on my left foot.

en sol.explanation: "En sol" means "a sun". To say the sun is shining, use the form with "-en": "Solen skinner" (The sun is shining). The word "sol" is also the start of "solskin" (sunshine) and "solbriller" (sunglasses).

sentence.da: Der er meget **sol** i dag.
sentence.en: There is a lot of sun today.

en solcelle.explanation: "En solcelle" means "a solar cell". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "en celle" (a cell). Many cells together form "et solcelleanlæg" (a solar cell system): "Vi har et solcelleanlæg på taget" (We have a solar cell system on the roof).

sentence.da: Hver **solcelle** laver sollys om til strøm.
sentence.en: Each solar cell turns sunlight into electricity.

en soldat.explanation: "En soldat" means "a soldier". To say that is someone's job, leave out "en": "Hun er soldat" (She is a soldier).

sentence.da: En **soldat** har uniform på og kæmper for sit land.
sentence.en: A soldier wears a uniform and fights for his country.

en solhat.explanation: "En solhat" means "a sun hat". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "en hat" (a hat).

sentence.da: Jeg tager min **solhat** på, når solen skinner.
sentence.en: I put on my sun hat when the sun is shining.

en solnedgang.explanation: "En solnedgang" means "a sunset". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "en nedgang" (a going down). The part "nedgang" also means a drop in numbers: "en nedgang i priserne" (a drop in prices).

sentence.da: Vi ser en **solnedgang** fra stranden.
sentence.en: We watch a sunset from the beach.

en solopgang.explanation: "En solopgang" means "a sunrise". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "en opgang" (a going up). The part "opgang" is also the stairwell entrance of an apartment building: "Vi bor i opgang 3" (We live in entrance 3).

sentence.da: Vi står tidligt op og ser en **solopgang**.
sentence.en: We get up early and watch a sunrise.

en solsikke.explanation: "En solsikke" means "a sunflower". To buy flowers, you can count them by the bunch: "Jeg køber et bundt solsikker" (I buy a bunch of sunflowers).

sentence.da: Den høje **solsikke** vender sig mod solen.
sentence.en: The tall sunflower turns toward the sun.

en solskoldning.explanation: "En solskoldning" means "a sunburn". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "en skoldning" (a scald, a burn from hot liquid). To say you got sunburned: "Jeg har fået solskoldning på ryggen" (I have sunburn on my back).

sentence.da: Hun glemte solcreme og fik en slem **solskoldning**.
sentence.en: She forgot sunscreen and got a bad sunburn.

en solsort.explanation: "En solsort" means "a blackbird". The plural has no -er ending: "Jeg ser to solsorte i haven" (I see two blackbirds in the garden).

sentence.da: En **solsort** synger i træet foran huset.
sentence.en: A blackbird sings in the tree in front of the house.

en sommelier.explanation: "En sommelier" means "a sommelier". To tell a guest to ask for wine advice: "Spørg sommelieren om vinen" (Ask the sommelier about the wine).

sentence.da: Vores **sommelier** anbefaler en rød vin til oksekødet.
sentence.en: Our sommelier recommends a red wine with the beef.

en sommer.explanation: "En sommer" means "a summer". To say what is true in the summer in general, use "om sommeren": "Om sommeren er det lyst i lang tid" (In the summer it is light for a long time).

sentence.da: I **sommer** bader vi i havet.
sentence.en: This summer we swim in the sea.

en sommerdag.explanation: "En sommerdag" means "a summer day". It is built from "sommer" (summer) and "en dag" (a day).

sentence.da: Det er en varm **sommerdag**, og vi svømmer i havet.
sentence.en: It is a warm summer day, and we are swimming in the sea.

en sommerferie.explanation: "En sommerferie" means "a summer vacation". It is built from "sommer" (summer) and "ferie" (vacation). To ask what someone will do during it: "Hvad skal du lave i sommerferien?" (What are you going to do during the summer vacation?).

sentence.da: I vores **sommerferie** bader vi i havet.
sentence.en: During our summer vacation we swim in the sea.

en sommerfest.explanation: "En sommerfest" means "a summer party". It is built from "sommer" (summer) and "en fest" (a party). To say a school or club holds one: "Skolen holder sommerfest på fredag" (The school is holding a summer party on Friday).

sentence.da: Vi holder **sommerfest** i haven, når det er varmt.
sentence.en: We have a summer party in the garden when it is warm.

en sommerfugl.explanation: "En sommerfugl" means "a butterfly". It is built from "sommer" (summer) and "en fugl" (a bird), so literally it is a summer bird.

sentence.da: En **sommerfugl** har store vinger og flyver fra blomst til blomst.
sentence.en: A butterfly has big wings and flies from flower to flower.

en sommerkjole.explanation: "En sommerkjole" means "a summer dress". It is built from "sommer" (summer) and "en kjole" (a dress).

sentence.da: Hun har en gul **sommerkjole** på til festen.
sentence.en: She is wearing a yellow summer dress to the party.

en sommernat.explanation: "En sommernat" means "a summer night". The plural changes the vowel: "to sommernætter" (two summer nights). In Denmark summer nights are short and light, so you can say "Det er stadig lyst klokken ti" (It is still light at ten o'clock).

sentence.da: Vi sover med åbent vindue på en varm **sommernat**.
sentence.en: We sleep with the window open on a warm summer night.

en sosu-assistent.explanation: "En sosu-assistent" means "a health care assistant". To say that is someone's job, leave out "en": "Hun er sosu-assistent" (She is a health care assistant).

sentence.da: Min mor arbejder som **sosu-assistent** på et plejehjem.
sentence.en: My mother works as a health care assistant at a nursing home.

en souvenir.explanation: "En souvenir" means "a souvenir". To say you bring one home from a trip: "Jeg tager en souvenir med hjem" (I am bringing a souvenir home). To say "the souvenir", the r is doubled: "souvenirren".

sentence.da: Jeg købte en lille **souvenir** til min mor.
sentence.en: I bought a small souvenir for my mother.

en sovepose.explanation: "En sovepose" means "a sleeping bag". It is built from "at sove" (to sleep) and "en pose" (a bag). The part "sove" is also in "en sovesofa" (a sofa bed) and "et soveværelse" (a bedroom).

sentence.da: Jeg fryser ikke, fordi min **sovepose** er varm.
sentence.en: I am not cold because my sleeping bag is warm.

en sovesofa.explanation: "En sovesofa" means "a sofa bed". It is built from "at sove" (to sleep) and "en sofa" (a sofa).

sentence.da: Gæsterne kan sove i vores **sovesofa**.
sentence.en: The guests can sleep in our sofa bed.

en sovs.explanation: "En sovs" means "a sauce or gravy". To name a kind of sauce, put the main ingredient in front: "tomatsovs" (tomato sauce).

sentence.da: Frikadellerne smager godt med brun **sovs**.
sentence.en: The meatballs taste good with brown gravy.

en spade.explanation: "En spade" means "a spade". To say you push it into the ground to start digging: "Han stikker spaden i jorden" (He sticks the spade into the ground).

sentence.da: Med en **spade** kan man grave huller i jorden.
sentence.en: With a spade you can dig holes in the ground.

en spand.explanation: "En spand" means "a bucket". To say a bucket of something, leave out "af" (of): "Hent en spand vand" (Get a bucket of water).

sentence.da: Jeg fylder en **spand** med varmt vand.
sentence.en: I fill a bucket with hot water.

en spanier.explanation: "En spanier" means "a Spaniard". It comes from "Spanien" (Spain). To describe things from Spain, use "spansk" (Spanish) instead: "spansk vin" (Spanish wine).

sentence.da: Han er **spanier**, men han bor i Danmark nu.
sentence.en: He is Spanish, but he lives in Denmark now.

en speciallæge.explanation: "En speciallæge" means "a specialist", as in a doctor. The part "læge" (doctor) is also in "en tandlæge" (a dentist).

sentence.da: Min egen læge sendte mig videre til en **speciallæge**.
sentence.en: My own doctor sent me on to a specialist.

en speeder.explanation: "En speeder" means "an accelerator". To tell the driver to speed up, use "at træde på" (to step on): "Træd på speederen" (Step on the accelerator). To slow down, use "en bremse" (a brake): "Træd på bremsen" (Step on the brake).

sentence.da: En **speeder** får bilen til at køre hurtigere.
sentence.en: An accelerator makes the car go faster.

en spejder.explanation: "En spejder" means "a scout". It comes from "at spejde" (to look out). To say you are a member, use "at gå til" (to go to): "Jeg går til spejder" (I am in the scouts).

sentence.da: Som **spejder** lærer man at klare sig ude i naturen.
sentence.en: As a scout you learn to manage out in nature.

en spids.explanation: "En spids" means "a tip or point". To name the tip of a body part, put it after "af" (of): "spidsen af næsen" (the tip of the nose). As an adjective, "spids" means "pointed": "en spids kniv" (a pointed knife).

sentence.da: Min blyant har en brækket **spids**.
sentence.en: My pencil has a broken tip.

en spidsmus.explanation: "En spidsmus" means "a shrew". It is built from "spids" (pointed) and "en mus" (a mouse), so literally it is a pointed mouse.

sentence.da: En **spidsmus** spiser insekter og orme, ikke korn.
sentence.en: A shrew eats insects and worms, not grain.

en spillefilm.explanation: "En spillefilm" means "a feature film". It is built from "at spille" (to play, to act) and "en film" (a film). To say what you will watch: "Vi ser en spillefilm i aften" (We are watching a feature film tonight).

sentence.da: En **spillefilm** varer ofte halvanden time og har skuespillere.
sentence.en: A feature film often lasts an hour and a half and has actors.

en spiller.explanation: "En spiller" means "a player", as in a game or sport. To name a musician by instrument, put the instrument in front: "en guitarspiller" (a guitar player).

sentence.da: En **spiller** løber efter bolden på banen.
sentence.en: A player runs after the ball on the field.

en spion.explanation: "En spion" means "a spy". The verb is "at spionere" (to spy): "Han spionerer for et andet land" (He spies for another country).

sentence.da: En **spion** arbejder i hemmelighed for et andet land.
sentence.en: A spy works in secret for another country.

en spiral.explanation: "En spiral" means "a spiral". It is also the start of "en spiraltrappe" (a spiral staircase): "Vi går op ad en spiraltrappe" (We walk up a spiral staircase).

sentence.da: Trappen snor sig op i en **spiral**.
sentence.en: The stairs wind up in a spiral.

en spiseske.explanation: "En spiseske" means "a tablespoon". It is built from "at spise" (to eat) and "en ske" (a spoon). To say two tablespoons of sugar, leave out "af" (of): "to spiseskeer sukker" (two tablespoons of sugar).

sentence.da: Opskriften kræver en **spiseske** smør.
sentence.en: The recipe needs a tablespoon of butter.

en spisestue.explanation: "En spisestue" means "a dining room". It is built from "at spise" (to eat) and "en stue" (a living room).

sentence.da: Vi spiser aftensmad i en stor **spisestue**.
sentence.en: We eat dinner in a big dining room.

en spisning.explanation: "En spisning" means "a meal", as in an event where people eat together. It is the noun for the verb "at spise" (to eat). For an ordinary meal, use "et måltid" (a meal): "Morgenmad er dagens første måltid" (Breakfast is the first meal of the day).

sentence.da: Vi laver mad sammen til klubbens **spisning**.
sentence.en: We cook together for the club's shared meal.

en sportsforretning.explanation: "En sportsforretning" means "a sports store". It is built from "sport" (sport) and "en forretning" (a shop). The word "forretning" also means "a business": "Han har en forretning" (He has a business).

sentence.da: Du kan købe bolde og sko i en **sportsforretning**.
sentence.en: You can buy balls and shoes in a sports store.

en sportsgren.explanation: "En sportsgren" means "a sport", as in one kind of sport such as soccer or handball. It is built from "sport" (sport) and "en gren" (a branch), so literally it is a branch of sport.

sentence.da: Svømning er en populær **sportsgren** i Danmark.
sentence.en: Swimming is a popular sport in Denmark.

en sportsklub.explanation: "En sportsklub" means "a sports club". It is built from "sport" (sport) and "en klub" (a club). To say you belong to one: "Jeg er medlem af en sportsklub" (I am a member of a sports club).

sentence.da: Jeg træner to gange om ugen i min **sportsklub**.
sentence.en: I work out twice a week at my sports club.

en sportstaske.explanation: "En sportstaske" means "a gym bag". It is built from "sport" (sport) and "en taske" (a bag).

sentence.da: Jeg pakker tøj og sko i min **sportstaske**.
sentence.en: I pack clothes and shoes in my gym bag.

en sporvogn.explanation: "En sporvogn" means "a tram". It is built from "et spor" (a track) and "en vogn" (a carriage).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **sporvogn** gennem den gamle by.
sentence.en: We take a tram through the old town.

en sprogskole.explanation: "En sprogskole" means "a language school". To say you attend one, use "på" (at) and leave out "en": "Jeg går på sprogskole" (I go to language school).

sentence.da: Jeg lærer dansk på en **sprogskole** i byen.
sentence.en: I am learning Danish at a language school in town.

en sprøjte.explanation: "En sprøjte" means "a syringe or sprayer". It comes from the verb "at sprøjte" (to spray): "Han sprøjter vand på planterne" (He sprays water on the plants).

sentence.da: Med en **sprøjte** kan lægen give medicin direkte i kroppen.
sentence.en: With a syringe the doctor can give medicine directly into the body.

en spurv.explanation: "En spurv" means "a sparrow". The plural has no -er ending: "Der sidder to spurve på taget" (Two sparrows are sitting on the roof).

sentence.da: Den lille brune fugl i haven er en **spurv**.
sentence.en: The little brown bird in the garden is a sparrow.

en spændingsroman.explanation: "En spændingsroman" means "a thriller". It is built from "spænding" (excitement) and "en roman" (a novel). To ask for one in a bookshop: "Har du en god spændingsroman?" (Do you have a good thriller?).

sentence.da: I en **spændingsroman** vil man vide, hvem der gjorde det.
sentence.en: In a thriller you want to know who did it.

en spøg.explanation: "En spøg" means "a joke or prank". To say you said something as a joke: "Jeg sagde det for spøg" (I said it as a joke). For a joke that you tell, use "en vits" (a joke): "Han fortæller en vits" (He tells a joke).

sentence.da: Det var kun en **spøg**, og alle grinede.
sentence.en: It was only a joke, and everyone laughed.

en squash.explanation: "En squash" means "a zucchini". The sport has the same name, but without "en": "Han spiller squash" (He plays squash).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer en **squash** i tynde skiver.
sentence.en: I cut a zucchini into thin slices.

en squat.explanation: "En squat" means "a squat". To say you do squats, use "at lave" (to do): "Jeg laver ti squats" (I do ten squats).

sentence.da: Jeg bøjer knæene i en dyb **squat**.
sentence.en: I bend my knees in a deep squat.

en stagnation.explanation: "En stagnation" means "a stagnation". It is the noun for the verb "at stagnere" (to stagnate). To say the economy is not growing: "Der er stagnation i økonomien" (There is stagnation in the economy).

sentence.da: Efter en lang **stagnation** begyndte firmaet endelig at vokse igen.
sentence.en: After a long stagnation the firm finally began to grow again.

en stak.explanation: "En stak" means "a stack". To say a stack of something, put the things right after it: "en stak tallerkener" (a stack of plates). For things lying in a pile, use "en bunke" (a pile): "Der ligger en bunke tøj på gulvet" (There is a pile of clothes on the floor).

sentence.da: Der ligger en høj **stak** bøger på bordet.
sentence.en: There is a tall stack of books on the table.

en stakkel.explanation: "En stakkel" means "a poor thing". To feel sorry for a named person, put "stakkels" (poor) before the name: "Stakkels Peter!" (Poor Peter!)

sentence.da: Din **stakkel**, du er helt gennemblødt af regnen.
sentence.en: You poor thing, you are completely soaked by the rain.
