en stald.explanation: "En stald" means "a stable". To say where the cows are, use "i stalden" (in the stable): "Køerne står i stalden" (The cows are in the stable).

sentence.da: Vi har en stor **stald** til hestene.
sentence.en: We have a big stable for the horses.

en stamme.explanation: "En stamme" means "a tribe or trunk". When you talk about a group of people with a shared language and way of life, it means "a tribe": "En stamme bor i junglen" (A tribe lives in the jungle). When you talk about the thick main part of a tree, it means "a trunk": "Katten klatrer op ad stammen" (The cat climbs up the trunk). The verb "at stamme" (to stutter) is spelled the same: "Han stammer, når han er nervøs" (He stutters when he is nervous).

sentence.da: Den gamle eg har en meget tyk **stamme**.
sentence.en: The old oak has a very thick trunk.

en stand.explanation: "En stand" means "a stand or booth". To describe the condition of something, use "i god stand" (in good condition): "Cyklen er i god stand" (The bike is in good condition).

sentence.da: På messen har hver virksomhed sin egen **stand**.
sentence.en: At the trade show each company has its own booth.

en stank.explanation: "En stank" means "a stench". To talk about a smell that is neither good nor bad, use "en lugt" (a smell): "Der er en lugt af kaffe" (There is a smell of coffee).

sentence.da: Der er en forfærdelig **stank** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: There is a terrible stench in the kitchen.

en startup.explanation: "En startup" means "a startup". It comes from the English word "startup". To say where someone works, use "i": "Han arbejder i en startup" (He works in a startup).

sentence.da: Hun er iværksætter og har startet en **startup** med to venner.
sentence.en: She is an entrepreneur and has started a startup with two friends.

en stat.explanation: "En stat" means "a state", as in a country or a part of a country. To talk about the national government, use "staten" (the state): "Skatten går til staten" (The tax goes to the state).

sentence.da: Hver **stat** i USA har sin egen guvernør.
sentence.en: Each state in the USA has its own governor.

en station.explanation: "En station" means "a station". To say where you meet someone, use "på" (at) before "stationen" (the station): "Vi mødes på stationen" (We meet at the station).

sentence.da: Vi venter på toget på en **station**.
sentence.en: We wait for the train at a station.

en statistik.explanation: "En statistik" means "a statistic". To talk about the school subject, leave out "en": "Hun læser statistik" (She studies statistics).

sentence.da: Ifølge den nye **statistik** ryger færre unge i dag.
sentence.en: According to the new statistics, fewer young people smoke today.

en statsadvokat.explanation: "En statsadvokat" means "a public prosecutor". It is built from "stat" (state) and "en advokat" (a lawyer). To talk about the lawyer who speaks for the accused, use "en forsvarer" (a defense lawyer): "Forsvareren taler for den anklagede" (The defense lawyer speaks for the accused).

sentence.da: En **statsadvokat** fører sagen mod den anklagede i retten.
sentence.en: A public prosecutor handles the case against the accused in court.

en statsleder.explanation: "En statsleder" means "a head of state". In Denmark, the head of state is the monarch. To talk about the person who leads the government, use "en statsminister" (a prime minister): "Statsministeren leder regeringen" (The prime minister leads the government).

sentence.da: En **statsleder** repræsenterer sit land over for andre lande.
sentence.en: A head of state represents their country to other countries.

en statsminister.explanation: "En statsminister" means "a prime minister". It is built from "stat" (state) and "en minister" (a minister). To say what someone's job is, leave out "en" after "er": "Hun er statsminister" (She is the prime minister).

sentence.da: Danmarks **statsminister** leder landets regering.
sentence.en: Denmark's prime minister leads the country's government.

en statue.explanation: "En statue" means "a statue". To say a statue is put up, use "at rejse" (to raise): "De rejser en statue på torvet" (They put up a statue in the square).

sentence.da: Der står en gammel **statue** af en konge.
sentence.en: There is an old statue of a king.

en status.explanation: "En status" means "a status". To ask how a project is going, say: "Hvad er status på projektet?" (What is the status of the project?). To talk about a short progress update at work, say: "Vi laver en status hver fredag" (We do a status update every Friday).

sentence.da: Chefen vil have en **status** på arbejdet i dag.
sentence.en: The boss wants a status update on the work today.

en stavelse.explanation: "En stavelse" means "a syllable". To say how many syllables a word has, say: "Ordet har to stavelser" (The word has two syllables).

sentence.da: Den første **stavelse** i ordet kaffe er kaf.
sentence.en: The first syllable in the word kaffe (coffee) is kaf.

en stedfar.explanation: "En stedfar" means "a stepfather". It is built from "sted-" (step) and "far" (father). The same "sted-" starts "en stedsøster" (a stepsister): "Hun er min stedsøster" (She is my stepsister).

sentence.da: Min mor er gift med min **stedfar**, ikke min far.
sentence.en: My mother is married to my stepfather, not my father.

en stedmor.explanation: "En stedmor" means "a stepmother". It is built from "sted-" (step) and "mor" (mother). The same "sted-" starts "en stedsøster" (a stepsister): "Hun er min stedsøster" (She is my stepsister).

sentence.da: Min far er gift med min **stedmor**, ikke min mor.
sentence.en: My father is married to my stepmother, not my mother.

en stegepande.explanation: "En stegepande" means "a frying pan". It is built from "at stege" (to fry) and "en pande" (a pan). To say it in a short way, use "panden" (the pan): "Læg kødet på panden" (Put the meat in the pan).

sentence.da: Jeg steger æg på en varm **stegepande**.
sentence.en: I fry eggs in a hot frying pan.

en stegning.explanation: "En stegning" means "a frying". It comes from the verb "at stege" (to fry). To say you fry food, use the verb: "Jeg steger kødet i smør" (I fry the meat in butter).

sentence.da: Ved **stegning** skal panden være meget varm.
sentence.en: When frying, the pan must be very hot.

en stemme.explanation: "En stemme" means "a voice or a vote". When you talk about how someone sounds, it means "a voice": "Hun har en dyb stemme" (She has a deep voice). When you talk about one person's choice in an election, it means "a vote": "Hver stemme tæller" (Every vote counts). To say you vote, use the verb "at stemme": "Jeg stemmer i morgen" (I vote tomorrow).

sentence.da: Hendes **stemme** er blød og rolig.
sentence.en: Her voice is soft and calm.

en stemmeseddel.explanation: "En stemmeseddel" means "a ballot". It is built from "en stemme" (a vote) and "en seddel" (a slip of paper). The same "seddel" ends "en pengeseddel" (a banknote): "Jeg har en pengeseddel på hundrede kroner" (I have a hundred-kroner banknote).

sentence.da: Du sætter et kryds på din **stemmeseddel**.
sentence.en: You put a cross on your ballot.

en stemning.explanation: "En stemning" means "a mood or atmosphere". To say a gathering feels pleasant, use "god stemning" (good atmosphere): "Der var god stemning til festen" (There was a good atmosphere at the party). To talk about one person's mood, use "et humør" (a mood): "Hun er i godt humør" (She is in a good mood).

sentence.da: Der er en rar **stemning** i klassen.
sentence.en: There is a nice atmosphere in the class.

en sten.explanation: "En sten" means "a stone". To say people throw stones, use "at kaste" (to throw) and leave out "en": "Børnene kaster sten i søen" (The children throw stones into the lake).

sentence.da: Muren er lavet af **sten**.
sentence.en: The wall is made of stone.

en stewardesse.explanation: "En stewardesse" means "a flight attendant". To say a man has this job, use "en steward" (a male flight attendant): "Min bror er steward" (My brother is a flight attendant).

sentence.da: Hun arbejder som **stewardesse** og rejser meget.
sentence.en: She works as a flight attendant and travels a lot.

en sti.explanation: "En sti" means "a path". To talk about the road that cars drive on, use "en vej" (a road): "Bilerne kører på vejen" (The cars drive on the road).

sentence.da: Den lille **sti** går gennem skoven og ned til søen.
sentence.en: The little path goes through the forest and down to the lake.

en stige.explanation: "En stige" means "a ladder". The verb "at stige" (to rise) is spelled the same. To say a price is going up, say: "Prisen stiger" (The price is going up).

sentence.da: Han står på en **stige** og skifter pæren.
sentence.en: He is standing on a ladder and changing the bulb.

en stigning.explanation: "En stigning" means "a rise or increase". When you talk about a slope that climbs, it means "a grade": "Bakken har en stigning på ti procent" (The hill has a ten percent grade). For the opposite, use "et fald" (a drop): "Der var et fald i temperaturen" (There was a drop in the temperature).

sentence.da: Der har været en stor **stigning** i priserne på mad.
sentence.en: There has been a big rise in the price of food.

en stikdåse.explanation: "En stikdåse" means "a power strip". To talk about the socket in the wall that the power strip is plugged into, use "en stikkontakt" (a wall outlet): "Stikdåsen er sat i stikkontakten" (The power strip is plugged into the wall outlet).

sentence.da: Jeg kan sætte fem ting i den nye **stikdåse**.
sentence.en: I can plug five things into the new power strip.

en stikkontakt.explanation: "En stikkontakt" means "an outlet". To talk about the part that you push into the outlet, use "et stik" (a plug): "Sæt stikket i stikkontakten" (Put the plug in the outlet).

sentence.da: Jeg sætter min oplader i en **stikkontakt**.
sentence.en: I put my charger in an outlet.

en stikling.explanation: "En stikling" means "a cutting". To say you take cuttings from a plant, use "at tage stiklinger" (to take cuttings): "Jeg tager stiklinger fra planten" (I take cuttings from the plant).

sentence.da: Hun satte en **stikling** i et glas vand.
sentence.en: She put a cutting in a glass of water.

en stil.explanation: "En stil" means "a style". At school, "en stil" also means "an essay": "Vi skriver en stil i dansk" (We write an essay in Danish class).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt lide din **stil**, især dine sko.
sentence.en: I like your style, especially your shoes.

en stilling.explanation: "En stilling" means "a position or job". To say you are applying for a job, use "at søge" (to apply for) before it: "Jeg søger en stilling som lærer" (I am applying for a job as a teacher). In sports, it also means "the score": "Stillingen er 2-1" (The score is 2-1).

sentence.da: Hun har fået en ny **stilling** i Aarhus.
sentence.en: She has gotten a new job in Aarhus.

en stillingsannonce.explanation: "En stillingsannonce" means "a job ad". It is built from "en stilling" (a job) and "en annonce" (an ad).

sentence.da: Jeg fandt en **stillingsannonce**, og jeg vil søge jobbet.
sentence.en: I found a job ad, and I want to apply for the job.

en stirren.explanation: "En stirren" means "a stare". It comes from the verb "at stirre" (to stare). To ask someone why they look at you so hard, say: "Hvorfor stirrer du på mig?" (Why are you staring at me?)

sentence.da: Hans lange **stirren** fik hende til at se væk.
sentence.en: His long stare made her look away.

en stjerne.explanation: "En stjerne" means "a star". To say how good a hotel is, use the number of stars: "Hotellet har fem stjerner" (The hotel has five stars).

sentence.da: Om natten ser vi en **stjerne** på himlen.
sentence.en: At night we see a star in the sky.

en stol.explanation: "En stol" means "a chair". To tell someone to sit down, use "på" (on): "Sæt dig på stolen" (Sit down on the chair).

sentence.da: Jeg sidder på en **stol** ved bordet.
sentence.en: I am sitting on a chair at the table.

en storby.explanation: "En storby" means "a big city". It is built from "stor" (big) and "en by" (a town). To talk about a small place in the countryside, use "en landsby" (a village): "Min bedstemor bor i en lille landsby" (My grandmother lives in a small village).

sentence.da: Jeg vil bo i en **storby**, fordi der sker meget.
sentence.en: I want to live in a big city because a lot happens there.

en storebror.explanation: "En storebror" means "a big brother". It is built from "stor" (big) and "bror" (brother). To talk about a younger brother, use "en lillebror" (a little brother): "Min lillebror er syv år" (My little brother is seven years old).

sentence.da: Min **storebror** er ti år ældre end mig.
sentence.en: My big brother is ten years older than me.

en storesøster.explanation: "En storesøster" means "a big sister". It is built from "stor" (big) and "søster" (sister). To talk about a younger sister, use "en lillesøster" (a little sister): "Min lillesøster er syv år" (My little sister is seven years old).

sentence.da: Min **storesøster** er tre år ældre end mig.
sentence.en: My big sister is three years older than me.

en storfamilie.explanation: "En storfamilie" means "an extended family". It is built from "stor" (big) and "en familie" (a family). To talk about only parents and children, use "en kernefamilie" (a nuclear family): "Vi er en kernefamilie med mor, far og to børn" (We are a nuclear family with mom, dad and two children).

sentence.da: Til jul samles hele min **storfamilie** hos mormor.
sentence.en: At Christmas my whole extended family gathers at Grandma's.

sentence.da: En **stork** har meget lange ben og et langt næb.
sentence.en: A stork has very long legs and a long beak.

en storm.explanation: "En storm" means "a storm". To say a storm is raging, say: "Stormen raser ude" (The storm is raging outside).

sentence.da: Der kommer en **storm** med meget vind.
sentence.en: A storm is coming with a lot of wind.

en stormflod.explanation: "En stormflod" means "a storm surge". To report a weather warning, say: "Der er varsel om stormflod i nat" (There is a storm surge warning tonight).

sentence.da: Ved en **stormflod** presser vinden havet ind over kysten.
sentence.en: In a storm surge, the wind pushes the sea in over the coast.

en straf.explanation: "En straf" means "a punishment". To say someone is punished, use "at få" (to get) before it: "Han fik en hård straf" (He got a harsh punishment).

sentence.da: Børn får en **straf**, når de gør noget forkert.
sentence.en: Children get a punishment when they do something wrong.

en straffeattest.explanation: "En straffeattest" means "a criminal record". It is built from "en straf" (a punishment) and "en attest" (a certificate).

sentence.da: Til jobbet skal du aflevere en **straffeattest** fra politiet.
sentence.en: For the job you have to hand in a criminal record from the police.

en strand.explanation: "En strand" means "a beach". To say you are at the beach, use "på" (on), not "i" (in): "Vi er på stranden" (We are at the beach).

sentence.da: Der er sand og hav ved en **strand**.
sentence.en: There is sand and sea at a beach.

en strandpromenade.explanation: "En strandpromenade" means "a beach promenade". It is built from "en strand" (a beach) and "en promenade" (a promenade).

sentence.da: Vi går langs havet på en lang **strandpromenade**.
sentence.en: We walk along the sea on a long beach promenade.

en strandtur.explanation: "En strandtur" means "a trip to the beach". It is built from "en strand" (a beach) and "en tur" (a trip). The same "tur" ends "en cykeltur" (a bike ride): "Vi tager på cykeltur i morgen" (We are going on a bike ride tomorrow).

sentence.da: Vi tager på **strandtur**, hvis det bliver pænt vejr.
sentence.en: We will go on a beach trip if the weather is nice.

en strategi.explanation: "En strategi" means "a strategy". To talk about one move at a certain moment, use "en taktik" (a tactic): "Hans taktik var at vente" (His tactic was to wait).

sentence.da: Firmaet har en klar **strategi** for de næste fem år.
sentence.en: The firm has a clear strategy for the next five years.

en streamingtjeneste.explanation: "En streamingtjeneste" means "a streaming service". It is built from "streaming" (streaming) and "en tjeneste" (a service). "En tjeneste" also means "a favor": "Kan du gøre mig en tjeneste?" (Can you do me a favor?)

sentence.da: Vi betaler for en **streamingtjeneste** hver måned.
sentence.en: We pay for a streaming service every month.

en streg.explanation: "En streg" means "a line or stroke". When a surprise ruins a plan, Danes say "en streg i regningen" (literally, "a line in the bill"): "Regnen var en streg i regningen for vores picnic" (The rain ruined our picnic).

sentence.da: Tegn en **streg** på papiret med en lineal.
sentence.en: Draw a line on the paper with a ruler.

en strejke.explanation: "En strejke" means "a strike", as in workers who stop working. To say workers go on strike, use the verb "at strejke" (to strike): "De vil strejke" (They will go on strike).

sentence.da: Toget kører ikke, fordi lokomotivførerne er i **strejke**.
sentence.en: The train is not running because the train drivers are on strike.

en strid.explanation: "En strid" means "a dispute or conflict". To say something goes against a rule, use "i strid med" (in conflict with): "Det er i strid med reglerne" (It is against the rules).

sentence.da: Der er en lang **strid** mellem naboerne om et hegn.
sentence.en: There is a long dispute between the neighbors about a fence.

en strikhue.explanation: "En strikhue" means "a knitted hat". It is built from "at strikke" (to knit) and "en hue" (a hat).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **strikhue** på, fordi det er koldt.
sentence.en: I put on a knitted hat because it is cold.

en strofe.explanation: "En strofe" means "a stanza". To point to a part of a poem, say which stanza it is: "Læs anden strofe højt" (Read the second stanza aloud).

sentence.da: Hver **strofe** i digtet har fire linjer og rimer.
sentence.en: Each stanza in the poem has four lines and rhymes.

en strube.explanation: "En strube" means "a throat". To talk about the neck, use "en hals" (a neck): "Han har en lang hals" (He has a long neck).

sentence.da: Der sidder noget fast i min **strube**.
sentence.en: Something is stuck in my throat.

en struktur.explanation: "En struktur" means "a structure". The verb "at strukturere" (to structure) goes with it: "Jeg strukturerer min dag" (I structure my day).

sentence.da: Teksten har en tydelig **struktur** med en indledning og en afslutning.
sentence.en: The text has a clear structure with an introduction and an ending.

en strygning.explanation: "En strygning" means "an ironing". It comes from the verb "at stryge" (to iron). To say you iron clothes, use the verb: "Jeg stryger skjorten" (I iron the shirt).

sentence.da: Efter **strygning** ser skjorten pæn og glat ud.
sentence.en: After ironing the shirt looks neat and smooth.

en strømpe.explanation: "En strømpe" means "a stocking or sock". Danes also say "en sok" (a sock): "Jeg har et hul i min sok" (I have a hole in my sock).

sentence.da: Man har en **strømpe** på hver fod.
sentence.en: You wear a sock on each foot.

en studentereksamen.explanation: "En studentereksamen" means "a high school diploma". In Denmark, you take it at the end of three years at "et gymnasium" (an upper secondary school). To say someone has passed it, use "student": "Hun er student" (She has passed her final exams).

sentence.da: Med en **studentereksamen** kan man søge ind på universitetet.
sentence.en: With a high school diploma you can apply to the university.

en studenterfest.explanation: "En studenterfest" means "a graduation party". It is built from "en student" (a school graduate) and "en fest" (a party).

sentence.da: Min familie holder en stor **studenterfest**, når jeg bliver student.
sentence.en: My family is holding a big graduation party when I graduate.

en studenterhue.explanation: "En studenterhue" means "a graduation cap". In Denmark, it is a white cap that young people put on after passing their final school exams.

sentence.da: Hun har sin **studenterhue** på, fordi hun lige har bestået eksamen.
sentence.en: She has her graduation cap on because she just passed her exam.

en studerende.explanation: "En studerende" means "a student". To talk about a child at school, use "en elev" (a pupil): "Min datter er elev i tredje klasse" (My daughter is a pupil in third grade).

sentence.da: Hun er **studerende** på universitetet.
sentence.en: She is a student at the university.

en studiegruppe.explanation: "En studiegruppe" means "a study group". It is built from "et studie" (a study) and "en gruppe" (a group).

sentence.da: Vi mødes i vores **studiegruppe** hver torsdag og læser sammen.
sentence.en: We meet in our study group every Thursday and read together.

en studiekammerat.explanation: "En studiekammerat" means "a fellow student". It is built from "et studie" (a study) and "en kammerat" (a pal).

sentence.da: Jeg låner noter af min **studiekammerat**, når jeg har været syg.
sentence.en: I borrow notes from my fellow student when I have been sick.

en studieplan.explanation: "En studieplan" means "a study plan". It is built from "et studie" (a study) and "en plan" (a plan).

sentence.da: I min **studieplan** står der, hvad jeg skal læse hver uge.
sentence.en: My study plan says what I must read each week.

en studieretning.explanation: "En studieretning" means "a field of study". In Denmark, it is the line you choose at "et gymnasium" (an upper secondary school), such as languages or science.

sentence.da: På min **studieretning** har vi meget matematik og fysik.
sentence.en: In my field of study we have a lot of math and physics.

en studietur.explanation: "En studietur" means "a study trip". It is built from "et studie" (a study) and "en tur" (a trip).

sentence.da: Klassen tager på **studietur** til Berlin og besøger flere museer.
sentence.en: The class is going on a study trip to Berlin and visiting several museums.

en stue.explanation: "En stue" means "a living room". The same "stue" is in "stueetagen" (the ground floor): "Vi bor i stueetagen" (We live on the ground floor).

sentence.da: Vi har en sofa i vores **stue**.
sentence.en: We have a sofa in our living room.

en stund.explanation: "En stund" means "a while". To say you waited a bit, say: "Vi ventede en stund" (We waited for a while). To describe a quiet moment, add a describing word: "en rolig stund" (a calm spell).

sentence.da: Det varer kun en **stund**, og så er det forbi.
sentence.en: It only lasts a while, and then it is over.

en styrelse.explanation: "En styrelse" means "an agency". An example is "Sundhedsstyrelsen" (the Danish Health Authority).

sentence.da: Ansøgningen skal sendes til en **styrelse** under ministeriet.
sentence.en: The application must be sent to an agency under the ministry.

en styrke.explanation: "En styrke" means "a strength". To talk about physical power, say: "Han har stor styrke i armene" (He has great strength in his arms).

sentence.da: Matematik er min **styrke**, men sprog er svært.
sentence.en: Math is my strength, but languages are hard.

en størrelse.explanation: "En størrelse" means "a size". It comes from "stor" (big). To ask about someone's size, say: "Hvilken størrelse bruger du?" (What size do you wear?)

sentence.da: Har I en større **størrelse** i kjolen?
sentence.en: Do you have a bigger size in the dress?

en støtte.explanation: "En støtte" means "a support". When you talk about money that someone receives, it means "financial support": "Hun får støtte fra staten" (She gets support from the state).

sentence.da: Min familie er en stor **støtte**.
sentence.en: My family is a great support.

en støvle.explanation: "En støvle" means "a boot". To talk about boots as a pair, say: "et par støvler" (a pair of boots). The word is also in "gummistøvler" (rubber boots): "Jeg tager gummistøvler på i regnvejr" (I put on rubber boots in rainy weather).

sentence.da: Min venstre **støvle** er våd i regnen.
sentence.en: My left boot is wet in the rain.

en støvsuger.explanation: "En støvsuger" means "a vacuum cleaner". It is built from "støv" (dust) and "suger" (sucker), which comes from "at suge" (to suck). To say you vacuum, use the verb "at støvsuge": "Han støvsuger hver lørdag" (He vacuums every Saturday).

sentence.da: Jeg henter en **støvsuger** og gør stuen ren.
sentence.en: I get a vacuum cleaner and clean the living room.

en støvsugning.explanation: "En støvsugning" means "a vacuuming". It comes from the verb "at støvsuge" (to vacuum). To say you vacuum before guests come, say: "Jeg støvsuger, før gæsterne kommer" (I vacuum before the guests arrive).

sentence.da: Efter en grundig **støvsugning** er hele gulvet rent.
sentence.en: After a thorough vacuuming the whole floor is clean.

en succes.explanation: "En succes" means "a success". To say someone is successful, leave out "en": "Han har succes som forfatter" (He is successful as an author).

sentence.da: Middagen blev en stor **succes**.
sentence.en: The dinner was a big success.

en suite.explanation: "En suite" means "a suite". To talk about an ordinary hotel room, use "et værelse" (a room): "Vi har et værelse med to senge" (We have a room with two beds).

sentence.da: Vi har booket en **suite** med to soveværelser.
sentence.en: We have booked a suite with two bedrooms.

en sukkerskål.explanation: "En sukkerskål" means "a sugar bowl". It is built from "sukker" (sugar) and "en skål" (a bowl). The same "skål" is what you say when you raise a glass: "Skål!" (Cheers!)

sentence.da: Sukkeret ligger i en lille **sukkerskål**.
sentence.en: The sugar is in a small sugar bowl.

en sum.explanation: "En sum" means "a sum". When you add numbers, "summen" (the sum) is the result: "Summen af to og tre er fem" (The sum of two and three is five).

sentence.da: Han betalte en stor **sum** for huset.
sentence.en: He paid a large sum for the house.

en sundhedsplejerske.explanation: "En sundhedsplejerske" means "a health visitor". It is built from "sundhed" (health) and "pleje" (care). In Denmark, a health visitor comes to see new families after a baby is born.

sentence.da: Vi har en tid hos en **sundhedsplejerske** med babyen.
sentence.en: We have an appointment with a health visitor for the baby.

en suppe.explanation: "En suppe" means "a soup". A soup is named after its main ingredient, as in "tomatsuppe" (tomato soup): "Der er tomatsuppe til middag" (There is tomato soup for dinner).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en varm **suppe** med en ske.
sentence.en: I eat hot soup with a spoon.

en sut.explanation: "En sut" means "a pacifier". To say a baby sucks on it, use "at sutte på" (to suck on): "Babyen sutter på sin sut" (The baby sucks on its pacifier).

sentence.da: Babyen falder i søvn med sin **sut** i munden.
sentence.en: The baby falls asleep with its pacifier in its mouth.

en sutteflaske.explanation: "En sutteflaske" means "a baby bottle". It is built from "at sutte" (to suck) and "en flaske" (a bottle).

sentence.da: Babyen drikker mælk af en **sutteflaske**.
sentence.en: The baby drinks milk from a baby bottle.

en svaghed.explanation: "En svaghed" means "a weakness". To say you cannot resist something, use "at have en svaghed for" (to have a weakness for): "Jeg har en svaghed for chokolade" (I have a weakness for chocolate).

sentence.da: Min største **svaghed** er, at jeg aldrig siger nej til kage.
sentence.en: My biggest weakness is that I never say no to cake.

en svamp.explanation: "En svamp" means "a mushroom or fungus". When you talk about picking mushrooms, use the plural "svampe": "Jeg plukker svampe om efteråret" (I pick mushrooms in the fall). When you talk about washing dishes, "en svamp" means "a sponge": "Jeg vasker op med en svamp" (I wash up with a sponge).

sentence.da: Han fandt en stor **svamp** i skoven.
sentence.en: He found a big mushroom in the forest.

en svane.explanation: "En svane" means "a swan". A young swan is "en svaneunge" (a cygnet): "Svaneungen følger efter moren" (The cygnet follows its mother).

sentence.da: En hvid **svane** svømmer på søen.
sentence.en: A white swan swims on the lake.

en svans.explanation: "En svans" means "a tail". An animal's tail is also "en hale" (a tail): "Hunden logrer med halen" (The dog wags its tail).

sentence.da: Ræven har en lang og tyk **svans**.
sentence.en: The fox has a long, thick tail.

en svensker.explanation: "En svensker" means "a Swede". It comes from "Sverige" (Sweden). To talk about something Swedish, use "svensk" (Swedish): "en svensk bil" (a Swedish car).

sentence.da: Han er **svensker** og kommer fra Malmø.
sentence.en: He is Swedish and comes from Malmö.

en svigerdatter.explanation: "En svigerdatter" means "a daughter-in-law". It is built from "sviger-" (in-law) and "en datter" (a daughter).

sentence.da: Min søns kone er min **svigerdatter**.
sentence.en: My son's wife is my daughter-in-law.

en svigerfar.explanation: "En svigerfar" means "a father-in-law". It is built from "sviger-" (in-law) and "far" (father).

sentence.da: Min **svigerfar** er pensioneret.
sentence.en: My father-in-law is retired.

en svigerinde.explanation: "En svigerinde" means "a sister-in-law". To talk about a brother-in-law, use "en svoger" (a brother-in-law): "Hendes svoger bor i Aalborg" (Her brother-in-law lives in Aalborg).

sentence.da: Min **svigerinde** er gift med min bror.
sentence.en: My sister-in-law is married to my brother.

en svigermor.explanation: "En svigermor" means "a mother-in-law". It is built from "sviger-" (in-law) and "mor" (mother).

sentence.da: Min **svigermor** kommer til middag i aften.
sentence.en: My mother-in-law is coming to dinner tonight.

en svigersøn.explanation: "En svigersøn" means "a son-in-law". It is built from "sviger-" (in-law) and "en søn" (a son).

sentence.da: Min datters mand er min **svigersøn**.
sentence.en: My daughter's husband is my son-in-law.

en svindler.explanation: "En svindler" means "a swindler". To say someone cheated you out of money, use the verb "at svindle" (to cheat): "Han svindlede mig for tusind kroner" (He cheated me out of a thousand kroner).

sentence.da: En **svindler** ringede og ville have mine bankoplysninger.
sentence.en: A swindler called and wanted my bank details.

en svinestald.explanation: "En svinestald" means "a pigsty". It is built from "et svin" (a pig) and "en stald" (a stable for farm animals).

sentence.da: Grisene bor i en varm **svinestald** på gården.
sentence.en: The pigs live in a warm pigsty on the farm.

en svoger.explanation: "En svoger" means "a brother-in-law". To talk about a sister-in-law, use "en svigerinde" (a sister-in-law): "Min svigerinde bor i Odense" (My sister-in-law lives in Odense).

sentence.da: Min **svoger** er gift med min søster.
sentence.en: My brother-in-law is married to my sister.

en sværm.explanation: "En sværm" means "a swarm". To talk about many fans around a star, use "en sværm af" (a swarm of): "En sværm af fans ventede foran hotellet" (A swarm of fans waited in front of the hotel).

sentence.da: Der fløj en **sværm** af myg rundt om lampen.
sentence.en: A swarm of mosquitoes flew around the lamp.

en svømmebane.explanation: "En svømmebane" means "a swimming lane". It is built from "at svømme" (to swim) and "en bane" (a track).

sentence.da: I konkurrencen har hver deltager sin egen **svømmebane**.
sentence.en: In the competition each participant has their own lane.

en svømmehal.explanation: "En svømmehal" means "an indoor swimming pool". It is built from "at svømme" (to swim) and "en hal" (a hall).

sentence.da: Vi går i **svømmehal** hver lørdag, og børnene elsker det.
sentence.en: We go to the swimming pool every Saturday, and the children love it.

en svømmetur.explanation: "En svømmetur" means "a swim". It is built from "at svømme" (to swim) and "en tur" (a trip).

sentence.da: Efter arbejde tager jeg en **svømmetur** i poolen.
sentence.en: After work I go for a swim in the pool.

en sweater.explanation: "En sweater" means "a sweater". To say you are wearing one, use "at have ... på" (literally "to have ... on"): "Jeg har en sweater på" (I am wearing a sweater).

sentence.da: Du kan holde varmen i en **sweater**.
sentence.en: You can stay warm in a sweater.

en sygdom.explanation: "En sygdom" means "a disease". It is built from "syg" (sick). To say a person is sick, use "syg" instead: "Hun er syg" (She is sick).

sentence.da: Han er syg og har en alvorlig **sygdom**.
sentence.en: He is sick and has a serious illness.

en sygemelding.explanation: "En sygemelding" means "a sick note or sick leave". To say you call in sick, use "at melde sig syg" (literally "to report oneself sick"): "Jeg melder mig syg i dag" (I am calling in sick today).

sentence.da: Jeg har sendt min **sygemelding** til chefen i morges.
sentence.en: I sent my sick note to the boss this morning.

en sygeplejerske.explanation: "En sygeplejerske" means "a nurse". It is built from "sygepleje" (nursing). To talk about a male nurse, use the same word: "Min bror er sygeplejerske" (My brother is a nurse).

sentence.da: Min søster er **sygeplejerske** på et hospital.
sentence.en: My sister is a nurse at a hospital.

en synagoge.explanation: "En synagoge" means "a synagogue". English speakers should note the Danish spelling ends in "-goge", not "-gogue".

sentence.da: Jøder samles i en **synagoge**, når de skal bede.
sentence.en: Jews gather in a synagogue when they are going to pray.

en synd.explanation: "En synd" means "a sin". To say you feel sorry for someone, use "synd" with no religious meaning: "Det er synd for ham" (I feel sorry for him). To say something is a pity, use it the same way: "Det er synd, at det regner" (It is a pity that it rains).

sentence.da: I mange religioner er det en **synd** at stjæle.
sentence.en: In many religions it is a sin to steal.

en synder.explanation: "En synder" means "a sinner". To ask who is to blame for something small, use it for the culprit: "Hvem er synderen?" (Who is the culprit?)

sentence.da: I kirken kan hver **synder** få tilgivelse.
sentence.en: In the church, every sinner can receive forgiveness.

en synkronisering.explanation: "En synkronisering" means "a sync". It comes from "at synkronisere" (to synchronize). To say sound and picture are not timed together, use it for the timing: "Synkroniseringen af lyd og billede er dårlig" (The sync of sound and picture is bad).

sentence.da: Efter **synkronisering** har telefonen og computeren de samme filer.
sentence.en: After syncing, the phone and the computer have the same files.

en synsvinkel.explanation: "En synsvinkel" means "a point of view or angle". It is built from "syn" (sight) and "en vinkel" (an angle). To talk about the real place you look from, use it for a physical angle: "Fra den synsvinkel kan man se hele byen" (From that angle you can see the whole city).

sentence.da: Fra hans **synsvinkel** ser problemet helt anderledes ud.
sentence.en: From his point of view the problem looks completely different.

en syre.explanation: "En syre" means "an acid". It is close to "sur" (sour). To say something tastes sour, use "sur": "Æblet er surt" (The apple is sour).

sentence.da: Citron smager surt, fordi den indeholder en **syre**.
sentence.en: Lemon tastes sour because it contains an acid.

en sæk.explanation: "En sæk" means "a sack". To name what is in the sack, put it after: "en sæk mel" (a sack of flour). To say backpack, add "ryg" (back) in front: "en rygsæk" (a backpack).

sentence.da: Kartoflerne ligger i en **sæk** i kælderen.
sentence.en: The potatoes are in a sack in the cellar.

en sæl.explanation: "En sæl" means "a seal". To mean the seal on a document, use a different word, "et segl": "Brevet har et rødt segl" (The letter has a red seal).

sentence.da: En **sæl** fanger fisk i havet.
sentence.en: A seal catches fish in the sea.

en sælger.explanation: "En sælger" means "a salesperson". It comes from "at sælge" (to sell). To say what someone does for a living: "Hun er sælger i en bilforretning" (She is a salesperson at a car dealership).

sentence.da: En **sælger** hjælper kunderne i butikken.
sentence.en: A salesperson helps the customers in the store.

en sælgerske.explanation: "En sælgerske" means "a saleswoman". It is "en sælger" (a salesperson) with the ending "-ske", which makes the word feminine. The same ending is in "en sygeplejerske" (a nurse).

sentence.da: Den venlige **sælgerske** hjalp mig med skoene.
sentence.en: The friendly saleswoman helped me with the shoes.

en sæson.explanation: "En sæson" means "a season", as in a TV season or a sports season. To name the time when something is in demand, put the thing before it: "jordbærsæsonen" (the strawberry season). For spring, summer, fall and winter, use "en årstid" (a season of the year): "Min yndlingsårstid er sommer" (My favorite season is summer).

sentence.da: Tv-serien har ti afsnit i hver **sæson**.
sentence.en: The TV series has ten episodes in each season.

en sæsonbillet.explanation: "En sæsonbillet" means "a season ticket". It is built from "en sæson" (a season) and "en billet" (a ticket). A similar word is "et sæsonkort" (a season pass): "Jeg har købt et sæsonkort" (I have bought a season pass).

sentence.da: Med en **sæsonbillet** kan jeg se alle klubbens hjemmekampe.
sentence.en: With a season ticket I can see all the club's home games.

en sætning.explanation: "En sætning" means "a sentence", as in grammar. To ask someone to write one: "Skriv en sætning" (Write a sentence). For a prison sentence, use "en dom" (a verdict): "Han fik en dom på to år" (He got a sentence of two years).

sentence.da: En **sætning** slutter med et punktum.
sentence.en: A sentence ends with a period.

en sø.explanation: "En sø" means "a lake". Do not mix it up with "et hav" (a sea): "Skibet sejler på havet" (The ship sails on the sea).

sentence.da: Man kan bade og fiske i en **sø**.
sentence.en: You can swim and fish in a lake.

en søgemaskine.explanation: "En søgemaskine" means "a search engine". It is built from "at søge" (to search) and "en maskine" (a machine). To say you search online: "Jeg søger på nettet efter en cykel" (I am searching online for a bike).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger ofte en **søgemaskine** til at finde opskrifter.
sentence.en: I often use a search engine to find recipes.

en sølvfisk.explanation: "En sølvfisk" means "a silverfish". It is built from "sølv" (silver) and "en fisk" (a fish), but the animal is an insect. To talk about more than one, the word does not change: "to sølvfisk" (two silverfish).

sentence.da: En **sølvfisk** bor helst på mørke og fugtige steder.
sentence.en: A silverfish prefers to live in dark and damp places.

en søn.explanation: "En søn" means "a son". To say son-in-law, add "sviger" (in-law) in front: "en svigersøn" (a son-in-law). To say how old a son is: "Min søn er fem år" (My son is five years old).

sentence.da: Min bror har en **søn** og en datter.
sentence.en: My brother has a son and a daughter.

en søndagsmiddag.explanation: "En søndagsmiddag" means "a Sunday dinner". It is built from "en søndag" (a Sunday) and "en middag" (a dinner). The word "middag" is also in other dinners, such as "en julemiddag" (a Christmas dinner).

sentence.da: Hele familien spiser sammen til **søndagsmiddag**.
sentence.en: The whole family eats together at Sunday dinner.

en søster.explanation: "En søster" means "a sister". To say a sister shares only one parent, use "en halvsøster" (a half sister): "Min halvsøster bor i Aarhus" (My half sister lives in Aarhus). The plural is "søstre", not "søstere": "Jeg har to søstre" (I have two sisters).

sentence.da: Min **søster** og jeg har samme mor.
sentence.en: My sister and I have the same mother.

en søstjerne.explanation: "En søstjerne" means "a starfish". It is built from "sø" (sea) and "en stjerne" (a star). The same "sø" means sea in "en søløve" (a sea lion).

sentence.da: En **søstjerne** har som regel fem arme og lever i havet.
sentence.en: A starfish usually has five arms and lives in the sea.

et s-tog.explanation: "Et S-tog" means "an S-train". It is the commuter train network around Copenhagen. The part "tog" (train) is also in "et godstog" (a freight train).

sentence.da: Jeg tager et **S-tog** ind til byen.
sentence.en: I take an S-train into the city.

et salg.explanation: "Et salg" means "a sale". To say something is offered for sale, use "til salg": "Huset er til salg" (The house is for sale). For a sale with lower prices, use "et udsalg" (a clearance sale): "Der er udsalg i dag" (There is a sale today).

sentence.da: Han tjener penge på **salg** af brugte biler.
sentence.en: He makes money from the sale of used cars.

et samarbejde.explanation: "Et samarbejde" means "a collaboration". It is built from "sam" (together) and "et arbejde" (work). To name who you work with, use "i samarbejde med" (in cooperation with): "Vi laver det i samarbejde med kommunen" (We are doing it in cooperation with the municipality).

sentence.da: Vi har et godt **samarbejde** med skolen.
sentence.en: We have a good collaboration with the school.

et samfund.explanation: "Et samfund" means "a society". To talk about people in general, use "i samfundet" (in society): "Alle i samfundet skal betale skat" (Everyone in society has to pay tax). The word is also in "samfundsfag" (social studies), a school subject in Denmark: "Vi har samfundsfag i dag" (We have social studies today).

sentence.da: Hvert **samfund** har sine egne regler.
sentence.en: Every society has its own rules.

et samfundsproblem.explanation: "Et samfundsproblem" means "a social problem". It is built from "et samfund" (a society) and "et problem" (a problem). The part "samfunds-" is also in "samfundsfag" (social studies), a school subject in Denmark: "Vi har samfundsfag i dag" (We have social studies today).

sentence.da: Ensomhed blandt ældre er et stort **samfundsproblem**.
sentence.en: Loneliness among older people is a big social problem.

et samliv.explanation: "Et samliv" means "a life together". It is built from "sam" (together) and "et liv" (a life). To say how long a couple has been together: "Deres samliv har varet i ti år" (Their life together has lasted ten years).

sentence.da: Deres **samliv** er roligt, og de skændes næsten aldrig.
sentence.en: Their life together is calm, and they almost never argue.

et sammenskudsgilde.explanation: "Et sammenskudsgilde" means "a potluck". It is built from "at skyde sammen" (to chip in together) and "et gilde" (a feast). The same "at skyde sammen" is used when people share a cost: "Vi skyder sammen til en gave" (We are chipping in for a gift).

sentence.da: Alle tager noget med til et **sammenskudsgilde**, så der er mad nok.
sentence.en: Everyone brings something to a potluck, so there is enough food.

et sammenstød.explanation: "Et sammenstød" means "a clash or collision". It is built from "sammen" (together) and "et stød" (a bump). To say two cars hit each other: "Der var et sammenstød mellem to biler" (There was a collision between two cars). To say two people disagree sharply: "Der var et hårdt sammenstød mellem de to politikere" (There was a harsh clash between the two politicians).

sentence.da: Der var et **sammenstød** mellem politiet og demonstranterne.
sentence.en: There was a clash between the police and the demonstrators.

et sammentræf.explanation: "Et sammentræf" means "a coincidence". To react to a surprising coincidence, say: "Sikke et sammentræf!" (What a coincidence!) The same "sikke et ..." works for other surprises: "Sikke et vejr!" (What weather!)

sentence.da: Det var et **sammentræf**, at vi begge besøgte Rom samme dag.
sentence.en: It was a coincidence that we both visited Rome on the same day.

et samtaleemne.explanation: "Et samtaleemne" means "a topic of conversation". It is built from "en samtale" (a conversation) and "et emne" (a topic). To ask someone to talk about something else: "Kan vi skifte samtaleemne?" (Can we change the subject?)

sentence.da: Vejret er altid et godt **samtaleemne**.
sentence.en: The weather is always a good topic of conversation.

et samvær.explanation: "Et samvær" means "a time together". To say you enjoyed the company, use the form "godt samvær" (good company): "Vi nød det gode samvær" (We enjoyed the good company). In family matters, it also means the time a child spends with the parent they do not live with: "Hvornår har faren samvær med børnene?" (When does the father have time with the children?)

sentence.da: Børnene har **samvær** med deres far hver anden weekend.
sentence.en: The children spend time with their father every other weekend.

et sankthansbål.explanation: "Et sankthansbål" means "a Midsummer bonfire". It is built from "Sankt Hans" (Saint John) and "et bål" (a bonfire). In Denmark, it is lit on the evening of 23 June. A straw witch, "en heks" (a witch), is burned on the fire.

sentence.da: Mange tænder et stort **sankthansbål** ved vandet og synger sammen.
sentence.en: Many people light a big Midsummer bonfire by the water and sing together.

et sejl.explanation: "Et sejl" means "a sail". The verb "at sejle" (to sail) comes from the same stem. It means to travel by any boat, even one without a sail: "Færgen sejler til Sverige" (The ferry sails to Sweden).

sentence.da: Båden har et hvidt **sejl**, som vinden blæser i.
sentence.en: The boat has a white sail that the wind blows into.

et sekund.explanation: "Et sekund" means "a second", as on a clock. To ask someone to wait a short moment, use "et øjeblik" (a moment) instead: "Et øjeblik, tak" (One moment, please).

sentence.da: Det tager kun et **sekund**.
sentence.en: It only takes a second.

et selskab.explanation: "Et selskab" means "a company or gathering". To talk about a party, use it for a gathering of people: "Vi var til et selskab hos naboerne" (We were at a party at the neighbors'). To talk about a business, it is the end of words like "et forsikringsselskab" (an insurance company): "Han arbejder i et forsikringsselskab" (He works at an insurance company).

sentence.da: Vi holder et **selskab** for vores venner i morgen.
sentence.en: We are throwing a party for our friends tomorrow.

et semester.explanation: "Et semester" means "a semester". To name which semester, put the season before it: "efterårssemestret" (the autumn semester) and "forårssemestret" (the spring semester).

sentence.da: Vi har eksamen i slutningen af hvert **semester**.
sentence.en: We have exams at the end of each semester.

et senat.explanation: "Et senat" means "a senate". Denmark has no senate, only one house called "Folketinget" (the Danish parliament).

sentence.da: USA har et **senat** med hundrede senatorer, to fra hver delstat.
sentence.en: The USA has a senate with a hundred senators, two from each state.

et shot.explanation: "Et shot" means "a shot", as in a small strong drink. To name the drink, put it after "shot": "et shot tequila" (a shot of tequila).

sentence.da: Jeg tager et **shot** espresso om morgenen.
sentence.en: I have a shot of espresso in the morning.

et show.explanation: "Et show" means "a show". To talk about a talk show on television, use "et talkshow" (a talk show): "Han er vært i et talkshow" (He hosts a talk show).

sentence.da: Vi så et fedt **show** med sang og dans i går.
sentence.en: We saw a cool show with singing and dancing yesterday.

et sidespor.explanation: "Et sidespor" means "a digression or sidetrack". It is built from "en side" (a side) and "et spor" (a track). On a railway, it is also a siding: "Toget holder på et sidespor" (The train is standing on a siding).

sentence.da: Vi kom ind på et **sidespor** og glemte, hvad mødet handlede om.
sentence.en: We got onto a sidetrack and forgot what the meeting was about.

et signal.explanation: "Et signal" means "a signal". To say someone sends a signal, use "at give et signal" (to give a signal): "Hun gav et signal med hånden" (She gave a signal with her hand). To say your phone has no reception: "Jeg har ikke noget signal her" (I do not have any signal here).

sentence.da: Når lyset skifter til grønt, er det et **signal** til at køre.
sentence.en: When the light changes to green, it is a signal to drive.

et sind.explanation: "Et sind" means "a mind". To describe someone who listens to new ideas: "et åbent sind" (an open mind). To say what someone intends, use "at have i sinde" (to intend): "Hvad har du i sinde?" (What do you intend to do?)

sentence.da: Hun har et roligt **sind** og bliver aldrig vred.
sentence.en: She has a calm mind and never gets angry.

et siv.explanation: "Et siv" means "a rush", as in the plant. The plural is the same as the singular: "to siv" (two rushes).

sentence.da: Ænderne bygger rede i det høje **siv** ved søen.
sentence.en: The ducks build nests in the tall rushes by the lake.

et skab.explanation: "Et skab" means "a cupboard". To name the kind of cupboard, add a word in front: "et køleskab" (a refrigerator, literally "a cooling cupboard").

sentence.da: Tallerkenerne står i et **skab**.
sentence.en: The plates are in a cupboard.

et skattekort.explanation: "Et skattekort" means "a tax card". It is built from "en skat" (a tax) and "et kort" (a card). In Denmark, the tax card is digital, and your employer gets it from the tax authorities.

sentence.da: Uden et **skattekort** kan arbejdsgiveren ikke trække den rigtige skat.
sentence.en: Without a tax card, the employer cannot withhold the right tax.

et skelet.explanation: "Et skelet" means "a skeleton". To talk about the bare frame of a building, use the same word: "Husets skelet er rejst" (The frame of the house is up).

sentence.da: Når kødet er væk, er der kun et **skelet** tilbage.
sentence.en: When the flesh is gone, only a skeleton is left.

et skema.explanation: "Et skema" means "a schedule or a form". To ask about today's lessons at school: "Hvad står der på skemaet i dag?" (What is on the schedule today?) To tell someone to fill in a form: "Udfyld skemaet" (Fill in the form).

sentence.da: Der er gymnastik på mit **skema** hver torsdag.
sentence.en: There is gym on my schedule every Thursday.

et skib.explanation: "Et skib" means "a ship". To say you are on a ship: "Vi er ombord på skibet" (We are on board the ship). For a small boat, use "en båd" (a boat): "Vi tog en båd over søen" (We took a boat across the lake).

sentence.da: Et stort **skib** sejler over havet til Norge.
sentence.en: A big ship sails across the sea to Norway.

et skift.explanation: "Et skift" means "a shift or change". To say a change in a plan: "et skift i planen" (a change in the plan). To name a work shift, put the time of day before it: "et natskift" (a night shift).

sentence.da: Han tager et ekstra **skift** i morgen.
sentence.en: He is taking an extra shift tomorrow.

et skilt.explanation: "Et skilt" means "a sign". To say a road sign: "et vejskilt" (a road sign). The same word "skilt" also means "divorced": "Hun er skilt" (She is divorced).

sentence.da: Et **skilt** viser vej til stationen.
sentence.en: A sign shows the way to the station.

et skind.explanation: "Et skind" means "a skin or hide". To name the animal, put it before "skind": "et fåreskind" (a sheepskin). For a person's skin, use "en hud" (skin) instead: "Min hud er tør" (My skin is dry).

sentence.da: Et **skind** fra et får kan holde dig varm om vinteren.
sentence.en: A hide from a sheep can keep you warm in the winter.

et skjold.explanation: "Et skjold" means "a shield". To say coat of arms, add "våben" (weapon) in front: "et våbenskjold" (a coat of arms).

sentence.da: Soldaten holdt sit **skjold** op for at stoppe pilene.
sentence.en: The soldier held up his shield to stop the arrows.

et skohorn.explanation: "Et skohorn" means "a shoehorn". It is built from "en sko" (a shoe) and "et horn" (a horn).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **skohorn**, fordi skoene er stramme.
sentence.en: I use a shoehorn because the shoes are tight.

et skolefag.explanation: "Et skolefag" means "a school subject". It is built from "en skole" (a school) and "et fag" (a subject). To say your favorite subject, use "yndlingsfag" (favorite subject): "Matematik er mit yndlingsfag" (Math is my favorite subject).

sentence.da: Hvilket **skolefag** kan du bedst lide?
sentence.en: Which school subject do you like best?

et skoleår.explanation: "Et skoleår" means "a school year". It is built from "en skole" (a school) and "et år" (a year). In Denmark, the school year starts in August.

sentence.da: Efter sommerferien begynder et nyt **skoleår**.
sentence.en: After the summer vacation a new school year begins.

et skridt.explanation: "Et skridt" means "a step", as in a footstep. To say something is an important move in a plan: "Det er et vigtigt skridt" (It is an important step). For a step on a stairway, use "et trin" (a step): "Pas på det sidste trin" (Watch the last step).

sentence.da: Hun tog et **skridt** frem og smilede.
sentence.en: She took a step forward and smiled.

et skrig.explanation: "Et skrig" means "a scream". It comes from the verb "at skrige" (to scream). To say someone lets out a scream: "Hun udstødte et skrig" (She let out a scream).

sentence.da: Vi hørte et **skrig** fra gaden.
sentence.en: We heard a scream from the street.

et skrivebord.explanation: "Et skrivebord" means "a desk". It is built from "at skrive" (to write) and "et bord" (a table). The same "skrive" is in "en skrivemaskine" (a typewriter).

sentence.da: Hun sidder ved sit **skrivebord** og arbejder.
sentence.en: She sits at her desk and works.

et skud.explanation: "Et skud" means "a shot", as from a gun. To say you heard a gunshot: "Vi hørte et skud" (We heard a shot). For a small strong drink, use "et shot" (a shot): "Vi drak hver et shot" (We each drank a shot).

sentence.da: Hans **skud** gik forbi målet.
sentence.en: His shot missed the goal.

et skudsår.explanation: "Et skudsår" means "a gunshot wound". It is built from "et skud" (a shot) and "et sår" (a wound). The same "sår" is in "et knivsår" (a stab wound). Do not mix it up with "et skudår" (a leap year): "Næste år er et skudår" (Next year is a leap year).

sentence.da: Den sårede mand havde et **skudsår** i benet og blødte meget.
sentence.en: The wounded man had a gunshot wound in his leg and bled a lot.

et skudår.explanation: "Et skudår" means "a leap year". The extra day is "en skuddag" (a leap day): "Den 29. februar er en skuddag" (29 February is a leap day). Do not mix it up with "et skudsår" (a gunshot wound): "Han har et skudsår i benet" (He has a gunshot wound in his leg).

sentence.da: Februar har 29 dage i et **skudår**.
sentence.en: February has 29 days in a leap year.

et skuespil.explanation: "Et skuespil" means "a play", as in theater. To say you go to see one: "Vi skal se et skuespil i aften" (We are going to see a play tonight). Do not mix it up with "en skuespiller" (an actor): "Skuespilleren glemte sin replik" (The actor forgot his line).

sentence.da: I et **skuespil** taler skuespillerne med hinanden foran publikum.
sentence.en: In a play, the actors talk to each other in front of an audience.

et skur.explanation: "Et skur" means "a shed". To say where things are kept: "Cyklerne står i skuret" (The bikes are in the shed). The word is also the end of "et regnskur" (a rain shower).

sentence.da: Vi har et lille **skur** bag huset.
sentence.en: We have a small shed behind the house.

et skybrud.explanation: "Et skybrud" means "a cloudburst". It is built from "en sky" (a cloud) and "et brud" (a break), so it is literally "a cloud break".

sentence.da: Efter et **skybrud** stod gaderne under vand.
sentence.en: After a cloudburst, the streets were under water.

et skydevåben.explanation: "Et skydevåben" means "a firearm". It is built from "at skyde" (to shoot) and "et våben" (a weapon).

sentence.da: Man må ikke have et **skydevåben** uden tilladelse.
sentence.en: You must not have a firearm without a permit.

et skæg.explanation: "Et skæg" means "a beard". For a mustache, use "et overskæg" (literally "an over-beard"): "Han har et overskæg" (He has a mustache).

sentence.da: Min far har et langt **skæg**.
sentence.en: My father has a long beard.

et skænderi.explanation: "Et skænderi" means "an argument". It comes from the verb "at skændes" (to quarrel). To say two people had an argument: "De havde et skænderi om penge" (They had an argument about money).

sentence.da: Det var et højlydt **skænderi**, og naboerne kunne høre det.
sentence.en: It was a loud argument, and the neighbors could hear it.

et skærebræt.explanation: "Et skærebræt" means "a cutting board". It is built from "at skære" (to cut) and "et bræt" (a board). The same "bræt" is in "et strygebræt" (an ironing board).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer tomaterne på et **skærebræt** af træ.
sentence.en: I cut the tomatoes on a wooden cutting board.

et skærmbillede.explanation: "Et skærmbillede" means "a screenshot". It is built from "en skærm" (a screen) and "et billede" (a picture). To ask someone to send one: "Kan du sende et skærmbillede?" (Can you send a screenshot?)

sentence.da: Jeg tog et **skærmbillede** af beskeden.
sentence.en: I took a screenshot of the message.

et skøn.explanation: "Et skøn" means "an estimate or judgment". To give your own estimate, use "efter mit skøn" (by my estimate): "Efter mit skøn tager det en time" (By my estimate it takes an hour). Do not mix it up with the adjective "skøn" (lovely): "Det er en skøn dag" (It is a lovely day).

sentence.da: Det er kun et **skøn**, så den rigtige pris kan være højere.
sentence.en: It is only an estimate, so the real price may be higher.

et slag.explanation: "Et slag" means "a blow or battle". To say someone was hit: "Han fik et slag i ansigtet" (He got a blow to the face). To name a battle: "Slaget ved Dybbøl" (the Battle of Dybbøl). The same word is in "et hjerteslag" (a heartbeat).

sentence.da: En hær kan vinde et **slag**, men tabe krigen.
sentence.en: An army can win a battle but lose the war.

et slagord.explanation: "Et slagord" means "a slogan". It is built from "et slag" (a blow) and "et ord" (a word). To ask someone what their slogan is: "Hvad er jeres slagord?" (What is your slogan?)

sentence.da: Partiets **slagord** er kort, og mange kan huske det.
sentence.en: The party's slogan is short, and many people can remember it.

et slagsmål.explanation: "Et slagsmål" means "a fight", with fists and blows. For a fight with words, use "et skænderi" (an argument): "De havde et skænderi" (They had an argument).

sentence.da: Drengene kom i **slagsmål** efter skole.
sentence.en: The boys got into a fight after school.

et slagtilfælde.explanation: "Et slagtilfælde" means "a stroke". It is built from "et slag" (a blow) and "et tilfælde" (a case). To say someone had a stroke: "Han fik et slagtilfælde" (He had a stroke).

sentence.da: Efter et **slagtilfælde** kunne han ikke bevæge sin højre arm.
sentence.en: After a stroke, he could not move his right arm.

et slips.explanation: "Et slips" means "a tie". To say you put on a tie: "Han tager slips på" (He puts on a tie).

sentence.da: Min far har **slips** på til mødet.
sentence.en: My father is wearing a tie to the meeting.

et slot.explanation: "Et slot" means "a castle". To say a palace, use the same word: "Amalienborg Slot" (Amalienborg Palace).

sentence.da: Kongen bor på et stort **slot**.
sentence.en: The king lives in a big castle.

et smagsløg.explanation: "Et smagsløg" means "a taste bud". It is built from "smag" (taste) and "et løg" (an onion), so it is literally "a taste onion". To say a dish is exciting to taste: "pirre smagsløgene" (to excite the taste buds).

sentence.da: Tungen har tusindvis af **smagsløg**, som kan mærke sødt og surt.
sentence.en: The tongue has thousands of taste buds that can feel sweet and sour.

et smil.explanation: "Et smil" means "a smile". The matching verb is "at smile" (to smile): "Hun smiler" (She is smiling). To say how someone answers: "Hun svarede med et smil" (She answered with a smile).

sentence.da: Hun gav mig et **smil** og sagde hej.
sentence.en: She gave me a smile and said hi.

et smykke.explanation: "Et smykke" means "a piece of jewelry". To talk about jewelry in general, use the plural "smykker": "Hun elsker smykker" (She loves jewelry).

sentence.da: Hun har et smukt **smykke** om halsen.
sentence.en: She has a beautiful piece of jewelry around her neck.

et småbarn.explanation: "Et småbarn" means "a toddler". It is built from "små" (small) and "et barn" (a child). The plural is "småbørn", not "småbarn": "Der er mange småbørn på legepladsen" (There are many toddlers on the playground).

sentence.da: Et **småbarn** er for lille til at gå i skole.
sentence.en: A toddler is too little to go to school.

et smørrebrød.explanation: "Et smørrebrød" means "an open sandwich". It is built from "smør" (butter) and "et brød" (bread). In Denmark, it is a traditional dish made on "rugbrød" (rye bread). The plural is the same as the singular: "to smørrebrød" (two open sandwiches).

sentence.da: Til frokost bestiller vi **smørrebrød** med fisk.
sentence.en: For lunch we order open sandwiches with fish.

et snefnug.explanation: "Et snefnug" means "a snowflake". It is built from "sne" (snow) and "et fnug" (a bit of fluff). To say big snowflakes are falling: "Der falder store snefnug" (Big snowflakes are falling).

sentence.da: Det første **snefnug** smelter i min hånd.
sentence.en: The first snowflake melts in my hand.

et snit.explanation: "Et snit" means "a cut or average". To say a cut in cloth: "et snit i stoffet" (a cut in the fabric). To say an average, you can also use "et gennemsnit" (an average): "Hendes gennemsnit er 9,5" (Her average is 9.5).

sentence.da: Hendes **snit** fra gymnasiet er højt nok til lægestudiet.
sentence.en: Her average from high school is high enough for medical school.

et snørebånd.explanation: "Et snørebånd" means "a shoelace". It is built from "at snøre" (to lace up) and "et bånd" (a band). The same "bånd" is in "et armbånd" (a bracelet).

sentence.da: Jeg skal binde mit **snørebånd**, før vi går.
sentence.en: I have to tie my shoelace before we go.

et sofabord.explanation: "Et sofabord" means "a coffee table". It is built from "en sofa" (a sofa) and "et bord" (a table). The same "bord" is in "et spisebord" (a dining table): "Vi spiser ved spisebordet" (We eat at the dining table).

sentence.da: Kopperne står på et lille **sofabord**.
sentence.en: The cups are on a small coffee table.

et solbær.explanation: "Et solbær" means "a blackcurrant". It is built from "en sol" (a sun) and "et bær" (a berry). Do not mix it up with "et ribs" (a redcurrant): "Solbær er sorte, og ribs er røde" (Blackcurrants are black, and redcurrants are red).

sentence.da: Jeg laver saft af **solbær** og vand.
sentence.en: I make juice from blackcurrants and water.

et solcenter.explanation: "Et solcenter" means "a tanning salon". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "et center" (a center). The same "sol" is in "en solbrille" (sunglasses): "Jeg har glemt mine solbriller" (I have forgotten my sunglasses).

sentence.da: Hun tager i **solcenter**, fordi hun vil være brun.
sentence.en: She goes to a tanning salon because she wants to be tan.

et solhverv.explanation: "Et solhverv" means "a solstice". To name which solstice, put the season in front: "sommersolhverv" (the summer solstice) and "vintersolhverv" (the winter solstice).

sentence.da: Ved **solhverv** i juni bliver det næsten aldrig helt mørkt.
sentence.en: At the solstice in June it almost never gets completely dark.

et solpanel.explanation: "Et solpanel" means "a solar panel". It is built from "en sol" (a sun) and "et panel" (a panel).

sentence.da: Vi har et **solpanel** på taget, og det giver strøm.
sentence.en: We have a solar panel on the roof, and it produces electricity.

et solstik.explanation: "Et solstik" means "a sunstroke". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "et stik" (a sting), so it is literally "a sun sting". The same "stik" is in "et myggestik" (a mosquito bite).

sentence.da: Hun fik **solstik** af at ligge i solen hele dagen.
sentence.en: She got sunstroke from lying in the sun all day.

et sommerhus.explanation: "Et sommerhus" means "a summer house". It is built from "sommer" (summer) and "et hus" (a house). To say you rent one: "Vi lejer et sommerhus i Jylland" (We are renting a summer house in Jutland).

sentence.da: Vi tager i **sommerhus** hver sommer.
sentence.en: We go to the summer house every summer.

et sommerhusområde.explanation: "Et sommerhusområde" means "a summer house area". It is built from "et sommerhus" (a summer house) and "et område" (an area).

sentence.da: Om vinteren er der stille i vores **sommerhusområde**.
sentence.en: In the winter, it is quiet in our summer house area.

et sommerjob.explanation: "Et sommerjob" means "a summer job". It is built from "sommer" (summer) and "et job" (a job). To ask if someone has work this summer: "Har du et sommerjob?" (Do you have a summer job?)

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have et **sommerjob** i en café.
sentence.en: I would like a summer job in a café.

et sortiment.explanation: "Et sortiment" means "an assortment". To say a shop sells many kinds of goods: "Butikken har et bredt sortiment" (The shop has a wide range).

sentence.da: Butikken har et stort **sortiment** af ost fra hele Europa.
sentence.en: The shop has a large assortment of cheese from all over Europe.

et soundtrack.explanation: "Et soundtrack" means "a soundtrack". To say you listen to the music from a film, use "at lytte til" (to listen to): "Jeg lytter til soundtracket" (I am listening to the soundtrack).

sentence.da: Filmen har et flot **soundtrack**.
sentence.en: The movie has a nice soundtrack.

et soveværelse.explanation: "Et soveværelse" means "a bedroom". It is built from "at sove" (to sleep) and "et værelse" (a room). "Sove" also appears in "en sovepose" (a sleeping bag).

sentence.da: Jeg sover i min seng i mit **soveværelse**.
sentence.en: I sleep in my bed in my bedroom.

et speciale.explanation: "Et speciale" means "a specialty or master's thesis". When you talk about what a restaurant or a person is best at, it means "specialty": "husets speciale" (the house specialty). When you talk about the large final project of a university degree, it means "master's thesis": "Jeg afleverer mit speciale i juni" (I am handing in my thesis in June).

sentence.da: Hun skriver **speciale** om børns sprog på universitetet.
sentence.en: She is writing her thesis about children's language at the university.

et spejl.explanation: "Et spejl" means "a mirror". To say you see yourself in the mirror, use "se sig selv i spejlet" (to see yourself in the mirror): "Hun ser sig selv i spejlet" (She sees herself in the mirror).

sentence.da: Jeg kan se mit ansigt i et **spejl**.
sentence.en: I can see my face in a mirror.

et spejlæg.explanation: "Et spejlæg" means "a fried egg". It is built from "et spejl" (a mirror) and "et æg" (an egg).

sentence.da: Han steger et **spejlæg** til morgenmad.
sentence.en: He fries a sunny-side-up egg for breakfast.

et spil.explanation: "Et spil" means "a game". It comes from "at spille" (to play). To say you play a game, use "at spille": "at spille skak" (to play chess). To say you play an instrument, use the same verb: "at spille guitar" (to play guitar).

sentence.da: Skak er et **spil** for to personer.
sentence.en: Chess is a game for two people.

et spindelvæv.explanation: "Et spindelvæv" means "a spiderweb". It is built from "spindel" (spider) and "et væv" (a woven fabric).

sentence.da: Edderkoppen fanger fluer i sit **spindelvæv**.
sentence.en: The spider catches flies in its spiderweb.

et spisebord.explanation: "Et spisebord" means "a dining table". It is built from "at spise" (to eat) and "et bord" (a table). "Spise" also appears in "en spiseske" (a tablespoon).

sentence.da: Vi har et stort **spisebord**, så der er plads til alle.
sentence.en: We have a big dining table, so there is room for everyone.

et spisekammer.explanation: "Et spisekammer" means "a pantry". It is built from "at spise" (to eat) and "et kammer" (a chamber).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger pasta og ris i vores **spisekammer**.
sentence.en: I put pasta and rice in our pantry.

et spisested.explanation: "Et spisested" means "an eatery". It is built from "at spise" (to eat) and "et sted" (a place). To ask for somewhere to eat nearby, say: "Er der et spisested i nærheden?" (Is there an eatery nearby?)

sentence.da: Der er et billigt **spisested** lige ved stationen.
sentence.en: There is a cheap eatery right by the station.

et spor.explanation: "Et spor" means "a track or a trace". When you talk about marks left behind, it means "a trace" or "a track": "Der er spor i sneen" (There are tracks in the snow). When you say where a train leaves from, it means "track": "Toget afgår fra spor 3" (The train leaves from track 3).

sentence.da: Politiet fandt et **spor** efter tyven.
sentence.en: The police found a trace of the thief.

et springvand.explanation: "Et springvand" means "a fountain". It is built from "at springe" (to jump) and "vand" (water).

sentence.da: Der er et smukt **springvand** midt i parken.
sentence.en: There is a beautiful fountain in the middle of the park.

et sprog.explanation: "Et sprog" means "a language". To say how many languages someone speaks, use "at tale" (to speak): "Hun taler tre sprog" (She speaks three languages).

sentence.da: Dansk og engelsk er to **sprog**.
sentence.en: Danish and English are two languages.

et sprogcenter.explanation: "Et sprogcenter" means "a language center". It is built from "et sprog" (a language) and "et center" (a center).

sentence.da: Jeg lærer dansk på et **sprogcenter** hver dag.
sentence.en: I learn Danish at a language center every day.

et spyd.explanation: "Et spyd" means "a spear". When you talk about the athletics event, the same word means "javelin": "at kaste spyd" (to throw the javelin).

sentence.da: Vikingerne brugte et **spyd** til at jage og kæmpe.
sentence.en: The Vikings used a spear to hunt and fight.

et spædbarn.explanation: "Et spædbarn" means "an infant". The plural is "spædbørn" (infants), because "et barn" (a child) has the plural "børn" (children).

sentence.da: Et **spædbarn** sover det meste af dagen.
sentence.en: An infant sleeps most of the day.

et spøgelse.explanation: "Et spøgelse" means "a ghost". It comes from the verb "at spøge" (to haunt). To say a place is haunted, say: "Det spøger i det gamle hus" (The old house is haunted).

sentence.da: Der er et **spøgelse** i det gamle hus.
sentence.en: There is a ghost in the old house.

et spørgeskema.explanation: "Et spørgeskema" means "a questionnaire". It is built from "at spørge" (to ask) and "et skema" (a chart or form).

sentence.da: Alle studerende skal udfylde et **spørgeskema** om kurset.
sentence.en: All students must fill in a questionnaire about the course.

et spørgsmål.explanation: "Et spørgsmål" means "a question". To ask permission to ask something, say: "Må jeg stille et spørgsmål?" (May I ask a question?) Literally, it says "May I put a question?"

sentence.da: Læreren svarer på mit **spørgsmål**.
sentence.en: The teacher answers my question.

et spørgsmålstegn.explanation: "Et spørgsmålstegn" means "a question mark". It is built from "et spørgsmål" (a question) and "et tegn" (a sign). When you mean a sign in general, "tegn" is used alone: "et tegn på forår" (a sign of spring).

sentence.da: Sætningen slutter med et **spørgsmålstegn**, fordi den er et spørgsmål.
sentence.en: The sentence ends with a question mark because it is a question.

et stadie.explanation: "Et stadie" means "a stage", as in one step in a process. To say where an actor stands in a theater, use "en scene" (a stage): "Skuespilleren står på scenen" (The actor stands on the stage).

sentence.da: Sygdommen er i et tidligt **stadie**, og lægen er positiv.
sentence.en: The illness is at an early stage, and the doctor is optimistic.

et stadion.explanation: "Et stadion" means "a stadium". To say where a concert takes place, say: "Koncerten er på stadion" (The concert is at the stadium).

sentence.da: Der er mange mennesker på **stadion** i dag.
sentence.en: There are many people at the stadium today.

et standpunkt.explanation: "Et standpunkt" means "a point of view". To say you form your own opinion on something, use "at tage standpunkt til" (to take a position on): "Man må tage standpunkt til spørgsmålet" (You have to take a position on the question).

sentence.da: Politikeren holder fast i sit **standpunkt**, selv når andre er uenige.
sentence.en: The politician sticks to his position, even when others disagree.

et statsborgerskab.explanation: "Et statsborgerskab" means "a citizenship". It is built from "en stat" (a state) and "en borger" (a citizen). To say you apply for it, use "at ansøge om" (to apply for): "Han ansøger om dansk statsborgerskab" (He is applying for Danish citizenship).

sentence.da: Hun fik dansk **statsborgerskab**, efter hun havde boet her i ni år.
sentence.en: She got Danish citizenship after she had lived here for nine years.

et stearinlys.explanation: "Et stearinlys" means "a candle". It is built from "stearin" (candle wax) and "lys" (light).

sentence.da: Hun tænder et **stearinlys**, når det bliver mørkt.
sentence.en: She lights a candle when it gets dark.

et sted.explanation: "Et sted" means "a place". To say you saw something somewhere, use "et sted": "Jeg har set det et sted" (I have seen it somewhere). To say somewhere else, add "andet" (other): "Vi kan spise et andet sted" (We can eat somewhere else).

sentence.da: Er der et **sted** at spise her?
sentence.en: Is there a place to eat here?

et stedord.explanation: "Et stedord" means "a pronoun". It is built from "et sted" (a place) and "et ord" (a word), so it is literally a place word.

sentence.da: Et **stedord** som han eller hun står i stedet for et navn.
sentence.en: A pronoun like he or she stands in place of a name.

et stik.explanation: "Et stik" means "a plug", as in the electrical plug on a cord. When a needle or an insect pricks you, it means "a sting": "Et stik fra en bi gør ondt" (A sting from a bee hurts). To say you pull the plug out of the wall, use "at trække stikket ud" (to pull the plug out): "Træk stikket ud" (Pull the plug out).

sentence.da: Sæt dit **stik** i væggen, så virker lampen.
sentence.en: Put your plug in the wall and the lamp works.

et stillads.explanation: "Et stillads" means "scaffolding". To say workers are putting it up, use "at rejse" (to put up): "De rejser stillads om huset" (They are putting up scaffolding around the house).

sentence.da: Malerne står på et **stillads**, når de maler husets facade.
sentence.en: The painters stand on scaffolding when they paint the front of the house.

et sting.explanation: "Et sting" means "a stitch", as in one loop of thread in sewing. To say you have a pain in your side from running, use "sidestik" (side stitch) instead: "Jeg har sidestik" (I have a stitch in my side).

sentence.da: Lægen lukkede såret med fem **sting**.
sentence.en: The doctor closed the wound with five stitches.

et stipendium.explanation: "Et stipendium" means "a scholarship". To say you apply for one, use "at søge" (to apply for): "Hun søger et stipendium" (She is applying for a scholarship).

sentence.da: Hun fik et **stipendium** og kunne studere i udlandet.
sentence.en: She got a scholarship and could study abroad.

et stof.explanation: "Et stof" means "a fabric". When you talk about cloth for sewing, it means "a fabric": "Stoffet er blødt" (The fabric is soft). When you talk about a chemical or a drug, it means "a substance": "Det er et farligt stof" (It is a dangerous substance).

sentence.da: Jeg vil sy en kjole af dette **stof**.
sentence.en: I want to sew a dress from this fabric.

et stoppested.explanation: "Et stoppested" means "a stop", as in where a bus or train stops. It is built from "at stoppe" (to stop) and "et sted" (a place). To say a bus stop, put "bus" in front: "et busstoppested" (a bus stop).

sentence.da: Næste **stoppested** er banegården.
sentence.en: The next stop is the railway station.

et storindkøb.explanation: "Et storindkøb" means "a big grocery shop". It is built from "stor" (big) and "indkøb" (a purchase). To say you go grocery shopping, use "at købe ind" (to shop): "Vi skal købe ind i aften" (We are going grocery shopping tonight).

sentence.da: Vi laver et **storindkøb** i supermarkedet hver lørdag.
sentence.en: We do a big grocery shop at the supermarket every Saturday.

et stormagasin.explanation: "Et stormagasin" means "a department store". It is built from "stor" (big) and "et magasin" (a store).

sentence.da: I et **stormagasin** kan man købe tøj, sko og køkkenudstyr.
sentence.en: In a department store, you can buy clothes, shoes and kitchenware.

et straffespark.explanation: "Et straffespark" means "a penalty kick". It is built from "en straf" (a punishment) and "et spark" (a kick). To say a player scores from one, use "at score på" (to score from): "Han scorer på straffespark" (He scores from a penalty kick).

sentence.da: Dommeren gav et **straffespark**, fordi forsvareren trak i trøjen.
sentence.en: The referee gave a penalty kick because the defender pulled the shirt.

et strygebræt.explanation: "Et strygebræt" means "an ironing board". It is built from "at stryge" (to iron) and "et bræt" (a board). The same "bræt" is in "et skærebræt" (a cutting board).

sentence.da: Hun stryger skjorten på et **strygebræt**.
sentence.en: She irons the shirt on an ironing board.

et strygejern.explanation: "Et strygejern" means "an iron", as in the one for clothes. It is built from "at stryge" (to iron) and "jern" (the metal iron), so literally it is an ironing iron.

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **strygejern** til skjorten.
sentence.en: I use an iron on the shirt.

et strømstik.explanation: "Et strømstik" means "a power plug". It is built from "strøm" (electric power) and "et stik" (a plug). To say you unplug something, use "at trække stikket ud" (to pull the plug out): "Træk stikket ud" (Pull the plug out).

sentence.da: Der sidder et **strømstik** for enden af ledningen.
sentence.en: There is a power plug at the end of the cord.

et studie.explanation: "Et studie" means "a study", as in a piece of research. To say a university study program, use "et studium" (a study program) instead: "Hendes studium tager fem år" (Her study program takes five years).

sentence.da: Et nyt **studie** viser, at søvn er vigtig for hukommelsen.
sentence.en: A new study shows that sleep is important for memory.

et studiejob.explanation: "Et studiejob" means "a student job". It is built from "et studie" (a study) and "et job" (a job). To say you work next to your studies, use "ved siden af" (next to): "Jeg har et studiejob ved siden af studiet" (I have a student job next to my studies).

sentence.da: Han har et **studiejob** på et advokatkontor to dage om ugen.
sentence.en: He has a student job at a law office two days a week.

et studiekort.explanation: "Et studiekort" means "a student card". It is built from "et studie" (a study) and "et kort" (a card). "Kort" also appears in "et kreditkort" (a credit card).

sentence.da: Med dit **studiekort** får du rabat på toget.
sentence.en: With your student card, you get a discount on the train.

et studielån.explanation: "Et studielån" means "a student loan". In Denmark, "SU" is the monthly support from the state for students, and you can take a "studielån" on top of it.

sentence.da: Mange unge optager et **studielån** for at betale husleje.
sentence.en: Many young people take out a student loan to pay rent.
