et studieår.explanation: "Et studieår" means "an academic year". It is built from "et studie" (a study) and "et år" (a year). To say which year you are in, use "i sit" (in your): "Han er i sit andet studieår" (He is in his second academic year).

sentence.da: Det første **studieår** er ofte det sværeste.
sentence.en: The first academic year is often the hardest.

et studium.explanation: "Et studium" means "a study program". Its form "studiet" is the same as for "et studie" (a study), so "studiet" can mean either "the study program" or "the study". To say a piece of research, use "et studie": "Studiet bygger på 500 personer" (The study is based on 500 people).

sentence.da: Hendes **studium** tager fem år og slutter med en kandidatgrad.
sentence.en: Her study program takes five years and ends with a master's degree.

et stykke.explanation: "Et stykke" means "a piece". To name what the piece is of, put it after: "et stykke papir" (a piece of paper). When you give a price for each item, put "stykket" (the piece) after the amount: "ti kroner stykket" (ten kroner each).

sentence.da: Må jeg få et **stykke** kage?
sentence.en: May I have a piece of cake?

et stød.explanation: "Et stød" means "a shock or jolt". When you talk about bad news, it means "a shock": "Nyheden var et stød" (The news was a shock). When you talk about a sudden bump, it means "a jolt": "Bilen fik et stød bagfra" (The car got a jolt from behind). In Danish pronunciation, "stød" is also the name of a short catch in the voice in some words.

sentence.da: Jeg fik et **stød**, da jeg rørte ved ledningen.
sentence.en: I got a shock when I touched the wire.

et støtteparti.explanation: "Et støtteparti" means "a supporting party". It is built from "at støtte" (to support) and "et parti" (a party). In Denmark, the parliament is called "Folketinget", and a government without a majority there can rely on a supporting party.

sentence.da: Regeringen har brug for et **støtteparti**, fordi den ikke har flertal.
sentence.en: The government needs a supporting party because it does not have a majority.

et sugerør.explanation: "Et sugerør" means "a drinking straw". It is built from "at suge" (to suck) and "et rør" (a tube).

sentence.da: Hun drikker sin juice med **sugerør**.
sentence.en: She drinks her juice with a straw.

et suk.explanation: "Et suk" means "a sigh". The matching verb is "at sukke" (to sigh). To say someone sighs, use the verb: "Han sukker højt" (He sighs loudly).

sentence.da: Hun udstødte et **suk** af lettelse, da eksamen var slut.
sentence.en: She let out a sigh of relief when the exam was over.

et sundhedskort.explanation: "Et sundhedskort" means "a health insurance card". It is built from "sundhed" (health) and "et kort" (a card). "Kort" also appears in "et kreditkort" (a credit card).

sentence.da: Du skal vise dit **sundhedskort** hos lægen.
sentence.en: You have to show your health insurance card at the doctor.

et supermarked.explanation: "Et supermarked" means "a supermarket". It is built from "super" (super) and "et marked" (a market). "Marked" is also the word for a market or fair, as in "et julemarked" (a Christmas market).

sentence.da: Et **supermarked** sælger mad og mange andre ting.
sentence.en: A supermarket sells food and many other things.

et svar.explanation: "Et svar" means "an answer". To thank someone for replying, say: "Tak for svaret" (Thanks for the reply).

sentence.da: Hun giver et **svar** på spørgsmålet.
sentence.en: She gives an answer to the question.

et svigt.explanation: "Et svigt" means "a betrayal or letdown". In the word "hjertesvigt" (heart failure), "svigt" means something stops working as it should.

sentence.da: Det var et stort **svigt**, at han ikke holdt sit løfte.
sentence.en: It was a big letdown that he did not keep his promise.

et svin.explanation: "Et svin" means "a pig". Calling a person "et svin" is rude: "Han er et svin" (He is a swine). To talk about the meat, add "kød" (meat): "svinekød" (pork).

sentence.da: Bonden har mange **svin** på gården.
sentence.en: The farmer has many pigs on the farm.

et sving.explanation: "Et sving" means "a turn or curve". To tell someone which turn to take when driving, use "at tage" (to take): "Tag første sving til højre" (Take the first turn on the right).

sentence.da: Pas på, der er et skarpt **sving** forude.
sentence.en: Be careful, there is a sharp curve ahead.

et sværd.explanation: "Et sværd" means "a sword". The word "sværd" also appears in "en sværdfisk" (a swordfish).

sentence.da: Ridderen trak sit **sværd** og stillede sig foran slottet.
sentence.en: The knight drew his sword and stood in front of the castle.

et sygehus.explanation: "Et sygehus" means "a hospital". It is built from "syg" (sick) and "et hus" (a house). "Et hospital" is another word for it.

sentence.da: Lægen og sygeplejerskerne arbejder på et **sygehus**.
sentence.en: The doctor and the nurses work at a hospital.

et symbol.explanation: "Et symbol" means "a symbol". To say something is used as a symbol, use "som symbol for" (as a symbol of): "Duen bruges som symbol for fred" (The dove is used as a symbol of peace).

sentence.da: Hjertet er et **symbol** på kærlighed.
sentence.en: The heart is a symbol of love.

et symptom.explanation: "Et symptom" means "a symptom". To say you feel no signs of illness, use "at have" (to have): "Jeg har ingen symptomer" (I have no symptoms). When you mean a sign of a problem in general, use it for the problem: "Støjen er et symptom på noget større" (The noise is a symptom of something bigger).

sentence.da: Feber er et almindeligt **symptom** på influenza.
sentence.en: A fever is a common symptom of the flu.

et syn.explanation: "Et syn" means "a sight or vision". When you talk about something you see, it means "a sight": "Det var et smukt syn" (It was a beautiful sight). When you talk about your ability to see, it means "vision": "Mit syn er blevet dårligere" (My vision has become worse).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar har dårligt **syn** og bruger briller.
sentence.en: My grandfather has bad eyesight and wears glasses.

et synonym.explanation: "Et synonym" means "a synonym". To ask for another word with the same meaning, say: "Kender du et synonym for glad?" (Do you know a synonym for happy?) The opposite is "et antonym" (an antonym): "Stor og lille er antonymer" (Big and small are antonyms).

sentence.da: Et **synonym** for glad er lykkelig.
sentence.en: A synonym for happy is joyful.

et synspunkt.explanation: "Et synspunkt" means "a viewpoint". To say you understand how someone sees something, use "forstå" (to understand): "Jeg forstår dit synspunkt" (I understand your viewpoint). Do not mix it up with "et standpunkt" (a position), the opinion you have decided on: "Det er mit standpunkt" (That is my position).

sentence.da: Det er et interessant **synspunkt**, men jeg er uenig.
sentence.en: That is an interesting viewpoint, but I disagree.

et system.explanation: "Et system" means "a system". To say you have a system for doing something, use "til" (for): "Vi har et system til at sortere affald" (We have a system for sorting waste).

sentence.da: Et **system** hjælper os med at holde orden.
sentence.en: A system helps us keep things in order.

et sår.explanation: "Et sår" means "a wound". When you talk about a sore in the mouth, it means "a sore": "Jeg har et sår i munden" (I have a sore in my mouth).

sentence.da: Jeg har et **sår** på mit knæ.
sentence.en: I have a wound on my knee.

et sæde.explanation: "Et sæde" means "a seat", as in a place to sit. To name a chair in a room, use "en stol" (a chair): "Der står en stol ved bordet" (There is a chair at the table).

sentence.da: Der er et ledigt **sæde** ved vinduet.
sentence.en: There is a free seat by the window.

et sølvbryllup.explanation: "Et sølvbryllup" means "a silver wedding anniversary". It is built from "sølv" (silver) and "et bryllup" (a wedding). To say the 50-year anniversary, use "et guldbryllup" (a golden wedding): "De holder guldbryllup i dag" (They are celebrating their golden wedding today).

sentence.da: Mine forældre holder **sølvbryllup**, fordi de har været gift i 25 år.
sentence.en: My parents are celebrating their silver wedding because they have been married for 25 years.

et søm.explanation: "Et søm" means "a nail". To say a screw that you turn in, use "en skrue" (a screw): "Jeg skruer en skrue i planken" (I screw a screw into the board). The word "søm" also means a seam in clothes, and then it takes "en": "Sømmen på bukserne er gået op" (The seam of the trousers has come apart).

sentence.da: Jeg hænger billedet op med et **søm**.
sentence.en: I hang the picture up with a nail.

saft.explanation: "Saft" means "a cordial". To say you dilute it, use "at blande" (to mix): "Jeg blander saft med koldt vand" (I mix cordial with cold water). Do not mix it up with "en juice" (a juice): "Jeg drikker en juice til morgenmad" (I drink a juice with breakfast).

sentence.da: **Saft** laves af frugt og er meget sød.
sentence.en: Cordial is made from fruit and is very sweet.

saftevand.explanation: "Saftevand" means "diluted cordial". It is built from "saft" (cordial) and "vand" (water). To offer a choice of drinks, say: "Vil du have saftevand eller mælk?" (Do you want diluted cordial or milk?)

sentence.da: **Saftevand** er saft blandet med vand.
sentence.en: Diluted cordial is cordial mixed with water.

sagtens.explanation: "Sagtens" means "easily". Use it with "kan" or "kunne" (can, could) to say that something is no problem for you: "Det kan jeg sagtens" (I can easily do that).

forms.da: Det kan sagtens lade sig gøre

sentence.da: Du kan **sagtens** nå toget, hvis du skynder dig.
sentence.en: You can easily catch the train if you hurry.

salt.explanation: "Salt" means "salt". To ask for some, use "noget" (some) and no article: "Kan jeg få noget salt?" (Can I have some salt?) When you talk about taste, it means "salty": "Suppen er for salt" (The soup is too salty).

sentence.da: Der er meget **salt** i havet.
sentence.en: There is a lot of salt in the sea.

saltet.explanation: "Saltet" means "salted". To say food has had salt added, use it before the noun: "saltet smør" (salted butter). "Saltet" is also "the salt": "Giv mig saltet" (Pass me the salt). Do not mix it up with "salt" (salty), a taste: "Suppen er for salt" (The soup is too salty).

sentence.da: Fisken er **saltet** og smager af salt.
sentence.en: The fish is salted and tastes of salt.

samfundsfag.explanation: "Et samfundsfag" means "a social studies subject". It is built from "et samfund" (a society) and "et fag" (a subject). To say you are good at it, use "god til" (good at): "Hun er god til samfundsfag" (She is good at social studies).

sentence.da: I **samfundsfag** lærer vi, hvordan et valg fungerer.
sentence.en: In social studies we learn how an election works.

samme.explanation: "Samme" means "same". To say something happens on the same day, put it before the noun: "samme dag" (the same day). To say "the same man", put "den", "det" or "de" (all three mean "the") before it: "den samme mand" (the same man). To answer a greeting with "you too", say "Det samme!" (The same!): "God weekend!" - "Det samme!" (Have a good weekend! - You too!)

sentence.da: Vi har den **samme** bil.
sentence.en: We have the same car.

sammen.explanation: "Sammen" means "together". To say people do something together, put it after the verb: "Vi spiser sammen" (We eat together). The opposite is "alene" (alone): "Jeg spiser alene" (I eat alone). To greet a group, use "alle sammen" (everyone): "Hej alle sammen!" (Hello everyone!)

sentence.da: Min ven og jeg bor **sammen**.
sentence.en: My friend and I live together.

sammenhold.explanation: "Et sammenhold" means "togetherness". It comes from "at holde sammen" (to stick together). To say something creates togetherness, use "at skabe" (to create): "Fælles spisning skaber sammenhold" (Eating together creates togetherness).

sentence.da: I vores klasse er der et stærkt **sammenhold**, og alle hjælper hinanden.
sentence.en: In our class there is strong togetherness, and everyone helps each other.

sammenhængende.explanation: "Sammenhængende" means "coherent". It comes from "at hænge sammen" (to hang together). To say a text hangs together, use it before the noun: "en sammenhængende tekst" (a coherent text). The opposite is "usammenhængende" (disconnected): "Hans svar var usammenhængende" (His answer was disconnected).

sentence.da: Hendes fortælling var **sammenhængende**, så alle kunne følge med.
sentence.en: Her story was coherent, so everyone could follow.

sammenhængskraft.explanation: "En sammenhængskraft" means "social cohesion". It is built from "sammenhæng" (connection) and "kraft" (strength). "Kraft" also appears in "et kraftværk" (a power plant).

sentence.da: Fælles regler og værdier styrker samfundets **sammenhængskraft**.
sentence.en: Shared rules and values strengthen society's social cohesion.

sammenlignelig.explanation: "Sammenlignelig" means "comparable". To say what something is compared to, add "med" (with): "Hans løn er sammenlignelig med min" (His pay is comparable to mine).

sentence.da: Prisen er **sammenlignelig** med prisen i de andre butikker.
sentence.en: The price is comparable to the price in the other stores.

sammensat.explanation: "Sammensat" means "composite". To say a word is made of two words, use it before the noun: "et sammensat ord" (a compound word). When a problem has many parts, it means "complex": "Det er et sammensat problem" (It is a complex problem). To say something is hard, use "kompliceret" (complicated): "en kompliceret regel" (a complicated rule).

sentence.da: Håndklæde er et **sammensat** ord af hånd og klæde.
sentence.en: Håndklæde (towel) is a compound word made of hand and cloth.

samt.explanation: "Samt" means "as well as". To join the last item of a list, put it before that item: "Kaffe, te samt kage" (Coffee, tea as well as cake). To say simply "and", use "og" (and): "Kaffe og kage" (Coffee and cake).

sentence.da: Husk at tage pas **samt** billet med til lufthavnen.
sentence.en: Remember to take your passport as well as your ticket to the airport.

samtidig.explanation: "Samtidig" means "at the same time". To say two things happen together, put it after the verb: "De kom samtidig" (They arrived at the same time). To name the other event, add "med" (with): "samtidig med mødet" (at the same time as the meeting).

forms.en: They arrived at the same time.
She laughed and cried at the same time.
At the same time, it is cheap.

sentence.da: Han taler og spiser **samtidig**.
sentence.en: He talks and eats at the same time.

samtlige.explanation: "Samtlige" means "all", and stresses that none are left out: "samtlige elever" (every single student). To say simply "all", use "alle" (all): "Alle elever er her" (All the students are here).

sentence.da: **Samtlige** elever skal aflevere opgaven inden fredag.
sentence.en: All the students must hand in the assignment before Friday.

sand.explanation: "Sand" means "sand". The adjective "sand" (true) is spelled the same. To say something is true, use "sandt" with "det" (it): "Det er sandt" (That is true).

sentence.da: På stranden er der meget **sand**.
sentence.en: There is a lot of sand on the beach.

sandaler.explanation: "Sandaler" means "sandals". To talk about only one, use "en sandal" (a sandal): "Jeg mistede en sandal" (I lost a sandal).

sentence.da: Om sommeren går jeg i **sandaler**.
sentence.en: In summer I wear sandals.

sandelig.explanation: "Sandelig" means "indeed". It comes from "sand" (true). To add emphasis to a statement, put it after the verb: "Det var sandelig dejligt" (That was indeed lovely).

forms.da: Det er jeg sandelig ikke enig i.
forms.en: I truly do not agree with that.

sentence.da: Det var **sandelig** en lang dag, men vi klarede den.
sentence.en: It was indeed a long day, but we made it.

sandsynlig.explanation: "Sandsynlig" means "likely". It is built from "sand" (true) and "synlig" (visible). To say something is likely to happen, use "sandsynligt" with "det" (it) and "at": "Det er sandsynligt, at det regner" (It is likely that it will rain).

sentence.da: Regn er **sandsynlig**, fordi himlen er mørk.
sentence.en: Rain is likely because the sky is dark.

sandsynligvis.explanation: "Sandsynligvis" means "probably". It is built from "sandsynlig" (likely). To answer a question with "probably not", say: "Kommer han?" - "Sandsynligvis ikke." (Is he coming? - Probably not.)

sentence.da: Det bliver **sandsynligvis** koldt i morgen.
sentence.en: It will probably be cold tomorrow.

sankthans.explanation: "Sankthans" means "Midsummer". It is written together from "Sankt Hans" (Saint John). In Denmark, people light a bonfire on the evening of 23 June and sing "Midsommervisen" (the Midsummer song).

sentence.da: Til **sankthans** tænder vi et stort bål ved stranden.
sentence.en: At Midsummer we light a big fire on the beach.

sarkastisk.explanation: "Sarkastisk" means "sarcastic". To say something nice about something bad, as a joke, speak in a flat voice: "Dejligt, det regner igen!" (Lovely, it is raining again!)

sentence.da: Han svarede **sarkastisk**, at det var en fantastisk idé.
sentence.en: He answered sarcastically that it was a fantastic idea.

sej.explanation: "Sej" means "cool". When you talk about a strong person who does not give up, it means "tough": "Hun er sej" (She is tough). When you talk about food that is hard to chew, it means "tough": "sejt kød" (tough meat).

sentence.da: Han er **sej** og giver aldrig op.
sentence.en: He is tough and never gives up.

sejlads.explanation: "En sejlads" means "a sailing trip". It comes from "at sejle" (to sail), which is used for any trip by ship or boat: "Vi sejler med færgen til Bornholm" (We take the ferry to Bornholm).

sentence.da: På en lang **sejlads** over havet kan man ikke se land.
sentence.en: On a long sailing trip across the sea you cannot see land.

seks.explanation: "Seks" means "six". English speakers may write it with "x", but it is spelled with "ks": "seks børn" (six children). To say someone's age, use it before "år" (years): "Hun er seks år" (She is six years old).

sentence.da: To gange tre er **seks**.
sentence.en: Two times three is six.

seksten.explanation: "Seksten" means "sixteen". To tell it apart from "seks" (six), note the difference between "seks børn" (six children) and "seksten børn" (sixteen children).

sentence.da: Ti plus seks er **seksten**.
sentence.en: Ten plus six is sixteen.

seksuel.explanation: "Seksuel" means "sexual". To say sexy, use "sexet" (sexy) instead: "en sexet kjole" (a sexy dress).

sentence.da: Skolen har undervisning om **seksuel** sundhed og beskyttelse.
sentence.en: The school has teaching about sexual health and protection.

selleri.explanation: "Selleri" means "celery". To name the green stalks, use "stangselleri" (celery stalks). To name the round root, use "knoldselleri" (celeriac).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer **selleri** og gulerod til suppen.
sentence.en: I cut celery and carrot for the soup.

selv.explanation: "Selv" means "myself". To say you do something without help, put it after the verb: "Jeg gør det selv" (I do it myself). It stays the same for every person: "Hun gør det selv" (She does it herself). When it starts a sentence, it means "even": "Selv børn kan det" (Even children can do it).

sentence.da: Jeg laver maden **selv**.
sentence.en: I make the food myself.

selv tak.explanation: "Selv tak" means "you're welcome". Literally, it means "thanks yourself". To answer someone who thanks you for help, say: "Tak for hjælpen." - "Selv tak." (Thanks for the help. - You're welcome.) When someone thanks you for last night, it also returns the thanks: "Tak for i aftes." - "Selv tak." (Thanks for last night. - Thanks to you too.)

forms.en: Thanks for the help. - You're welcome.

forms.da: Tak for i aftes. - Selv tak.
forms.en: Thanks for last night. - Thanks to you too.

sentence.da: "Tak for hjælpen!" - "**Selv tak**!"
sentence.en: "Thanks for the help!" - "You're welcome!"

selvforsvar.explanation: "Et selvforsvar" means "self-defense". It is built from "selv" (self) and "et forsvar" (a defense). In law, use "nødværge" (legal self-defense) instead: "Han handlede i nødværge" (He acted in self-defense).

sentence.da: I **selvforsvar** lærer man at slippe fri, hvis nogen griber fat i en.
sentence.en: In self-defense you learn to get free if someone grabs hold of you.

selvfølgelig.explanation: "Selvfølgelig" means "of course". To agree to a request right away, answer with it: "Kan du hjælpe mig?" "Selvfølgelig!" (Can you help me? Of course!) To say something happened as expected, put it inside the sentence: "Hun kommer selvfølgelig for sent" (Of course she is going to be late).

sentence.da: "Må jeg låne din bog?" - "**Selvfølgelig**!"
sentence.en: "May I borrow your book?" - "Of course!"

selvglad.explanation: "Selvglad" means "smug". It is built from "selv" (self) and "glad" (happy), so it is literally "happy with oneself". To say you are pleased with your own work in a good way, use "tilfreds" (satisfied): "Jeg er tilfreds med min indsats" (I am satisfied with my effort).

sentence.da: Han er så **selvglad**, at han aldrig lytter til andre.
sentence.en: He is so smug that he never listens to others.

selvmodsigende.explanation: "Selvmodsigende" means "contradictory". It is built from "selv" (self) and "at modsige" (to contradict), so it contradicts itself. To say that an explanation does not agree with itself: "Hans forklaring er selvmodsigende" (His explanation is contradictory).

sentence.da: Reglen er **selvmodsigende**, fordi den både tillader og forbyder det.
sentence.en: The rule is contradictory, because it both allows and forbids it.

selvom.explanation: "Selvom" means "even though". To say something happens in spite of a fact, put it before the fact: "Jeg går en tur, selvom det regner" (I am going for a walk even though it is raining). To give just the noun instead of a whole clause, use "på trods af" (despite): "Jeg går en tur på trods af regnen" (I am going for a walk despite the rain).

forms.en: even though he does not know

sentence.da: Jeg løber, **selvom** jeg er meget træt.
sentence.en: I am running even though I am very tired.

selvsikker.explanation: "Selvsikker" means "confident". It is built from "selv" (self) and "sikker" (sure). "Selv" also begins other words, such as "selvstændig" (independent).

sentence.da: Hun er **selvsikker** og taler højt foran alle.
sentence.en: She is confident and speaks loudly in front of everyone.

selvstændig.explanation: "Selvstændig" means "independent". When you say a grown person runs their own business, it means "self-employed": "Min søster er selvstændig" (My sister is self-employed).

sentence.da: Hun vil være **selvstændig** og åbne sin egen frisørsalon.
sentence.en: She wants to be self-employed and open her own hair salon.

selvstændighed.explanation: "Selvstændighed" means "independence". It is built from "selvstændig" (independent) and the ending "-hed", which makes a noun. To say a person learns to manage alone: "Børn lærer selvstændighed" (Children learn independence). To say a country wants to be free: "Landet kæmper for sin selvstændighed" (The country is fighting for its independence).

sentence.da: Mange unge flytter hjemmefra for at få **selvstændighed**.
sentence.en: Many young people move out to gain independence.

selvtillid.explanation: "Selvtillid" means "self-confidence". It is built from "selv" (self) and "tillid" (trust). To say someone is missing self-confidence: "Han mangler selvtillid" (He lacks self-confidence).

sentence.da: Hun har stor **selvtillid** og er aldrig bange.
sentence.en: She has great self-confidence and is never afraid.

senere.explanation: "Senere" means "later". To say later on the same day: "senere i dag" (later today). Do not mix it up with "sent" (late in time): "Det er sent" (It is late).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til dig **senere**.
sentence.en: I will call you later.

seneste.explanation: "Seneste" means "latest". To talk about the newest thing someone made: "Har du set hans seneste film?" (Have you seen his latest movie?) To talk about the recent past: "de seneste uger" (the last few weeks). To talk about the final one in a row, use "sidste" (last): "Det er den sidste bus" (It is the last bus).

sentence.da: Har du hørt den **seneste** nyhed?
sentence.en: Have you heard the latest news?

sengetid.explanation: "Sengetid" means "bedtime". It is built from "seng" (bed) and "tid" (time). "Tid" also ends other words for set times, such as "spisetid" (mealtime).

sentence.da: Nu er det **sengetid**, og børnene er trætte.
sentence.en: Now it is bedtime, and the kids are tired.

sennep.explanation: "Sennep" means "mustard". When you talk about mustard in general, leave out "en": "Vil du have sennep på?" (Do you want mustard on it?) To say a small amount, use "en klat sennep" (a dollop of mustard).

sentence.da: Pølsen smager godt med ketchup og **sennep**.
sentence.en: The sausage tastes good with ketchup and mustard.

sensitiv.explanation: "Sensitiv" means "sensitive", for skin, teeth or a child who reacts easily. "Følsom" also means "sensitive" and is used for feelings: "Han er meget følsom" (He is very sensitive).

sentence.da: Hun bruger en mild creme, fordi hendes hud er **sensitiv**.
sentence.en: She uses a mild cream because her skin is sensitive.

sent.explanation: "Sent" means "late". To say you arrived after the expected time: "Vi kom sent" (We came late). Do not mix it up with "senere" (later): "Vi kommer senere" (We will come later). To say you are too late, use "for sent": "Jeg kommer for sent" (I am coming too late).

sentence.da: Vi kommer **sent** hjem i dag.
sentence.en: We come home late today.

september.explanation: "September" means "September". In Danish, month names are not capitalized. To say something happens in that month: "Vi rejser i september" (We travel in September).

sentence.da: Børnene starter i skole igen i **september**.
sentence.en: The children start school again in September.

seriøs.explanation: "Seriøs" means "serious". To ask whether someone is not joking: "Er du seriøs?" (Are you serious?)

sentence.da: Han er meget **seriøs** og laver aldrig sjov.
sentence.en: He is very serious and never jokes.

ses i morgen.explanation: "Ses i morgen" means "see you tomorrow". "Ses" is short for "vi ses" (we see each other). To say you will meet that evening instead, change the time: "Ses i aften" (See you tonight).

forms.en: Will we see each other tomorrow?

sentence.da: Jeg skal hjem nu. **Ses i morgen**!
sentence.en: I am going home now. See you tomorrow!

sexet.explanation: "Sexet" means "sexy". English speakers should note that it ends in "-et", not "-y". To describe a car: "Bilen er sexet" (The car is sexy).

sentence.da: Hun har en **sexet** kjole på.
sentence.en: She is wearing a sexy dress.

shampoo.explanation: "Shampoo" means "shampoo" and is spelled the same as in English. It takes "en" ("shampooen" is the form with "the"), but when you talk about some shampoo, leave out "en": "Har du noget shampoo?" (Do you have any shampoo?) To count it by the bottle: "en flaske shampoo" (a bottle of shampoo).

sentence.da: Jeg vasker mit hår med **shampoo**.
sentence.en: I wash my hair with shampoo.

shorts.explanation: "Shorts" means "shorts". Danish treats it as plural, as English does. To talk about one pair, say "et par shorts" (a pair of shorts): "Mine shorts er nye" (My shorts are new).

sentence.da: Jeg har **shorts** og T-shirt på.
sentence.en: I am wearing shorts and a T-shirt.

siddende.explanation: "Siddende" means "seated". It comes from the verb "at sidde" (to sit). When you talk about whoever holds an office right now, it means "sitting": "den siddende regering" (the sitting government).

sentence.da: Den **siddende** mand ved vinduet læste en bog.
sentence.en: The seated man by the window was reading a book.

siden.explanation: "Siden" means "since". To say when something began, name the time after it: "siden i går" (since yesterday). It also means "ago". To say how long before now, put it last: "for to år siden" (two years ago).

sentence.da: Jeg har boet her **siden** 2020.
sentence.en: I have lived here since 2020.

sidenhen.explanation: "Sidenhen" means "since then". It is built from "siden" (since). To say how things changed after a moment in the past: "Han var genert som barn, men sidenhen er han blevet mere åben" (He was shy as a child, but since then he has become more open).

forms.en: and later on he became a doctor

sentence.da: Vi mødtes i 2010, og **sidenhen** har vi været venner.
sentence.en: We met in 2010, and since then we have been friends.

sidst.explanation: "Sidst" means "last". To say "the last time", use "sidste" before the noun: "Det var sidste gang" (That was the last time).

sentence.da: Han kom **sidst** til festen.
sentence.en: He came last to the party.

sidste.explanation: "Sidste" means "last". To point to the final one before a noun: "den sidste bus" (the last bus). To name a recent period of time: "sidste uge" (last week). To say you came after everyone else, use "sidst": "Jeg kom sidst" (I came last).

sentence.da: Det er den **sidste** bus i dag.
sentence.en: It is the last bus today.

sig.explanation: "Sig" means "himself". It also means "herself", "itself" and "themselves". When the person doing the action and the person receiving it are the same, use "sig": "Han vasker sig" (He washes himself). When they are two different people, use "ham" (him): "Han vasker ham" (He washes him). Some verbs always go with "sig". To say you look forward to something, use "at glæde sig": "Børnene glæder sig til jul" (The children look forward to Christmas).

forms.en: She is looking forward to it.

sentence.da: Han vasker **sig** hver morgen.
sentence.en: He washes himself every morning.

sikke.explanation: "Sikke" means "what a" and starts an exclamation. With a word that takes "en", say: "Sikke en overraskelse!" (What a surprise!) With a word that takes "et", say: "Sikke et vejr!" (What weather!)

sentence.da: Åh, **sikke** en flot hund du har!
sentence.en: Oh, what a nice dog you have!

sikke en dag.explanation: "Sikke en dag" means "what a day". To react to a day that was hard, say: "Sikke en dag! Jeg er helt udmattet." (What a day! I am completely worn out.) "Sikke en" goes before a word that takes "en". Before a word that takes "et", use "sikke et": "Sikke et vejr!" (What weather!)

forms.da: Sikke en dag, alt gik galt!
forms.en: What a day, everything went wrong!

sentence.da: **Sikke en dag**, vi vandt hele turneringen!
sentence.en: What a day, we won the whole tournament!

sikke noget.explanation: "Sikke noget" means "wow". To react to something that surprised you, add the thing you noticed: "Sikke noget vejr!" (What weather!)

sentence.da: **Sikke noget** rod, der er mel overalt!
sentence.en: What a mess, there is flour everywhere!

sikker.explanation: "Sikker" means "safe". To say something cannot hurt you: "Cyklen er sikker" (The bike is safe). When you have no doubt, it means "sure": "Er du sikker?" (Are you sure?)

sentence.da: Jeg er helt **sikker** på det.
sentence.en: I am completely sure about it.

sikkerhed.explanation: "Sikkerhed" means "security", as in being protected from harm. It is built from "sikker" (safe) and the ending "-hed", which makes a noun. To say you know something for sure, use "med sikkerhed": "Jeg ved det med sikkerhed" (I know it for sure).

sentence.da: Bilbælter giver **sikkerhed** i trafikken.
sentence.en: Seat belts give safety in traffic.

sild.explanation: "Sild" means "herring". The plural is the same word. To name herring in a marinade, say: "marineret sild" (pickled herring).

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser vi **sild** på rugbrød.
sentence.en: For lunch we eat herring on rye bread.

silke.explanation: "Silke" means "silk". When you talk about the material, use it without an article: "Jeg elsker silke" (I love silk). When it starts a longer word, it names what something is made of: "et silketørklæde" (a silk scarf).

sentence.da: Hendes kjole er lavet af **silke**.
sentence.en: Her dress is made of silk.

simpel.explanation: "Simpel" means "simple". To describe a house with nothing extra: "Det er et simpelt hus" (It is a plain house).

sentence.da: Det er en **simpel** opgave, og børn kan klare den.
sentence.en: It is a simple task, and children can handle it.

simpelthen.explanation: "Simpelthen" means "simply". To add force to a statement, put it before the word it strengthens: "Jeg kan simpelthen ikke lide det" (I simply do not like it).

forms.en: I simply do not understand it

sentence.da: Det er **simpelthen** den bedste kage.
sentence.en: It is simply the best cake.

sin.explanation: "Sin" means "his own". It also means "her own" and "its own". It goes before a word that takes "en" and points back to the person doing the action: "Peter ser sin bror" (Peter sees his own brother). When the brother belongs to someone else, use "hans" (his): "Peter ser Jens og hans bror" (Peter sees Jens and Jens's brother). For "I" and "you", use "min" (my) and "din" (your): "Jeg ser min bror" (I see my brother).

sentence.da: Hun elsker **sin** hund.
sentence.en: She loves her (own) dog.

sindssyg.explanation: "Sindssyg" means "insane". It is built from "sind" (mind) and "syg" (sick). To say something is extremely good: "Det er sindssygt godt" (It is insanely good).

sentence.da: Det er en **sindssyg** idé, og den er farlig.
sentence.en: That is an insane idea, and it is dangerous.

sine.explanation: "Sine" means "his own". It also means "her own". It goes before more than one thing: "Peter ser sine venner" (Peter sees his own friends). When the friends belong to someone else, use "hans" (his): "Peter ser Jens og hans venner" (Peter sees Jens and Jens's friends). For one thing that takes "en", use "sin": "sin bror" (his own brother). For one thing that takes "et", use "sit": "sit hus" (his own house).

sentence.da: Hun ringer til **sine** forældre.
sentence.en: She calls her (own) parents.

single.explanation: "Single" means "single", as in not being in a relationship. It is spelled the same as in English. To say "just one" of something, use "enkelt": "en enkelt dag" (a single day).

sentence.da: Jeg er **single** og har tid til venner.
sentence.en: I am single and have time for friends.

sirup.explanation: "En sirup" means "a syrup". Do not mix it up with "saft" (fruit cordial, which you mix with water): "Vil du have saft?" (Do you want some cordial?)

sentence.da: **Sirup** er tyk og sød, og den passer til pandekager.
sentence.en: Syrup is thick and sweet, and it goes well with pancakes.

sit.explanation: "Sit" means "his own". It also means "her own" and "its own". It goes before a word that takes "et" and points back to the person doing the action: "Peter elsker sit hus" (Peter loves his own house). When the house belongs to someone else, use "hans" (his): "Peter ser Jens og hans hus" (Peter sees Jens and Jens's house). Before a word that takes "en", use "sin": "sin bil" (his own car).

sentence.da: Han passer på **sit** barn.
sentence.en: He looks after his (own) child.

sjette.explanation: "Sjette" means "sixth". English speakers might expect it to look like "seks" (six), but it is spelled "sjette", not "sekste". To give a date: "den sjette maj" (the sixth of May).

sentence.da: Efter femte sal kommer **sjette** sal.
sentence.en: After the fifth floor comes the sixth floor.

sjov.explanation: "Sjov" means "fun". To say you enjoyed something: "Det var sjovt" (That was fun). It also means "funny", for something that makes you laugh: "en sjov vittighed" (a funny joke). To say you did something as a joke: "Jeg gjorde det for sjov" (I did it as a joke).

sentence.da: Klovnen er **sjov** og alle ler.
sentence.en: The clown is funny and everyone laughs.

sjusket.explanation: "Sjusket" means "sloppy". To describe work done too fast: "Han lavede et sjusket stykke arbejde" (He did a sloppy job).

sentence.da: Rapporten er **sjusket**, og der er mange stavefejl i den.
sentence.en: The report is sloppy, and there are many spelling mistakes in it.

sjælden.explanation: "Sjælden" means "rare". To say a thing is hard to find: "Den bog er sjælden" (That book is rare). Do not mix it up with "sjældent" (rarely), which describes how seldom you do something: "Jeg ser ham sjældent" (I rarely see him).

sentence.da: Det er en **sjælden** fugl i Danmark.
sentence.en: It is a rare bird in Denmark.

sjældent.explanation: "Sjældent" means "rarely". To say you do something seldom: "Han kommer sjældent for sent" (He is rarely late). For something hard to find, use "sjælden": "Den bog er sjælden" (That book is rare).

sentence.da: Jeg ser **sjældent** min bror, fordi han bor langt væk.
sentence.en: I rarely see my brother because he lives far away.

skadelig.explanation: "Skadelig" means "harmful". It is built from "skade" (harm) and the ending "-lig". To say something damages your health: "skadelig for helbredet" (harmful to health).

sentence.da: Rygning er **skadelig** for både lungerne og hjertet.
sentence.en: Smoking is harmful to both the lungs and the heart.

skak.explanation: "Skak" means "chess". It has no article when you talk about the game: "Han er god til skak" (He is good at chess). In the game, shout "Skak!" (Check!) when the king is under attack. The game ends with "skak mat" (checkmate).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar spiller **skak** hver søndag.
sentence.en: My grandfather plays chess every Sunday.

skal vi ikke bare...?.explanation: "Skal vi ikke bare...?" means "shall we just...?". It is literally "shall we not just...?". To suggest the easy option: "Det regner. Skal vi ikke bare tage hjem?" (It is raining. Shall we just go home?)

forms.da: Skal vi ikke bare bestille pizza?

sentence.da: **Skal vi ikke bare** tage bussen i dag?
sentence.en: Shall we just take the bus today?

skaldet.explanation: "Skaldet" means "bald". To say a man is starting to lose his hair, use "ved at blive" (in the middle of becoming): "Han er ved at blive skaldet" (He is going bald).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er **skaldet**, men han har et pænt skæg.
sentence.en: My grandfather is bald, but he has a nice beard.

skaldyr.explanation: "Skaldyr" means "shellfish". It is built from "skal" (shell) and "dyr" (animal). To say you cannot eat shellfish because of an allergy: "Jeg er allergisk over for skaldyr" (I am allergic to shellfish). It has no article when you talk about shellfish in general.

forms.en: Is there shellfish in the dish?

sentence.da: Krabber og hummere er **skaldyr**.
sentence.en: Crabs and lobsters are shellfish.

skam.explanation: "Skam" means "shame". To say asking is nothing to be ashamed of: "Der er ingen skam i at spørge" (There is no shame in asking). It also means "a pity" in "en skam": "Det er en skam, at du ikke kan komme" (It is a pity that you cannot come).

sentence.da: Hun følte **skam**, fordi alle grinede af hende.
sentence.en: She felt shame because everyone laughed at her.

skamfuld.explanation: "Skamfuld" means "ashamed". It is built from "skam" (shame) and "fuld" (full), so it is literally "full of shame". To say what you are ashamed of, add "over" (about): "Jeg er skamfuld over, hvad jeg gjorde" (I am ashamed of what I did).

sentence.da: Han følte sig **skamfuld**, fordi han havde løjet for sin mor.
sentence.en: He felt ashamed because he had lied to his mother.

skandinavien.explanation: "Skandinavien" means "Scandinavia". Place names such as "Skandinavien" start with a big first letter in Danish, but "skandinavisk" (Scandinavian) does not. To include Finland and Iceland too, say "Norden" (the Nordic countries): "Island hører til Norden" (Iceland belongs to the Nordic countries).

sentence.da: Danmark ligger i **Skandinavien**.
sentence.en: Denmark is in Scandinavia.

skarp.explanation: "Skarp" means "sharp". To say a blade cuts well: "Kniven er skarp" (The knife is sharp). To say someone thinks quickly: "Hun er meget skarp" (She is very sharp).

sentence.da: Saksen er **skarp** og klipper papiret let.
sentence.en: The scissors are sharp and cut the paper easily.

skarpt.explanation: "Skarpt" means "sharply". To describe a cutting tone of voice: "Han svarede skarpt" (He answered sharply). To describe a sudden, steep turn: "Vejen drejer skarpt til højre" (The road turns sharply to the right). To say a thing itself is sharp, use "skarp": "Kniven er skarp" (The knife is sharp).

forms.en: to turn sharply to the right

sentence.da: Læreren talte **skarpt** til drengen, fordi han larmede.
sentence.en: The teacher spoke sharply to the boy because he was noisy.

skeptisk.explanation: "Skeptisk" means "skeptical". To say which idea you doubt, add "over for" (about): "Jeg er skeptisk over for planen" (I am skeptical about the plan).

sentence.da: Jeg er **skeptisk**, fordi tilbuddet virker for godt til at være sandt.
sentence.en: I am skeptical because the offer seems too good to be true.

skidt.explanation: "Skidt" means "bad". To say something went better than expected: "Det gik ikke så skidt" (It did not go so badly). To say you do not care about a problem, say "Skidt med det" (Never mind). It also means "dirt": "Der er skidt på dine sko" (There is dirt on your shoes).

forms.en: There is dirt on the floor.

sentence.da: Maden var ikke **skidt**, men den var kold.
sentence.en: The food was not bad, but it was cold.

skiløb.explanation: "Skiløb" means "skiing". It is built from "ski" (ski) and "løb" (run). To say you ski, use "at stå på ski" (literally, to stand on skis): "Jeg står på ski hver vinter" (I ski every winter). It also means "a ski race": "Han vandt skiløbet" (He won the ski race).

sentence.da: Han elsker **skiløb** og tager til Norge hver vinter.
sentence.en: He loves skiing and goes to Norway every winter.

skinnende.explanation: "Skinnende" means "shiny". It comes from the verb "at skinne" (to shine). To describe jewelry that catches the light: "en skinnende ring" (a shiny ring).

sentence.da: Efter rengøring er gulvet rent og **skinnende**.
sentence.en: After cleaning, the floor is clean and shiny.

sko.explanation: "Sko" means "shoes". When you talk about more than one shoe, the word does not change: "to sko" (two shoes). To say you put your shoes on, Danish says "the shoes" where English says "my shoes": "Jeg tager skoene på" (I put my shoes on).

sentence.da: Vi har **sko** på fødderne.
sentence.en: We have shoes on our feet.

skrald.explanation: "Skrald" means "garbage". It takes "et" (the form with "the" is "skraldet"). To say you carry the garbage outside: "Jeg tager skraldet ud" (I take the garbage out). The container is "en skraldespand" (a garbage can).

sentence.da: Der ligger **skrald** på gaden.
sentence.en: There is garbage lying in the street.

skriftlig.explanation: "Skriftlig" means "written". To name the opposite, for things done by speaking, use "mundtlig" (oral): "en mundtlig prøve" (an oral test).

sentence.da: Der er både en mundtlig og en **skriftlig** prøve.
sentence.en: There is both an oral and a written test.

skråt.explanation: "Skråt" means "at an angle". To say where something is diagonally across from something else, use "skråt over for": "Caféen ligger skråt over for stationen" (The cafe is diagonally across from the station).

sentence.da: Solen skinner **skråt** ind ad vinduet om morgenen.
sentence.en: The sun shines in at an angle through the window in the morning.

skræk.explanation: "Skræk" means "fright". To say someone screamed because of sudden fear: "Hun skreg af skræk" (She screamed in terror). Do not mix it up with "en bekymring" (a worry), which lasts: "Jeg har en bekymring for pengene" (I have a worry about money).

sentence.da: Han fik en **skræk**, da lyset gik ud.
sentence.en: He got a fright when the light went out.

skræmmende.explanation: "Skræmmende" means "frightening". To say how you feel, use "bange" (scared): "Jeg er bange" (I am scared).

sentence.da: Mørket kan være **skræmmende** for børn.
sentence.en: The dark can be frightening for children.

skræmt.explanation: "Skræmt" means "scared". It comes from the verb "at skræmme" (to scare). To name what you are afraid of, use "bange for": "Jeg er bange for edderkopper" (I am afraid of spiders).

sentence.da: Barnet så **skræmt** ud efter tordenen.
sentence.en: The child looked scared after the thunder.

skrøbelig.explanation: "Skrøbelig" means "frail". It describes a weak, old or sick person. When you say something breaks easily, it means "fragile": "Glasset er skrøbeligt" (The glass is fragile). To describe something that could easily collapse, such as a peace: "en skrøbelig fred" (a fragile peace).

sentence.da: Pas på, vasen er meget **skrøbelig**.
sentence.en: Careful, the vase is very fragile.

skuffende.explanation: "Skuffende" means "disappointing". To say a person feels let down, use "skuffet" (disappointed): "Jeg er skuffet" (I am disappointed).

sentence.da: Vi trænede hårdt, men resultatet var **skuffende**.
sentence.en: We trained hard, but the result was disappointing.

skuffet.explanation: "Skuffet" means "disappointed". It describes how a person feels. For what let you down, use "skuffende" (disappointing): "Filmen var skuffende" (The film was disappointing).

sentence.da: Hun var **skuffet** over sin karakter.
sentence.en: She was disappointed with her grade.

skummetmælk.explanation: "Skummetmælk" means "skim milk". It is built from "skummet" (skimmed) and "mælk" (milk). To ask for a drink: "Jeg vil gerne have et glas skummetmælk" (I would like a glass of skim milk).

sentence.da: **Skummetmælk** har næsten intet fedt.
sentence.en: Skim milk has almost no fat.

sky.explanation: "Sky" means "shy". Do not mix it up with "en sky" (a cloud), which is spelled the same: "Hun er sky" (She is shy), but "Der er en sky på himlen" (There is a cloud in the sky).

forms.en: He was shy as a child

sentence.da: Han er **sky** og siger næsten ikke noget til fremmede.
sentence.en: He is shy and hardly says anything to strangers.

skyet.explanation: "Skyet" means "cloudy". It comes from "en sky" (a cloud). When clouds cover the whole sky, use "overskyet" (overcast): "Det er overskyet i dag" (It is overcast today).

sentence.da: Himlen er grå og **skyet** i dag.
sentence.en: The sky is gray and cloudy today.

skyld.explanation: "Skyld" means "guilt". When you say who caused a problem, it means "fault": "Det er ikke din skyld" (It is not your fault). To ask who is to blame: "Hvem har skylden?" (Who is to blame?)

sentence.da: Jeg følte **skyld**, fordi jeg glemte hendes fødselsdag.
sentence.en: I felt guilt because I forgot her birthday.

skyldfølelse.explanation: "En skyldfølelse" means "a feeling of guilt". It is built from "skyld" (guilt) and "følelse" (feeling). To say you feel bad about something, say: "Jeg har dårlig samvittighed" (I feel bad about it). It is literally "I have a bad conscience".

sentence.da: Hun fik en **skyldfølelse**, fordi hun glemte sin mors fødselsdag.
sentence.en: She felt a sense of guilt because she forgot her mother's birthday.

skyldig.explanation: "Skyldig" means "guilty". When you say you owe someone money, it means "owing": "Jeg er dig 50 kroner skyldig" (I owe you 50 kroner).

sentence.da: Retten finder ham **skyldig**.
sentence.en: The court finds him guilty.

skynd dig.explanation: "Skynd dig" means "hurry up". The small word "dig" means "yourself", so you say it to one person. To tell several people to hurry, use "jer" (yourselves) instead: "Skynd jer, bussen kommer!" (Hurry up, the bus is coming!)

forms.da: Skynd dig, vi er sent på den.

sentence.da: **Skynd dig**, toget går nu!
sentence.en: Hurry up, the train is leaving now!

skyr.explanation: "Skyr" means "skyr". It is a dairy food that came to Denmark from Iceland. When you talk about skyr in general, use no article: "Jeg spiser skyr til morgenmad" (I eat skyr for breakfast).

sentence.da: **Skyr** er tyk, syrlig og kommer oprindeligt fra Island.
sentence.en: Skyr is thick, tart and originally comes from Iceland.

skål.explanation: "Skål" means "cheers". To toast a person, add "for" and the name: "Skål for Anna!" (Cheers to Anna!) The same word also means "a bowl": "en skål med frugt" (a bowl of fruit).

sentence.da: Vi løfter glassene og siger **skål**!
sentence.en: We raise the glasses and say cheers!

skærtorsdag.explanation: "Skærtorsdag" means "Maundy Thursday". It is the Thursday before "langfredag" (Good Friday). It is a public holiday in Denmark.

sentence.da: Mange danskere holder fri på **skærtorsdag** og tager på ferie.
sentence.en: Many Danes take the day off on Maundy Thursday and go on vacation.

skæv.explanation: "Skæv" means "crooked". To describe a line or a picture that is not straight: "Billedet hænger skævt" (The picture hangs crooked). For a humor that is odd, it means "quirky": "en skæv humor" (a quirky sense of humor).

sentence.da: Stolen er **skæv**, fordi det ene ben er for kort.
sentence.en: The chair is crooked because one leg is too short.

skødesløs.explanation: "Skødesløs" means "careless". To say someone does not look after their belongings: "Han er skødesløs med sine ting" (He is careless with his things).

sentence.da: Han var **skødesløs** og glemte at låse døren.
sentence.en: He was careless and forgot to lock the door.

skøjteløb.explanation: "Skøjteløb" means "ice skating". It is built from "skøjte" (ice skate) and "løb" (run). To say you go ice skating, use "at løbe på skøjter" (literally, to run on skates): "Vi løber på skøjter i weekenden" (We go ice skating at the weekend).

sentence.da: Børnene elsker **skøjteløb** om vinteren.
sentence.en: The children love ice skating in the winter.

skønt.explanation: "Skønt" means "although" and joins two parts of a sentence: "Jeg gik, skønt det regnede" (I went although it rained). To say the same with "selvom" (even though): "Jeg gik, selvom det regnede" (I went even though it rained). The same spelling also means "lovely": "Det er skønt!" (That is lovely!)

sentence.da: Hun blev hjemme, **skønt** hun gerne ville med.
sentence.en: She stayed home although she really wanted to go along.

skør.explanation: "Skør" means "crazy". To tell a friend they are being silly: "Du er skør!" (You are crazy!)

sentence.da: Min onkel er lidt **skør**, men han er sjov.
sentence.en: My uncle is a bit crazy, but he is funny.

sladder.explanation: "Sladder" means "gossip". It takes "en" (the form with "the" is "sladderen"). To say people talk a lot about others: "Der er meget sladder på kontoret" (There is a lot of gossip at the office). A person who spreads it is "en sladrehank" (a tattletale): "Han er en sladrehank" (He is a tattletale).

sentence.da: Det er bare **sladder**, og det er ikke sandt.
sentence.en: It is just gossip, and it is not true.

sladrevorn.explanation: "Sladrevorn" means "gossipy". It comes from the verb "at sladre" (to gossip). To describe a small place where everyone talks about each other: "en sladrevorn by" (a gossipy town).

sentence.da: Min nabo er **sladrevorn** og ved alt om alle i gaden.
sentence.en: My neighbor is gossipy and knows everything about everyone on the street.

slank.explanation: "Slank" means "slim". It is used for things too: "en slank mobil" (a slim phone).

sentence.da: Hun er høj og **slank**, og hun løber hver morgen.
sentence.en: She is tall and slim, and she runs every morning.

slet ikke.explanation: "Slet ikke" means "not at all". To make a no stronger: "Jeg er slet ikke træt" (I am not at all tired). Without "slet", it is a plain no: "Jeg er ikke træt" (I am not tired).

forms.en: It is not expensive at all.
I do not understand at all.

sentence.da: Jeg er **slet ikke** sulten i dag.
sentence.en: I am not hungry at all today.

slidt.explanation: "Slidt" means "worn". To say you are completely exhausted: "Jeg er helt slidt" (I am completely worn out).

sentence.da: Dækket er **slidt**, så vi skal have et nyt.
sentence.en: The tire is worn, so we need a new one.

slik.explanation: "Slik" means "candy". It takes "et" (the form with "the" is "slikket"), but when you mean candy in general, leave out the article: "Jeg spiser for meget slik" (I eat too much candy). Danes have a word for candy eaten on Saturdays: "lørdagsslik" (literally, Saturday candy).

sentence.da: Børn elsker **slik** og kage.
sentence.en: Children love candy and cake.

slud.explanation: "Slud" means "sleet". Do not mix it up with "hagl" (hail): "Der falder hagl" (Hail is falling).

sentence.da: I dag falder der **slud**, og alle har våde sko.
sentence.en: Today sleet is falling and everyone has wet shoes.

slut.explanation: "Slut" means "over". To say an event has ended, use it after "er" (is): "Filmen er slut" (The movie is over). When you say supplies are gone, it means "all gone": "Mælken er slut" (The milk has run out).

sentence.da: Skoledagen er **slut** nu.
sentence.en: The school day is over now.

sløret.explanation: "Sløret" means "blurred". To say something is hinted at on purpose, use "tilsløret" (veiled): "en tilsløret trussel" (a veiled threat).

sentence.da: Billedet er **sløret**, fordi kameraet rystede.
sentence.en: The picture is blurred because the camera shook.

smagløs.explanation: "Smagløs" means "tasteless". It is built from "smag" (taste) and "-løs" (without). For food with no flavor: "Suppen er smagløs" (The soup is tasteless). For a remark in bad taste: "Det var en smagløs bemærkning" (That was a tasteless remark).

sentence.da: Suppen var **smagløs** uden salt og peber.
sentence.en: The soup was tasteless without salt and pepper.

smal.explanation: "Smal" means "narrow". Do not mix it up with "tynd" (thin), which describes thickness: "et tyndt papir" (a thin sheet of paper).

sentence.da: Den lille gade er meget **smal**.
sentence.en: The little street is very narrow.

smart.explanation: "Smart" means "clever". For clothes that look stylish, it means "stylish": "en smart jakke" (a stylish jacket). For a person who is intelligent, use "klog" (smart): "Hun er klog" (She is smart).

sentence.da: Det er en **smart** måde at spare tid på.
sentence.en: It is a clever way to save time.

smertefuld.explanation: "Smertefuld" means "painful". It is built from "smerte" (pain) and "fuld" (full). To say a body part hurts right now, use "at gøre ondt" (to hurt): "Det gør ondt" (It hurts).

sentence.da: Det var en **smertefuld** operation, men han blev rask.
sentence.en: It was a painful operation, but he got well.

smertelig.explanation: "Smertelig" means "painful". Do not mix it up with "smertefuld" (painful), which is a different word: "en smertefuld skade" (a painful injury).

sentence.da: Tabet af hendes bror var en **smertelig** oplevelse.
sentence.en: The loss of her brother was a painful experience.

smertestillende.explanation: "Smertestillende" means "painkillers". It is short for "smertestillende midler" (pain-relieving medicines). To ask a pharmacist: "Har I noget smertestillende?" (Do you have any painkillers?)

sentence.da: Hun tog **smertestillende**, fordi hendes tand gjorde ondt.
sentence.en: She took painkillers because her tooth hurt.

smigret.explanation: "Smigret" means "flattered". To say you feel flattered, use "føle sig" (to feel) before it: "Jeg føler mig smigret" (I feel flattered).

sentence.da: Jeg blev **smigret**, da min chef roste mit arbejde.
sentence.en: I was flattered when my boss praised my work.

smitsom.explanation: "Smitsom" means "contagious". It comes from the verb "at smitte" (to infect). To ask whether an illness can spread to you, say: "Er det smitsomt?" (Is it contagious?)

sentence.da: Influenza er **smitsom**, og syge børn bør blive hjemme.
sentence.en: Influenza is contagious, and sick children should stay home.

smuk.explanation: "Smuk" means "beautiful". To admire a view, say: "Sikke en smuk udsigt" (What a beautiful view). To say something is done beautifully, add "t": "Hun synger smukt" (She sings beautifully).

sentence.da: Hun har en **smuk** kjole på.
sentence.en: She is wearing a beautiful dress.

småpenge.explanation: "Småpenge" means "small change". It is built from "små" (small) and "penge" (money). To say a price is nothing to someone, say: "Det er småpenge for ham" (It is peanuts to him).

sentence.da: Har du nogle **småpenge** til automaten?
sentence.en: Do you have some small change for the machine?

småting.explanation: "Småting" means "small things". It is built from "små" (small) and "ting" (things). To say someone gets upset over unimportant matters, say: "Hun bliver sur over småting" (She gets angry over trivial things).

forms.en: I am buying some small things.

sentence.da: Jeg skal bare købe nogle **småting** i byen.
sentence.en: I just have to buy a few small things in town.

smør.explanation: "Smør" means "butter". To say you spread butter on bread, use the verb "at smøre" (to spread): "Jeg smører brødet" (I am buttering the bread). The open sandwich "smørrebrød" is literally "butter bread".

sentence.da: Vil du have **smør** på dit brød?
sentence.en: Do you want butter on your bread?

smøreost.explanation: "Smøreost" means "spreadable cheese". It is built from "smøre" (to spread) and "ost" (cheese). The part "ost" also appears in "en ostemad" (a cheese sandwich).

sentence.da: Jeg smører **smøreost** på mit rugbrød.
sentence.en: I spread spreadable cheese on my rye bread.

snakkesalig.explanation: "Snakkesalig" means "chatty". It is built on the verb "at snakke" (to talk). To describe a child who talks a lot today, say: "Hun er meget snakkesalig i dag" (She is very chatty today).

sentence.da: Han er **snakkesalig** og fortæller gerne om hele sin dag.
sentence.en: He is chatty and likes to tell about his whole day.

snarere.explanation: "Snarere" means "rather". To correct what you just said, use it before the better description: "Han er ikke doven, snarere træt" (He is not lazy, rather tired). To say you prefer one thing, use "hellere" (rather) instead: "Jeg vil hellere gå" (I would rather walk).

sentence.da: Det var ikke en fejl, men **snarere** en dårlig plan.
sentence.en: It was not a mistake, but rather a bad plan.

snart.explanation: "Snart" means "soon". To say goodbye until next time, say: "Vi ses snart" (See you soon). With a clock time it means "almost": "Klokken er snart ti" (It is almost ten o'clock). With "så" before it, it means "as soon as": "Så snart jeg kommer hjem, ringer jeg" (As soon as I get home, I will call).

sentence.da: Maden er **snart** klar.
sentence.en: The food will be ready soon.

snavs.explanation: "Snavs" means "dirt", as in filth on things. To say something is full of it, use "fuld af" (full of): "Skoene er fulde af snavs" (The shoes are full of dirt). For soil in the ground, use "jord" (soil): "Planterne står i jord" (The plants are in soil).

sentence.da: Der er meget **snavs** på mine sko.
sentence.en: There is a lot of dirt on my shoes.

snavset.explanation: "Snavset" means "dirty". It comes from the noun "snavs" (dirt). To describe more than one thing, the word ends in "-e": "Mine hænder er snavsede" (My hands are dirty).

sentence.da: Tøjet er **snavset** og skal vaskes.
sentence.en: The clothes are dirty and need washing.

sne.explanation: "Sne" means "snow". It is also the start of other snow words, such as "en snebold" (a snowball) and "en snestorm" (a snowstorm).

sentence.da: Børnene laver en snemand af **sne**.
sentence.en: The children make a snowman out of snow.

snu.explanation: "Snu" means "cunning". To say a person is cunning, say: "Han er meget snu" (He is very cunning).

sentence.da: Ræven er **snu** og stjæler æg fra hønsegården.
sentence.en: The fox is cunning and steals eggs from the henhouse.

snue.explanation: "Snue" means "a head cold". To say you caught one, leave out the article: "Jeg har fået snue" (I have caught a head cold). For the flu, use "influenza" (flu): "Jeg har influenza" (I have the flu).

sentence.da: Jeg har **snue**, og min næse løber.
sentence.en: I have a head cold, and my nose is running.

social.explanation: "Social" means "social", as in liking company. When you talk about problems in society, it is used too: "sociale problemer" (social problems).

sentence.da: Min søster er meget **social** og elsker fester.
sentence.en: My sister is very social and loves parties.

sociale medier.explanation: "Sociale medier" means "social media". To say you are taking a break from it, say: "Jeg holder pause fra sociale medier" (I am taking a break from social media).

sentence.da: Facebook og Instagram er **sociale medier**.
sentence.en: Facebook and Instagram are social media.

socialistisk.explanation: "Socialistisk" means "socialist". It comes from the noun "socialisme" (socialism). A Danish party has it in its name: "Socialistisk Folkeparti" (the Socialist People's Party).

sentence.da: Et **socialistisk** parti vil have, at staten ejer mere.
sentence.en: A socialist party wants the state to own more.

software.explanation: "Software" means "software". It is an English word that Danish uses unchanged. Its opposite, the physical machine parts, is "hardware" (hardware). To say you put it on a computer, say: "at installere software" (to install software).

sentence.da: Vi bruger gratis **software** til at redigere billeder.
sentence.en: We use free software to edit pictures.

sojamælk.explanation: "Sojamælk" means "soy milk". It is built from "soja" (soy) and "mælk" (milk). To ask for it in your coffee, say: "Kan jeg få sojamælk i kaffen?" (Can I have soy milk in my coffee?)

sentence.da: Hun drikker **sojamælk**, fordi hun er veganer.
sentence.en: She drinks soy milk because she is vegan.

sokker.explanation: "Sokker" means "socks". To say wool socks, join "uld" (wool) and "sokker": "uldsokker" (wool socks).

sentence.da: Jeg tager **sokker** og sko på.
sentence.en: I put on socks and shoes.

solbriller.explanation: "Solbriller" means "sunglasses". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "briller" (glasses). To say you forgot yours, say: "Jeg har glemt mine solbriller" (I have forgotten my sunglasses).

sentence.da: Jeg tager **solbriller** på i solen.
sentence.en: I put on sunglasses in the sun.

solbrændt.explanation: "Solbrændt" means "sunburned". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "brændt" (burned). To say you got sunburned, use "blive" (to become): "Jeg blev solbrændt" (I got sunburned).

sentence.da: Efter en uge på stranden var han rød og **solbrændt**.
sentence.en: After a week on the beach he was red and sunburned.

solcreme.explanation: "Solcreme" means "sunscreen". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "creme" (cream). When you mean sunscreen in general, leave out "en": "Jeg har solcreme med" (I have sunscreen with me).

sentence.da: Husk at tage **solcreme** med på stranden.
sentence.en: Remember to bring sunscreen to the beach.

solenergi.explanation: "Solenergi" means "solar power". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "energi" (energy). To say a house has solar panels, use "solceller" (solar cells): "Huset har solceller på taget" (The house has solar cells on the roof).

sentence.da: Med **solenergi** kan huset lave strøm af solens lys.
sentence.en: With solar power the house can make electricity from sunlight.

solid.explanation: "Solid" means "solid", as in strong and well built. To describe a person you can trust, it means "reliable": "en solid mand" (a reliable man).

sentence.da: Vi byggede en **solid** hytte af sten.
sentence.en: We built a solid cabin made of stone.

solrig.explanation: "Solrig" means "sunny". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "rig" (rich), so it is literally "sun-rich". To say the weather is sunny, add "t": "Det er solrigt i dag" (It is sunny today).

sentence.da: Det er en varm og **solrig** dag.
sentence.en: It is a warm and sunny day.

solrigt.explanation: "Solrigt" means "sunny". To describe the weather, use it after "det er" (it is): "Det er solrigt" (It is sunny). It is the form of "solrig" that goes before "vejr" (weather): "solrigt vejr" (sunny weather).

sentence.da: I dag er det **solrigt** og varmt.
sentence.en: Today it is sunny and warm.

solskin.explanation: "Solskin" means "sunshine". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "skin" (shine). The verb "at skinne" (to shine) goes with the sun: "Solen skinner" (The sun is shining).

sentence.da: Efter regnen kommer **solskin**.
sentence.en: After the rain comes sunshine.

solskinsvejr.explanation: "Solskinsvejr" means "sunny weather". It is built from "solskin" (sunshine) and "vejr" (weather). To say you do something in sunny weather, use "i" (in): "Vi spiser ude i solskinsvejr" (We eat outside in sunny weather).

sentence.da: Det er dejligt at gå tur i **solskinsvejr**.
sentence.en: It is lovely to go for a walk in sunny weather.

solsystemet.explanation: "Solsystemet" means "solar system". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "system" (system). To say a planet circles the sun, use the verb "at kredse" (to orbit): "Jorden kredser om solen" (The Earth orbits the sun).

sentence.da: Jorden er en af otte planeter i **solsystemet**.
sentence.en: Earth is one of eight planets in the solar system.

som.explanation: "Som" means "that" when it joins two parts of a sentence. To say which person you mean, say: "manden, som bor her" (the man who lives here). To say what someone was when younger, it means "as": "Som barn boede jeg i Aarhus" (As a child I lived in Aarhus). To compare, it means "like": "Hun synger som en engel" (She sings like an angel).

sentence.da: Det er den bog, **som** jeg læser.
sentence.en: That is the book that I am reading.

som følge af.explanation: "Som følge af" means "as a result of". To name the cause of something, put the cause after it: "Skolen lukkede som følge af snestormen" (The school closed as a result of the snowstorm). To say "because of" in plain terms, use "på grund af" (because of): "Toget var forsinket på grund af sne" (The train was delayed because of snow).

forms.en: as a result of the accident
as a result of the rain

sentence.da: Flere fly blev aflyst **som følge af** den kraftige storm.
sentence.en: Several flights were canceled as a result of the strong storm.

som helst.explanation: "Som helst" means "any". To say anyone may do something, add it after "hvem" (who): "Hvem som helst kan komme" (Anyone can come). After "noget" (something) in a sentence with "ikke" (not), it means "at all": "Jeg ved ikke noget som helst" (I know nothing at all).

forms.da: Det kan være hvad som helst

sentence.da: Du kan spørge mig om hvad **som helst**.
sentence.en: You can ask me about anything.

som om.explanation: "Som om" means "as if". To describe how someone acts, say: "Han opfører sig, som om han ejer stedet" (He acts as if he owns the place).

forms.en: as if we know each other

sentence.da: Det føles **som om** vi har kendt hinanden længe.
sentence.en: It feels as if we have known each other for a long time.

som regel.explanation: "Som regel" means "usually". Literally, it is "as a rule". To say something is always true with no exceptions, use "altid" (always) instead: "Jeg drikker altid kaffe" (I always drink coffee).

forms.da: Jeg står som regel op klokken syv.
forms.en: I usually get up at seven o'clock.
As a rule we eat late.

sentence.da: Jeg drikker **som regel** kaffe om morgenen.
sentence.en: I usually drink coffee in the morning.

somme tider.explanation: "Somme tider" means "sometimes". Literally, it is "some times". Danish also allows the spelling "sommetider" (sometimes) as one word.

sentence.da: Jeg er **somme tider** træt om morgenen.
sentence.en: I am sometimes tired in the morning.

sommertid.explanation: "Sommertid" means "daylight saving time". It is built from "sommer" (summer) and "tid" (time). To say you move the clock forward, say: "Vi stiller uret frem" (We set the clock forward).

forms.da: Der er sommertid fra marts til oktober
forms.en: Daylight saving time runs from March to October
Daylight saving time starts in March
It is daylight saving time now

sentence.da: Vi skifter til **sommertid** i marts.
sentence.en: We switch to daylight saving time in March.

sommetider.explanation: "Sommetider" means "sometimes". It is built from "somme" (some) and "tider" (times). Danish also allows the spelling "somme tider" (sometimes) as two words.

forms.en: I sometimes go for a walk

sentence.da: Jeg tager **sommetider** cyklen på arbejde.
sentence.en: Sometimes I take the bike to work.

sorg.explanation: "Sorg" means "sorrow", which also covers grief. For everyday sadness that is not grief, say: "Jeg er ked af det" (I am sad).

sentence.da: Hele byen delte familiens **sorg**.
sentence.en: The whole town shared the family's grief.

sort.explanation: "Sort" means "black". For work done without telling the tax authorities, it is used in "sort arbejde" (undeclared work): "Det er sort arbejde" (That is undeclared work).

sentence.da: Natten er mørk og **sort**.
sentence.en: The night is dark and black.

sov godt.explanation: "Sov godt" means "sleep well". It is built from "sov" (sleep) and "godt" (well). To ask the next morning whether someone slept well, say: "Har du sovet godt?" (Did you sleep well?)

sentence.da: Godnat, **sov godt**!
sentence.en: Good night, sleep well!

spaghetti.explanation: "Spaghetti" means "spaghetti". To say you want some, leave out "en": "Jeg vil have spaghetti" (I want spaghetti). To name a portion, use "en tallerken" (a plate): "en tallerken spaghetti" (a plate of spaghetti).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **spaghetti** med kødsovs.
sentence.en: We eat spaghetti with meat sauce.

spanien.explanation: "Spanien" means "Spain". Danish uses "i" (in) for being in a country and "til" (to) for going there: "i Spanien" (in Spain), "til Spanien" (to Spain).

sentence.da: Vi holder ferie i **Spanien**.
sentence.en: We are on vacation in Spain.

spansk.explanation: "Spansk" means "Spanish". It comes from "Spanien" (Spain). To say you are learning the language, say: "Jeg lærer spansk" (I am learning Spanish).

sentence.da: I Spanien taler man **spansk**.
sentence.en: In Spain, people speak Spanish.

spartansk.explanation: "Spartansk" means "plain", as in without comfort or extras. It comes from "Sparta", the ancient Greek city known for its hard way of life.

sentence.da: Værelset var **spartansk** og havde kun en seng og en stol.
sentence.en: The room was spartan and only had a bed and a chair.

speciel.explanation: "Speciel" means "special". Danish ends it in "-el", not "-al" as English does. To say someone is a little odd, use it about the person: "Han er lidt speciel" (He is a bit odd).

sentence.da: I dag er en **speciel** dag for os.
sentence.en: Today is a special day for us.

specifik.explanation: "Specifik" means "specific". Its opposite is "generel" (general): "et generelt spørgsmål" (a general question).

sentence.da: Jeg leder efter en **specifik** bog, ikke bare en krimi.
sentence.en: I am looking for a specific book, not just a crime novel.

specifikt.explanation: "Specifikt" means "specifically". Put it right before the one person or thing you mean, to rule out the others: "Hun spurgte specifikt efter dig" (She asked for you specifically). To describe a thing itself as exact, use "specifik" (specific): "en specifik grund" (a specific reason).

forms.en: What are you looking for specifically?

sentence.da: Jeg vil **specifikt** have den røde jakke, ikke den blå.
sentence.en: I specifically want the red jacket, not the blue one.

spegepølse.explanation: "En spegepølse" means "a salami". To say what is in your packed lunch, say: "Der er spegepølse i min madpakke" (There is salami in my packed lunch).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger en tynd skive **spegepølse** på rugbrødet.
sentence.en: I put a thin slice of salami on the rye bread.

spids.explanation: "Spids" means "pointed". To describe a knife that cuts well, use "skarp" (sharp) instead: "en skarp kniv" (a sharp knife). As a noun, "en spids" means "a tip": "Spidsen af blyanten er knækket" (The tip of the pencil is broken).

sentence.da: Nålen er **spids**, og den kan stikke dig.
sentence.en: The needle is pointed, and it can prick you.

spinat.explanation: "Spinat" means "spinach". To say you eat it, leave out the article: "Jeg spiser spinat" (I eat spinach). To name a bag of it, use "en pose" (a bag): "en pose spinat" (a bag of spinach).

sentence.da: **Spinat** er grøn og sund.
sentence.en: Spinach is green and healthy.

spinkel.explanation: "Spinkel" means "slender". To say a basis or evidence is too weak to rely on, it means "flimsy": "et spinkelt grundlag" (a flimsy basis).

sentence.da: Pigen er **spinkel**, men stærk og hurtig.
sentence.en: The girl is slender, but strong and fast.

spirituel.explanation: "Spirituel" means "witty". English speakers mix it up with "spiritual". To say spiritual or religious, use "åndelig" (spiritual): "en åndelig oplevelse" (a spiritual experience).

sentence.da: Hun er **spirituel** og har altid et skarpt svar klar.
sentence.en: She is witty and always has a sharp answer ready.

spiselig.explanation: "Spiselig" means "edible". It comes from the verb "at spise" (to eat). To say something is also tasty, add "lækker" (delicious): "Svampen er både spiselig og lækker" (The mushroom is both edible and delicious).

sentence.da: Denne svamp er **spiselig**, men den anden er giftig.
sentence.en: This mushroom is edible, but the other one is poisonous.

spontan.explanation: "Spontan" means "spontaneous". Danish ends it in "-an", not "-aneous". To describe a choice made on the spot, say: "Jeg tog en spontan beslutning" (I made a spontaneous decision).

sentence.da: Vi tog en **spontan** tur til stranden i går.
sentence.en: We took a spontaneous trip to the beach yesterday.

sport.explanation: "Sport" means "sport". To talk about sport in general, leave out the article: "Jeg elsker sport" (I love sports). To name one kind, use "en sport" (a sport): "Tennis er en sport" (Tennis is a sport). To say you do sports, use "at dyrke" (to practice): "Han dyrker meget sport" (He does a lot of sports).

sentence.da: Fodbold og tennis er **sport**.
sentence.en: Soccer and tennis are sports.

sportslig.explanation: "Sportslig" means "athletic", as in about sports events and results. For clothes, use "sporty" (sporty): "en sporty jakke" (a sporty jacket).

sentence.da: Holdet havde en stor **sportslig** succes i år.
sentence.en: The team had a big athletic success this year.

sporty.explanation: "Sporty" means "sporty". It is borrowed from English and keeps the same ending with "en", with "et" and with a plural noun. For something about sports events and results, use "sportslig" (athletic): "en sportslig præstation" (an athletic achievement).

sentence.da: Hun kommer altid i **sporty** sko og en let jakke.
sentence.en: She always comes in sporty shoes and a light jacket.

sprogkundskaber.explanation: "Sprogkundskaber" means "language skills". It is built from "et sprog" (a language) and "kundskaber" (knowledge). To say in which language your skills are weak, say: "Mine sprogkundskaber i tysk er dårlige" (My language skills in German are poor).

sentence.da: Jobbet kræver **sprogkundskaber** i både engelsk og tysk.
sentence.en: The job requires language skills in both English and German.

sprængstof.explanation: "Et sprængstof" means "an explosive". It is built from "at sprænge" (to blow up) and "stof" (substance). The word "stof" also means "fabric": "Jeg køber stof til gardiner" (I am buying fabric for curtains).

sentence.da: Arbejderne bruger **sprængstof** til at lave tunneler i fjeldet.
sentence.en: The workers use explosives to make tunnels in the rock.

sprød.explanation: "Sprød" means "crispy". For a raw carrot that crunches when you bite it, "sprød" is used as well: "en sprød gulerod" (a crunchy carrot).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt lide **sprød** bacon.
sentence.en: I like crispy bacon.

spændende.explanation: "Spændende" means "exciting". To describe something that makes you want to know what happens next, say: "en spændende film" (an exciting movie). For something that interests you calmly, use "interessant" (interesting): "en interessant artikel" (an interesting article).

sentence.da: Jeg læser en **spændende** bog.
sentence.en: I am reading an exciting book.

spænding.explanation: "Spænding" means "excitement". It also means "tension" between people: "Der er spænding mellem dem" (There is tension between them). The matching adjective is "spændende" (exciting): "en spændende film" (an exciting movie).

sentence.da: Vi ventede med **spænding** på resultatet.
sentence.en: We waited with excitement for the result.

spærret.explanation: "Spærret" means "blocked". To say who blocked a place, add "af" (by): "Indgangen er spærret af politiet" (The entrance is blocked by the police).

sentence.da: Broen er **spærret**, fordi der er vejarbejde i dag.
sentence.en: The bridge is closed because there are roadworks today.

stabil.explanation: "Stabil" means "stable". To describe a person's health, say: "Hans helbred er stabilt" (His health is stable).

sentence.da: Den nye stige er meget **stabil**, så den er sikker.
sentence.en: The new ladder is very stable, so it is safe.

stadig.explanation: "Stadig" means "still". To say something has not happened yet, use "endnu" (yet) instead: "Jeg er ikke færdig endnu" (I am not finished yet).

sentence.da: Barnet sover **stadig** klokken ti.
sentence.en: The child is still sleeping at ten o'clock.

stadigvæk.explanation: "Stadigvæk" means "still". It is "stadig" (still) with "væk" (away) added. To say something has not happened yet, use "endnu" (yet) instead: "Jeg er ikke færdig endnu" (I am not finished yet).

sentence.da: Han bor **stadigvæk** hos sin mor.
sentence.en: He still lives with his mother.

stakkels.explanation: "Stakkels" means "poor", as in pitiful. To show pity for someone, say: "Stakkels dig!" (Poor you!). For someone with little money, use "fattig" (poor): "en fattig familie" (a poor family).

sentence.da: Den **stakkels** hund er våd og kold.
sentence.en: The poor dog is wet and cold.

standard.explanation: "Standard" means "standard". To talk about quality, say: "Hotellet har høj standard" (The hotel has a high standard).

sentence.da: Bilen har varme i sæderne som **standard**.
sentence.en: The car has heated seats as standard.

standhaftig.explanation: "Standhaftig" means "steadfast". To say someone held firm when questioned, say: "Han var standhaftig under forhøret" (He was steadfast during the questioning). It is a different word from "stædig" (stubborn): "et stædigt barn" (a stubborn child).

sentence.da: Hun forblev **standhaftig** og gav ikke efter for presset.
sentence.en: She remained steadfast and did not give in to the pressure.

stavning.explanation: "En stavning" means "a spelling". It comes from the verb "at stave" (to spell). To ask how a word is spelled, say: "Hvordan staver man det?" (How do you spell that?)

sentence.da: Ordbogen viser den rigtige **stavning** af hvert ord.
sentence.en: The dictionary shows the correct spelling of each word.

stegt.explanation: "Stegt" means "fried". It is the form of the verb "at stege" (to fry) that describes food. A Danish dish with it is "stegt flæsk" (fried pork belly).

sentence.da: Fisken er **stegt** i panden.
sentence.en: The fish is fried in the pan.

stegt flæsk.explanation: "Stegt flæsk" means "fried pork belly". It is built from "stegt" (fried) and "flæsk" (pork belly).

forms.en: two slices of fried pork belly
We are eating fried pork belly

sentence.da: **Stegt flæsk** med persillesovs er en klassisk dansk ret.
sentence.en: Fried pork belly with parsley sauce is a classic Danish dish.

stemmeret.explanation: "En stemmeret" means "a right to vote". It is built from "en stemme" (a vote) and "ret" (right). To say when women got it in Denmark, say: "Kvinder fik stemmeret i 1915" (Women got the right to vote in 1915).
