sentence.da: I Danmark får man **stemmeret**, når man fylder atten år.
sentence.en: In Denmark you get the right to vote when you turn eighteen.

stemningsfuld.explanation: "Stemningsfuld" means "atmospheric". It is built from "en stemning" (a mood) and "fuld" (full). To praise a concert, say: "Det var en stemningsfuld koncert" (It was an atmospheric concert).

sentence.da: Caféen er **stemningsfuld**, med levende lys og blød musik.
sentence.en: The café is atmospheric, with candles and soft music.

stilhed.explanation: "Stilhed" means "silence". It comes from the adjective "stille" (quiet). For peace and quiet, use "ro" (peace) instead: "Jeg vil have ro" (I want peace and quiet).

sentence.da: Efter skriget var der **stilhed** i huset.
sentence.en: After the scream there was silence in the house.

stille.explanation: "Stille" means "quiet". To tell someone to be quiet, say: "Vær stille" (Be quiet). For a relaxed person, use "rolig" (calm): "Hun er meget rolig" (She is very calm). The verb "at stille" (to put) is a different use: "at stille et spørgsmål" (to ask a question).

sentence.da: Det er meget **stille** i huset.
sentence.en: It is very quiet in the house.

stillehavet.explanation: "Stillehavet" means "the Pacific Ocean". It is built from "stille" (calm) and "hav" (ocean), with "-et" at the end for "the". To say where a country lies, say: "Japan ligger ved Stillehavet" (Japan lies by the Pacific).

sentence.da: **Stillehavet** er det største hav på Jorden og ligger mellem Asien og Amerika.
sentence.en: The Pacific Ocean is the biggest ocean on Earth and lies between Asia and America.

stinkende.explanation: "Stinkende" means "stinking". It comes from the verb "at stinke" (to stink). To make "rig" (rich) stronger, put it before: "Han er stinkende rig" (He is stinking rich).

sentence.da: Der er **stinkende** fisk i skraldespanden, og alle kan lugte det.
sentence.en: There is stinking fish in the trash can, and everyone can smell it.

stiv.explanation: "Stiv" means "stiff". To say your body feels tight and sore, say: "Mine ben er stive efter turen" (My legs are stiff after the trip).

sentence.da: Jeg er **stiv** i nakken i dag.
sentence.en: My neck is stiff today.

stolt af.explanation: "Stolt af" means "proud of". To name the person you are proud of, put the name or "dig" (you) after "af": "Jeg er stolt af dig" (I am proud of you). To name an achievement you are proud of, put "at" (to) and a verb after "af": "stolt af at have klaret det" (proud of having managed it).

forms.da: Jeg er stolt af min datter.
forms.en: I am proud of my daughter.

forms.da: Hun er stolt af sit hus.
forms.en: She is proud of her house.
We are proud of the team.

sentence.da: Jeg er **stolt af** min lille bror.
sentence.en: I am proud of my little brother.

stolthed.explanation: "Stolthed" means "pride". It comes from the adjective "stolt" (proud). To say someone is full of it, say: "Han var fyldt af stolthed" (He was filled with pride).

sentence.da: Hans mor græd af **stolthed**, fordi han vandt.
sentence.en: His mother cried with pride because he won.

stop.explanation: "Stop" means "stop". To tell someone to wait a moment, add "lige" (just): "Stop lige!" (Hold on a second!)

sentence.da: **Stop**! Der kommer en bil!
sentence.en: Stop! A car is coming!

stor.explanation: "Stor" means "big". To say a child has grown, use it after "blevet" (become): "Hvor er du blevet stor!" (How big you have grown!) It is also the start of other words, such as "en storby" (a big city).

sentence.da: Elefanten er meget **stor**.
sentence.en: The elephant is very big.

storartet.explanation: "Storartet" means "magnificent". To praise a meal, say: "Det var en storartet middag" (It was a magnificent dinner). For a view, use "storslået" (grand): "en storslået udsigt" (a grand view).

sentence.da: Det var en **storartet** forestilling, og publikum klappede længe.
sentence.en: It was a magnificent performance, and the audience clapped for a long time.

storbritannien.explanation: "Storbritannien" means "Great Britain". It is built from "stor" (big) and "Britannien" (Britain). The part "stor" also starts other words, such as "en storby" (a big city).

sentence.da: London ligger i **Storbritannien**.
sentence.en: London is in Great Britain.

stormfuld.explanation: "Stormfuld" means "stormy". It is built from "storm" (storm) and "fuld" (full). To describe troubled years in someone's life, say: "Han havde en stormfuld ungdom" (He had a stormy youth).

sentence.da: Natten var **stormfuld**, og vinden ruskede i træerne.
sentence.en: The night was stormy, and the wind shook the trees.

storslået.explanation: "Storslået" means "grand". To praise a party, say: "Det var en storslået fest" (It was a grand party).

sentence.da: Fra toppen af bjerget har man en **storslået** udsigt.
sentence.en: From the top of the mountain you have a magnificent view.

stort set.explanation: "Stort set" means "almost". To say nearly all of a job is done, say: "Vi er stort set færdige" (We are almost done). To say you have hardly slept, say: "Jeg har stort set ikke sovet" (I have hardly slept).

sentence.da: Vi er **stort set** enige om det.
sentence.en: We basically agree about it.

straks.explanation: "Straks" means "right away". To say you are coming now, say: "Jeg kommer straks" (I am coming right away).

sentence.da: Sæt dig ned, maden er **straks** klar.
sentence.en: Sit down, the food will be ready in a moment.

stram.explanation: "Stram" means "tight". To describe rules, it means "strict": "stramme regler" (strict rules).

sentence.da: Jakken er for **stram** over skuldrene, og jeg vil bytte den.
sentence.en: The jacket is too tight over the shoulders, and I want to exchange it.

stramt.explanation: "Stramt" means "tightly". It goes with verbs such as "at trække" (to pull): "Hun trak rebet stramt" (She pulled the rope tight). To describe a thing, use "stram" (tight): "en stram kjole" (a tight dress).

sentence.da: Hun bandt sækken **stramt** til.
sentence.en: She tied the sack tightly.

streaming.explanation: "Streaming" means "streaming". It is an English word that Danish uses unchanged. To say you watch a film this way, use the verb "at streame" (to stream): "Vi streamer en film" (We are streaming a movie).

sentence.da: Vi bruger **streaming** i stedet for dvd'er.
sentence.en: We use streaming instead of DVDs.

streng.explanation: "Streng" means "strict". For weather, it means "harsh": "en streng vinter" (a harsh winter).

sentence.da: Vores lærer er **streng**, men retfærdig.
sentence.en: Our teacher is strict but fair.

stress.explanation: "Stress" means "stress". To say someone is off work because of it, use "sygemeldt" (on sick leave): "Han er sygemeldt med stress" (He is on sick leave with stress).

sentence.da: Meget arbejde og lidt søvn kan give **stress**.
sentence.en: A lot of work and little sleep can cause stress.

stresset.explanation: "Stresset" means "stressed". It comes from the noun "stress" (stress). To describe the thing that causes it, use "stressende" (stressful): "Det er stressende" (It is stressful).

sentence.da: Hun er **stresset**, fordi hun har for meget arbejde.
sentence.en: She is stressed because she has too much work.

stribet.explanation: "Stribet" means "striped". It comes from the noun "en stribe" (a stripe).

sentence.da: Zebraens pels er **stribet** i sort og hvid.
sentence.en: The zebra's coat is striped in black and white.

strikning.explanation: "Strikning" means "knitting". It comes from the verb "at strikke" (to knit): "Jeg strikker en trøje" (I am knitting a sweater).

sentence.da: Min mormor elsker **strikning** og laver mange trøjer.
sentence.en: My grandmother loves knitting and makes many sweaters.

strålende.explanation: "Strålende" means "brilliant". It comes from "en stråle" (a ray of light). To say things are going very well, say: "Det går strålende" (It is going great).

sentence.da: Vi havde **strålende** vejr hele ugen.
sentence.en: We had brilliant weather all week.

stråling.explanation: "Stråling" means "radiation". It comes from "en stråle" (a ray). To name the kind that comes from the sun and tanning beds, say "UV-stråling" (UV radiation).

sentence.da: For meget **stråling** fra solen kan skade huden.
sentence.en: Too much radiation from the sun can damage the skin.

strøm.explanation: "Strøm" means "electricity". To say the power has gone off, say: "Strømmen er gået" (The power has gone out). To talk about water, it also means "current": "en stærk strøm i floden" (a strong current in the river).

sentence.da: Lamper og computere bruger **strøm**.
sentence.en: Lamps and computers use electricity.

strømpebukser.explanation: "Strømpebukser" means "tights". To say you put them on, use "at tage på" (to put on): "Jeg tager strømpebukser på" (I put on tights).

sentence.da: Hun har sorte **strømpebukser** på til kjolen.
sentence.en: She is wearing black tights with the dress.

styrketræning.explanation: "Styrketræning" means "strength training". To say you do it, use "at lave" (to do): "Jeg laver styrketræning om mandagen" (I do strength training on Mondays). For running, say "konditionstræning" (cardio training): "Jeg elsker konditionstræning" (I love cardio training).

sentence.da: Med **styrketræning** bliver musklerne større og stærkere.
sentence.en: With strength training, the muscles get bigger and stronger.

stål.explanation: "Stål" means "steel". When you say what something is made of, use it without an article after "af" (of): "Skeen er af stål" (The spoon is made of steel).

sentence.da: Broen er lavet af **stål** og er meget stærk.
sentence.en: The bridge is made of steel and is very strong.

stædig.explanation: "Stædig" means "stubborn". To name the quality as a noun, use "stædighed" (stubbornness): "Hans stædighed er irriterende" (His stubbornness is annoying).

sentence.da: Han er **stædig** og vil aldrig lytte til andre.
sentence.en: He is stubborn and never wants to listen to others.

stærk.explanation: "Stærk" means "strong". To describe food that burns your mouth, it also means "spicy": "en stærk sovs" (a spicy sauce).

sentence.da: Han er **stærk** og kan løfte tunge ting.
sentence.en: He is strong and can lift heavy things.

støj.explanation: "Støj" means "noise". To say where the noise comes from, use "fra" (from): "støj fra trafikken" (noise from the traffic). For a sound you like, use "lyd" (sound) instead: "en dejlig lyd" (a lovely sound).

sentence.da: Naboerne laver meget **støj** om natten.
sentence.en: The neighbors make a lot of noise at night.

støjende.explanation: "Støjende" means "noisy". It comes from "støj" (noise). To say music is loud, use "høj" (loud) instead: "Musikken er for høj" (The music is too loud).

sentence.da: Vores naboer er meget **støjende** om natten.
sentence.en: Our neighbors are very noisy at night.

størst.explanation: "Størst" means "biggest". To say "bigger", use "større" (bigger) instead: "Hun er større end mig" (She is bigger than me). To say "biggest" among three or more, use "størst": "Han er størst i klassen" (He is the biggest in the class).

sentence.da: Hvalen er **størst** af dyrene.
sentence.en: The whale is the biggest of the animals.

støv.explanation: "Støv" means "dust". To say you wipe the dust off something, use "at tørre støv af" (to wipe dust off): "Jeg tørrer støv af hylderne" (I am wiping the dust off the shelves).

sentence.da: Der er meget **støv** under sofaen.
sentence.en: There is a lot of dust under the sofa.

støvler.explanation: "Støvler" means "boots". It is the plural of "en støvle" (a boot). To say a pair, use "et par støvler" (a pair of boots).

sentence.da: Jeg tager **støvler** på i regnen.
sentence.en: I put on boots in the rain.

støvregn.explanation: "Støvregn" means "drizzle". It is built from "støv" (dust) and "regn" (rain): drops as small as dust.

sentence.da: I **støvregn** bliver man næsten ikke våd.
sentence.en: In drizzle you hardly get wet.

su.explanation: "SU" means "a student grant". The letters stand for "statens uddannelsesstøtte" (the state's study support). To say you live on the grant, use "på SU" (on SU): "Jeg er på SU" (I am on SU).

sentence.da: Studerende på universitetet får **SU** hver måned.
sentence.en: Students at the university get SU every month.

subjektiv.explanation: "Subjektiv" means "subjective". The Danish word ends in "-iv", not "-ive". To say something rests on facts, use "objektiv" (objective) instead: "en objektiv vurdering" (an objective judgment).

sentence.da: Smag er **subjektiv**.
sentence.en: Taste is subjective.

succesfuld.explanation: "Succesfuld" means "successful". It is built from "succes" (success) and "fuld" (full).

sentence.da: Hun er en **succesfuld** læge.
sentence.en: She is a successful doctor.

sukker.explanation: "Sukker" means "sugar". The word is part of other words: "sukkerroe" (sugar beet) and "sukkerskål" (sugar bowl).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have **sukker** i kaffen.
sentence.en: I want sugar in my coffee.

sult.explanation: "Sult" means "hunger". To say you are hungry, use "sulten" (hungry) instead: "Jeg er sulten" (I am hungry).

sentence.da: Mange mennesker i verden lider af **sult** og har ikke mad.
sentence.en: Many people in the world suffer from hunger and have no food.

sulten.explanation: "Sulten" means "hungry". To say you are getting hungry, use "at blive" (to become): "Jeg bliver sulten om aftenen" (I get hungry in the evening).

sentence.da: Jeg er meget **sulten** og vil spise.
sentence.en: I am very hungry and want to eat.

sund.explanation: "Sund" means "healthy". To say a sick person is well again, use "rask" (well) instead: "Jeg er rask igen" (I am well again).

sentence.da: Æbler og gulerødder er **sund** mad.
sentence.en: Apples and carrots are healthy food.

sundhed.explanation: "Sundhed" means "health". It is built from "sund" (healthy). To talk about health in general, say: "Sundhed er vigtigt" (Health is important). For a person's own condition, use "helbred" (health) instead: "Han har dårligt helbred" (He is in poor health).

forms.en: It is good for your health.

sentence.da: Frugt og søvn er gode for din **sundhed**.
sentence.en: Fruit and sleep are good for your health.

sundhedsvæsenet.explanation: "Sundhedsvæsenet" means "a healthcare system". To say where someone works, use "i" (in): "Hun arbejder i sundhedsvæsenet" (She works in the healthcare system).

sentence.da: I Danmark er **sundhedsvæsenet** betalt over skatten.
sentence.en: In Denmark the healthcare system is paid for through taxes.

super.explanation: "Super" means "great". To cheer at good news, say it alone: "Super!" (Great!). To make another word stronger, put "super" before it: "super god" (really good).

sentence.da: Vi vandt kampen. Det var **super**!
sentence.en: We won the game. It was great!

sur.explanation: "Sur" means "sour". To describe a person in a bad mood, it also means "grumpy": "Han er sur i dag" (He is grumpy today).

sentence.da: Min bror er altid **sur** om morgenen.
sentence.en: My brother is always grumpy in the morning.

sur på.explanation: "Sur på" means "mad at". To name who you are mad at, put that person after "på" (at): "Jeg er sur på mig selv" (I am mad at myself). The word "sur" without "på" describes taste: "Citronen er sur" (The lemon is sour).

forms.da: Jeg er sur på min bror.
forms.en: I am mad at my brother.

sentence.da: Min mor er **sur på** mig i dag.
sentence.en: My mom is mad at me today.

suspenderet.explanation: "Suspenderet" means "suspended". It comes from "at suspendere" (to suspend). To say what someone is suspended from, use "fra" (from): "Eleven er suspenderet fra skolen" (The student is suspended from school).

sentence.da: Spilleren blev **suspenderet** i to kampe.
sentence.en: The player was suspended for two games.

svag.explanation: "Svag" means "weak". To describe a sound or light that is hard to notice, it also means "faint": "en svag lyd" (a faint sound).

sentence.da: Han er stadig **svag** efter sygdommen.
sentence.en: He is still weak after the illness.

sved.explanation: "Sved" means "sweat". To describe sweat that comes from fear, use "koldsved" (cold sweat): "Han vågnede i koldsved" (He woke up in a cold sweat).

sentence.da: Efter løbeturen havde han **sved** på panden.
sentence.en: After the run he had sweat on his forehead.

svensk.explanation: "Svensk" means "Swedish". It comes from "Sverige" (Sweden). To name the language, use it without an article: "Jeg taler svensk" (I speak Swedish).

sentence.da: Han kommer fra Sverige og er **svensk**.
sentence.en: He comes from Sweden and is Swedish.

sverige.explanation: "Sverige" means "Sweden". Sweden lies just across "Øresund" (the Øresund strait) from Copenhagen. Do not mix it up with "Schweiz" (Switzerland): "Jeg har været i Schweiz" (I have been in Switzerland).

sentence.da: **Sverige** er et land ved siden af Danmark.
sentence.en: Sweden is a country next to Denmark.

svigerforældre.explanation: "Svigerforældre" means "parents-in-law". To talk about one mother-in-law, use "en svigermor" (a mother-in-law): "Min svigermor er sød" (My mother-in-law is nice). To talk about one father-in-law, use "en svigerfar" (a father-in-law): "Min svigerfar kan lide at male" (My father-in-law likes to paint).

sentence.da: Min mands forældre er mine **svigerforældre**.
sentence.en: My husband's parents are my parents-in-law.

svimmel.explanation: "Svimmel" means "dizzy". To say how you feel now, use "er" (am): "Jeg er svimmel" (I am dizzy). To say it is starting, use "bliver" (get): "Jeg bliver svimmel" (I am getting dizzy).

sentence.da: Jeg er **svimmel** og skal sidde ned.
sentence.en: I am dizzy and need to sit down.

svimmelhed.explanation: "Svimmelhed" means "dizziness". It is the noun for "svimmel" (dizzy). To say you feel dizzy right now, use "svimmel" instead: "Jeg er svimmel" (I am dizzy).

sentence.da: **Svimmelhed** kan være et tegn på for lavt blodtryk.
sentence.en: Dizziness can be a sign of low blood pressure.

svindel.explanation: "Svindel" means "a fraud". To say someone was the victim of fraud, use "at blive udsat for" (to be subjected to): "Hun blev udsat for svindel" (She was the victim of fraud).

sentence.da: Politiet advarer mod **svindel** på nettet.
sentence.en: The police warn against fraud online.

svinekød.explanation: "Svinekød" means "pork". It is built from "svin" (pig) and "kød" (meat). A classic Danish dinner made with it is "flæskesteg" (roast pork with crackling).

sentence.da: **Svinekød** er kød fra en gris.
sentence.en: Pork is meat from a pig.

svær.explanation: "Svær" means "difficult". To say a task is hard to do, put "at" (to) and a verb after "Det er svært" (It is hard): "Det er svært at lære dansk" (It is hard to learn Danish).

sentence.da: Opgaven er meget **svær** for mig.
sentence.en: The task is very difficult for me.

svømning.explanation: "Svømning" means "swimming". To say you are able to swim, use the verb "at svømme" (to swim): "Jeg kan svømme" (I can swim).

sentence.da: Børnene har **svømning** i svømmehallen i dag.
sentence.en: The children have swim class at the pool today.

syd.explanation: "Syd" means "south". It is part of "sydpå" (southward) and "Sydamerika" (South America).

sentence.da: Fuglene flyver mod **syd** om vinteren.
sentence.en: The birds fly south in the winter.

sydamerika.explanation: "Sydamerika" means "South America". It is built from "syd" (south) and "Amerika" (America). To say you travel there, use "til" (to): "Vi rejser til Sydamerika" (We are traveling to South America).

sentence.da: Brasilien og Argentina ligger i **Sydamerika**.
sentence.en: Brazil and Argentina are in South America.

sydlig.explanation: "Sydlig" means "southerly". When you talk about a part of a country, it means "southern": "Sønderborg ligger i det sydlige Danmark" (Sønderborg is in southern Denmark).

sentence.da: Der kommer en **sydlig** vind i aften.
sentence.en: A southerly wind is coming tonight.

sydpå.explanation: "Sydpå" means "south". To say where a vehicle is heading, put it after the verb: "Toget kører sydpå" (The train goes south). To say a place is south of another place, use "syd for" (south of): "Odense ligger syd for Aarhus" (Odense is south of Aarhus).

sentence.da: Vi kører **sydpå** i morgen.
sentence.en: We are driving south tomorrow.

syg.explanation: "Syg" means "sick". To tell your work you are sick, use "at melde sig syg" (to call in sick): "Jeg melder mig syg i dag" (I am calling in sick today).

sentence.da: Min søn er **syg** og bliver hjemme.
sentence.en: My son is sick and stays home.

syltetøj.explanation: "Syltetøj" means "jam". To say the kind, put the name of a fruit in front: "hindbærsyltetøj" (raspberry jam) and "blommesyltetøj" (plum jam).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have **syltetøj** på mit brød.
sentence.en: I want jam on my bread.

sympati.explanation: "Sympati" means "sympathy". To say you support an idea, it also means "support": "Jeg har sympati for forslaget" (I am sympathetic to the proposal).

sentence.da: Vi sendte blomster som tegn på **sympati**.
sentence.en: We sent flowers as a sign of sympathy.

sympatisk.explanation: "Sympatisk" means "likeable". Do not use it for English "sympathetic". To say a person feels sorry for others, use "medfølende" (compassionate): "Hun er meget medfølende" (She is very compassionate).

sentence.da: Din nye chef virker meget **sympatisk**.
sentence.en: Your new boss seems very likeable.

syning.explanation: "Syning" means "sewing". To say what you are doing right now, use the verb "at sy" (to sew): "Jeg syr en kjole" (I am sewing a dress).

sentence.da: Min mor elsker **syning**, og hun syr mange kjoler.
sentence.en: My mother loves sewing, and she sews many dresses.

synlig.explanation: "Synlig" means "visible". To describe something you can see with your eyes, say: "et synligt mærke" (a visible mark). To describe a change people can notice, say: "en synlig forbedring" (a visible improvement).

sentence.da: Månen er **synlig** på himlen i aften.
sentence.en: The moon is visible in the sky tonight.

sytten.explanation: "Sytten" means "seventeen". Do not mix it up with "syv" (seven): "syv børn" (seven children) and "sytten børn" (seventeen children).

sentence.da: Efter seksten kommer **sytten**.
sentence.en: After sixteen comes seventeen.

syv.explanation: "Syv" means "seven". Do not mix it up with "sytten" (seventeen): "syv dage" (seven days) and "sytten dage" (seventeen days).

sentence.da: Der er **syv** dage i en uge.
sentence.en: There are seven days in a week.

syvende.explanation: "Syvende" means "seventh". When you count eggs, use "syv" (seven): "syv æg" (seven eggs). When you give the place in order, use "syvende": "det syvende æg" (the seventh egg). To say a date, use it before the month: "den syvende juli" (the seventh of July).

sentence.da: Søndag er den **syvende** dag i ugen.
sentence.en: Sunday is the seventh day of the week.

så.explanation: "Så" means "so". To give a result, say: "Det regner, så vi bliver hjemme" (It is raining, so we stay home). To say what comes next, it also means "then": "Først spiser vi, og så går vi" (First we eat, and then we go). Do not mix it up with "så" as the past of "at se" (to see): "Jeg så ham" (I saw him).

sentence.da: Jeg er **så** glad i dag!
sentence.en: I am so happy today!

så at sige.explanation: "Så at sige" means "so to speak". To say something is not exactly true but very close, put it in the middle of the sentence: "Han bor så at sige på kontoret" (He practically lives at the office).

forms.da: Han er så at sige min bror
forms.en: He is, so to speak, my brother

forms.da: Det er så at sige færdigt
forms.en: It is, so to speak, finished

forms.da: Vi bor så at sige i skoven
forms.en: We live, so to speak, in the forest

sentence.da: Vi har **så at sige** ingen penge tilbage.
sentence.en: We have, so to speak, no money left.

så længe.explanation: "Så længe" means "as long as". Do not mix it up with "indtil" (until): "Jeg bliver, indtil du kommer" (I stay until you come). When you tell someone to wait a while, "så længe" at the end means "for now": "Vent her så længe" (Wait here for now).

forms.en: as long as there is time

sentence.da: Jeg er glad, **så længe** solen skinner.
sentence.en: I am happy as long as the sun shines.

så snart.explanation: "Så snart" means "as soon as". It is built from "så" (as) and "snart" (soon). When you only mean "when", use "når" (when) instead: "Når jeg er færdig, ringer jeg" (When I am finished, I will call).

forms.en: as soon as it is ready

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til dig, **så snart** jeg er hjemme.
sentence.en: I will call you as soon as I am home.

så vidt.explanation: "Så vidt" means "as far as". To say what you know when you are not completely sure, put it before "jeg ved" (I know): "Så vidt jeg ved, kommer han i morgen" (As far as I know, he is coming tomorrow). To say you only just managed something, it also means "only just": "Jeg nåede så vidt toget" (I only just caught the train).

forms.en: as far as I can see

sentence.da: **Så vidt** jeg ved, åbner butikken klokken ni.
sentence.en: As far as I know, the store opens at nine o'clock.

sådan.explanation: "Sådan" means "like that". To show how to do something, say: "Gør det sådan" (Do it like this). To say "a car like that", put "en" after it: "sådan en bil". To cheer someone on, say "Sådan!" (There you go!).

sentence.da: Se, jeg gør det **sådan**.
sentence.en: Look, I do it like this.

sådan er det bare.explanation: "Sådan er det bare" means "that's just how it is". Literally, it is "so is it just". To accept something you cannot change, say: "Der er kø her, men sådan er det bare" (There is a line here, but that's just how it is).

related.en: that's just the way it is

sentence.da: Det regner meget her, men **sådan er det bare**.
sentence.en: It rains a lot here, but that's just how it is.

sådanne.explanation: "Sådanne" means "such". It is used before more than one thing. To say "such a rule" for one thing, use "sådan en regel" (such a rule).

sentence.da: Vi køber aldrig **sådanne** dyre ting.
sentence.en: We never buy such expensive things.

sågar.explanation: "Sågar" means "even". To add a surprising extra, say: "Sågar min lille bror kan gøre det" (Even my little brother can do it). Do not use it for "even if". For that, use "selv om" (even if): "Jeg går ud, selv om det regner" (I go out even if it rains).

sentence.da: Det regnede hele dagen og sneede **sågar** om aftenen.
sentence.en: It rained all day and even snowed in the evening.

såkaldt.explanation: "Såkaldt" means "so-called". It is built from "så" (so) and "kaldt" (called). To use it before a noun, put it between the article and the noun: "den såkaldte chef" (the so-called boss).

sentence.da: Han er en **såkaldt** ekspert uden uddannelse.
sentence.en: He is a so-called expert without any training.

således.explanation: "Således" means "like this". It sounds formal. For everyday talk, use "sådan" (like this) instead: "Gør det sådan" (Do it like this).

sentence.da: Du skal skrive det **således**.
sentence.en: You must write it like this.

sårbar.explanation: "Sårbar" means "vulnerable". It is built from "et sår" (a wound) and "-bar", which works like "-able" in English, as in "brugbar" (usable).

sentence.da: En nyfødt fugl er meget **sårbar**.
sentence.en: A newborn bird is very vulnerable.

såret.explanation: "Såret" means "wounded". To describe a hurt body, say: "en såret soldat" (a wounded soldier). To describe hurt feelings, say: "såret stolthed" (hurt pride).

sentence.da: Hunden er **såret** i benet og kan ikke gå.
sentence.en: The dog is wounded in the leg and cannot walk.

såsom.explanation: "Såsom" means "such as". It introduces examples after a general word. In everyday talk, "som" (like) works too: "frugt som æbler" (fruit such as apples).

forms.en: countries such as Norway and Sweden

sentence.da: Han spiser meget grønt, **såsom** broccoli og spinat.
sentence.en: He eats a lot of greens, such as broccoli and spinach.

sæbe.explanation: "Sæbe" means "a soap". To say you want some, say: "noget sæbe" (some soap). For washing dishes, use "opvaskemiddel" (dishwashing liquid) instead: "Jeg bruger opvaskemiddel til tallerkenerne" (I use dishwashing liquid for the plates).

sentence.da: Jeg vasker mine hænder med **sæbe** og vand.
sentence.en: I wash my hands with soap and water.

sædvanlig.explanation: "Sædvanlig" means "usual". To say something happened as it always does, use "som sædvanligt" (as usual): "Maden var god som sædvanligt" (The food was good as usual).

sentence.da: Det er en helt **sædvanlig** tirsdag.
sentence.en: It is a completely usual Tuesday.

særegen.explanation: "Særegen" means "distinctive". It is built from "sær" (odd) and "egen" (own).

sentence.da: Byen har en **særegen** lugt af tang og røg.
sentence.en: The city has a distinctive smell of seaweed and smoke.

særlig.explanation: "Særlig" means "special". To say "not very", use "ikke særlig" (not very): "Det er ikke særlig dyrt" (It is not very expensive).

sentence.da: I dag er en **særlig** dag for os.
sentence.en: Today is a special day for us.

sød.explanation: "Sød" means "sweet", for taste and for kind or cute people. To say someone did something kind, say: "Det er sødt af dig" (That is sweet of you).

sentence.da: Kagen er for **sød** for mig.
sentence.en: The cake is too sweet for me.

sødmælk.explanation: "Sødmælk" means "whole milk". It is built from "sød" (sweet) and "mælk" (milk), but the milk is not sweet.

sentence.da: Jeg vælger **sødmælk**, fordi den har mere fedt.
sentence.en: I choose whole milk because it has more fat.

sølle.explanation: "Sølle" means "measly". To complain about too little money, put it before the noun: "Jeg fik en sølle krone for det" (I got a measly krone for it).

sentence.da: Jeg fik kun en **sølle** halv time til at spise.
sentence.en: I only got a measly half hour to eat.

sølv.explanation: "Sølv" means "silver". To say second place in a competition, use it for the medal: "Hun vandt sølv" (She won silver). To name the color, use "sølvfarvet" (silver-colored): "en sølvfarvet bil" (a silver-colored car).

sentence.da: Min ring er lavet af **sølv**.
sentence.en: My ring is made of silver.

sølvpapir.explanation: "Sølvpapir" means "aluminum foil". It is built from "sølv" (silver) and "papir" (paper). Despite the name, it is made of aluminum, not silver.

sentence.da: Jeg pakker kartoflerne ind i **sølvpapir**.
sentence.en: I wrap the potatoes in aluminum foil.

søndag.explanation: "Søndag" means "a Sunday". Danish does not capitalize day names, so write "søndag" in the middle of a sentence. To say this coming Sunday, use "på søndag" (on Sunday). To say every Sunday, use "om søndagen" (on Sundays).

sentence.da: Efter lørdag kommer **søndag**.
sentence.en: After Saturday comes Sunday.

sørgelig.explanation: "Sørgelig" means "sad", for a situation or news, not a feeling inside you. To say that you feel sad, use "ked af det" (sad): "Jeg er ked af det" (I am sad). To call a poor result "pathetic", it also fits: "et sørgeligt resultat" (a pathetic result).

sentence.da: Det var en **sørgelig** nyhed for hele familien.
sentence.en: That was a sad piece of news for the whole family.

sørgmodig.explanation: "Sørgmodig" means "sorrowful". To say you feel sad yourself, use "trist" (sad) instead: "Jeg er trist i dag" (I am sad today).

sentence.da: Hendes stemme var **sørgmodig**, og alle i rummet blev stille.
sentence.en: Her voice was sorrowful, and everyone in the room went quiet.

søskende.explanation: "Søskende" means "siblings". To talk about one person, use "en bror" (a brother) or "en søster" (a sister): "Jeg har en søster" (I have a sister).

sentence.da: Jeg har to **søskende**, en bror og en søster.
sentence.en: I have two siblings, a brother and a sister.

søvn.explanation: "Søvn" means "sleep". To say how much you slept, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg fik lidt søvn i nat" (I got little sleep last night). To say you do not get enough, use "at mangle" (to lack): "Jeg mangler søvn" (I lack sleep).

sentence.da: Jeg er meget træt og har brug for **søvn**.
sentence.en: I am very tired and need sleep.

søvnløshed.explanation: "Søvnløshed" means "insomnia". It is built from "søvn" (sleep) and "-løs" (without), the same "-løs" as in "hjemløs" (homeless).

sentence.da: Efter flere nætter med **søvnløshed** var hun meget træt.
sentence.en: After several nights with insomnia she was very tired.
